description: The Social Security Administration introduced advanced anti-fraud technologies to its telephone claim processing workflow. Starting April 14, 2025, all claim types can be completed over the phone, with suspicious patterns automatically flagged. Those flagged must undergo in-person identity verification—enhancing both accessibility and security for claimants.

Sacramento’s City Council has approved a five-year extension (≈ US$2.6 million) of the ShotSpotter gunshot detection system. This network of audio sensors detects and locates likely gunfire incidents, enabling faster police response, ballistic evidence collection, and victim aid. The renewal includes an obligation for law enforcement to provide yearly performance data (false positives, arrest rates, etc.) to assess effectiveness. Supporters argue it's part of what has helped reduce firearm assaults in the city; critics question its cost and overall impact.

The Government of India is considering establishing special courts dedicated to adjudicating bank fraud cases to accelerate legal resolution. Discussions are underway between the Law and Finance Ministries. Key features under review include a threshold for fraud amounts to qualify for these courts, and faster disposal to improve financial recoveries and minimize asset deterioration caused by delays. Banks support this proposal, noting that judicial delays reduce recovery rates and raise legal costs.

The U.S. Department of Justice (DOJ) has a “Corporate Whistleblower Awards Pilot Program” (CWA), introduced in August 2024, to encourage people to report corporate wrongdoing, especially in priority areas like healthcare

The Dallas County Sheriff’s Office in Texas plans to upgrade its jail management software, specifically the “Adult Information Systems” (AIS), to reduce delays in releasing inmates. They aim to make AIS work better with the courts’ case management system called Odyssey

HMRC is enhancing its surveillance of taxpayers via the AI-powered Connect tool, which analyzes data from over 30 sources—including financial, property, and vehicle records—to flag discrepancies. It now also directly accesses banking data, monitors digital platforms and social media for undeclared income, and employs informants and site-based inspections to clamp down on tax evasion.

The IRS’s “Dirty Dozen” is an annual list of the most common and dangerous tax scams for 2025. It warns taxpayers, businesses, and tax professionals about schemes including phishing and smishing, misleading advice on social media, fake charities, overstated withholding, false claims on sick/family leave credits, and fraud by unscrupulous tax preparers. The campaign is meant to raise awareness and help people avoid falling victim to these scams.

With growing passenger traffic, China Customs at Shanghai Pudong International Airport streamlined tax refund processing through self-service terminals and simplified packaging checks.

Customs report that currently, for 300-passenger flights, the clearance time for customs procedures has been reduced to under 30 minutes - a 50-percent efficiency improvement, with tax refund verification now taking only seconds per transaction

South Korea’s National Tax Service (NTS) is introducing an AI-driven system to counter tax evasion. The initiative was presented at the 59th General Assembly of the Inter-American Center of Tax Administrations in Santiago, Chile. The system aims to enhance tax compliance by detecting evasion, using advanced analytics and AI tools, including for cross-border or international contexts.

The article claims that HMRC is using AI tools to monitor workers’ social media posts for signs of tax evasion. It states that this monitoring is reserved for criminal investigations, combined with HMRC’s “Connect” system (which already analyses financial records, spending habits, etc.). It also says HMRC may send “automated nudges” to suspected evaders, and that the move is part of a broader initiative to close tax gaps without raising taxes on working people. There are concerns from some MPs about privacy, potential mistakes, and overreach.

President Donald Trump signed the GENIUS Act on July 18, 2025, creating the first comprehensive U.S. federal law to regulate stablecoins (cryptocurrencies pegged to the U.S. dollar). The law requires stablecoin issuers to hold reserves in liquid assets (such as U.S. dollars and U.S. Treasury bills) and to publish monthly disclosures about reserve compositions. It is intended to provide legitimacy and regulatory clarity to the stablecoin market as usage expands.

On August 25, 2025, Cambodia’s National Assembly passed amendments to its Citizenship / Nationality Law that give the government sweeping powers to revoke citizenship from nationals, naturalized, or dual citizens who are convicted—by courts under the ruling party—of treason or “collusion with foreign powers.” Earlier in July, a constitutional amendment removed prohibition on depriving someone of nationality. Human rights groups say the law is vaguely worded, can be used to suppress opposition, dissent, free expression, activism, and could lead to statelessness. The law alters Article 33 of Cambodia’s Constitution and has drawn criticism for violating international human rights norms.

The U.S. Government Accountability Office report examines how financial institutions and U.S. financial regulators use and oversee artificial intelligence. It looks at AI applications such as automated credit scoring, trading, customer service, and detecting illegal financial activity. It finds that AI offers efficiency and improved customer experiences, but also raises risks (bias, data quality, cybersecurity, privacy). Among recommendations: expand oversight tools, improve guidance on model risk (especially for credit unions), and give regulators authority to examine service providers used by financial institutions.

Germany’s financial regulator (BaFin) has deployed artificial intelligence into its market surveillance tools (alert systems and market-analysis platforms) to better detect suspicious trading patterns and market abuse. This effort is part of broader reforms following the Wirecard scandal. According to BaFin, the AI tools have already improved the accuracy of alerts, increasing the chances that market abuse will be caught.

Malaysia’s parliament has passed a Government Procurement Bill designed to reform and regulate how public procurement works across government agencies and local authorities. The law aims to standardize procurement procedures, reduce corruption and misuse (such as rent-seeking, wrongful sub-contracting and ministerial interference), enhance fiscal oversight, and introduce penalties for abuses.

A new cooperative purchasing portal has been launched (by the Alliance for Innovation, Batteries Plus, Edge Public, supported by Civic Marketplace) for state, local, educational and non-profit public-sector agencies. It connects them to vetted vendors and expert advice, especially for specialized tech and infrastructure purchases like energy storage, lighting, and fleet management. The goal is to streamline procurement, improve transparency, reduce cost (by up to ~30%), and support local vendor networks.

Albania has appointed an AI bot named Diella as a virtual minister responsible for public procurement. Declared by Prime Minister Edi Rama, Diella will be tasked with managing and awarding all government tenders with the goal of eliminating human bias, corruption, and influence. Diella originally served as a virtual assistant on Albania’s e-Albania portal; now its role is elevated to a “ministerial” level to ensure transparency and integrity in procurement. Critics are concerned about oversight, potential manipulation, and how much human control there will remain.

The new dashboard from Connected Nation will simplify access to states’ plans for funds allocated through the Benefit of the Bargain Round.

The tool aggregates states’ final proposals for the BEAD program, highlighting how the dollars will be spent. This includes the total number of locations slated to be served by various Internet service providers and the types of broadband technology being funded. Users can also view information specific to an individual state, broadband platform, or service provider.

A new UNODC study reveals how forest crime is increasingly connected to other organized criminal activities like drug trafficking, corruption, and human trafficking. These interlinked crimes exacerbate environmental degradation, harm local communities, and impact global economic stability.

Trusted Resources 2.0 is a U.S. government reform program aimed at modernizing the background check process for federal employees and contractors to assess eligibility for security-sensitive or sensitive jobs. Key components include shifting from periodic re-investigations to continuous monitoring, reducing the number of levels of investigation from five to three, updating survey policies (including mental health and international travel), and creating a new technology system called NBIS to replace outdated systems. The goals are to reduce vetting times, improve hiring speed, reduce risk, standardize interagency processes, and facilitate employee mobility. Some progress has been made (reducing backlogs, implementing continuous monitoring in critical positions), but significant challenges remain—particularly in NBIS development, delays, project costs, IT system compatibility, and resource constraints

On 8 September 2025, the Kolkata Meteorological Center (under IMD) launched an AI-powered Storm Prediction Lab aimed at improving cyclone and storm forecast accuracy. The lab applies AI and machine learning to large datasets from satellites, Doppler radar, and historical cyclone tracks. Officials project a 20–25% improvement in prediction accuracy and more timely early warnings for the Bay of Bengal region, which is highly cyclone-prone.

The UK Government launched the Concentrations of Crime Data Challenge, investing £4M to develop AI-driven crime maps that can predict and prevent crimes like knife crime, theft, and anti-social behavior. The system will integrate data from police, councils, and social services, with prototypes due in 2026 and full rollout by 2030 under the £500M R&D Missions Accelerator Programme.

The UK government (via its Ministry of Justice) is implementing new AI tools to predict violent behavior in prisons before it happens. The initiative includes:

A violence predictor using inmate age, history of violence in custody, etc., to assess which inmates may pose elevated risk so intervention or tighter supervision can happen in advance.

Tools to scan mobile phones seized from prisoners (past trials covered ~8.6 million messages from ~33,000 phones) to detect gang communication, planning of escapes or smuggling of contraband.

A plan for a unified digital offender ID to link records across courts, prisons, and probation, overcoming inconsistencies in old systems (typos, missing data).

It aims to reduce prison violence, improve safety for inmates and staff, streamline surveillance / supervision, and improve operational efficiency through prediction and earlier interventions.

Under Operation Shakti, Nagpur Police have launched Maharashtra’s first AI-powered crackdown on human trafficking and prostitution networks. Tools like “Garuda Drishti” scan social media for fake job ads, escort service ads, fraud, etc., while facial recognition-enabled cameras placed at known trafficking hotspots send real-time alerts to local stations. The initiative uses historical data to map vulnerable zones and is supported by NGOs. Early results include multiple raids within a month.

Montgomery County, Maryland piloted a security robot named Parker (human-sized, ~420 pounds) intended to patrol parking garages (specifically a downtown Silver Spring garage) to deter crime, vandalism, theft, and improve safety. The pilot cost ~$90,000, with the robot capable of motion detection and reading license plates, but without facial recognition or audio recording. It sparked public concern (privacy, transparency) when it was deployed without prior notice. The county has paused its activation, requiring public outreach sessions and clearer information before moving forward. Data collected (video) is retained only for 30 days, shared with law enforcement and under public information law requests.

Shanghai has developed a highly accurate digital twin of the entire city (approx. 25 million people), built by public mapping / surveying agencies using LiDAR (airborne and street), drone data, backpack sensors, 3D AI-modelling. The twin enables police and emergency responders to conduct virtual patrols, view building interiors, tenant registries, utility lines, overlay live surveillance and traffic feeds, and prepare mission plans with very detailed geographic accuracy (within ~3 cm). It supports real-time situational awareness for crime prevention and emergency response.

The U.S. IRS is deploying AI and machine learning across its audit programs, replacing legacy systems with models that analyze entire populations of returns. For individuals, ML models flag the top three likely issues per return; for mid-sized corporations, the new Line Anomaly Recommender (LAR) detects relationships among line items; for large partnerships, the LPC model finally enables systematic auditing. The aim is to reduce wasted audits, improve fairness, and close the $688B “Tax Gap.” High-income individuals, corporations, and partnerships face greater scrutiny, while small business, gig economy, and crypto taxpayers may also be flagged.

By Sept. 30, 2025, the federal government will cease issuing paper checks for disbursements, shifting entirely to electronic and real-time payment methods. This $175 billion overhaul touches everything from Social Security to tax refunds — marking the most ambitious government modernization of payments infrastructure in a generation.

Chile’s financial sector is rapidly adopting AI across banking, lending, payments, and fraud detection, supported by Corfo’s AI co-funding programs and university supercomputing labs. AI-powered chatbots cut call-center volumes by 40%, while automation trims operational costs by ~22–25%. With 348 fintech startups active, Chile combines infrastructure, regulation, and talent to drive efficiency and financial inclusion.

The Market Research Future report analyzes the France applied AI in finance market, covering adoption of AI in fraud detection, credit scoring, risk management, robo-advisory, and customer engagement. It highlights growth drivers such as regulatory support, investment in fintech, and increasing demand for automation.
The EU is close to passing a regulation that would compel messaging apps (including encrypted ones) to scan private chats for child sexual abuse material (CSAM).

On 6 April 2025, the UK brought into force the consumer protection provisions of the Digital Markets, Competition and Consumers Act 2024 (DMCCA). Under this new regime, the Competition & Markets Authority (CMA) has expanded powers to enforce consumer protection directly (without going to court), including issuing administrative penalties (up to 10% of a business’s global turnover), issuing online interface notices (requiring removal or modification of content, warnings, domain deletion, etc.), and tackling practices such as “drip pricing” (hidden mandatory fees revealed late in purchasing), fake reviews, unfair terms in contracts, and aggressive marketing practices. The law aims to modernize the UK’s consumer protection framework to keep up with digital commerce and services. Businesses are expected to adapt compliance practices accordingly.

The U.S. Consumer Financial Protection Bureau (CFPB) has launched a process to redo federal open banking rules, which dictate how consumers share financial data with third parties. The move comes after legal disputes between banks and fintechs over fees, privacy, and access rights. The CFPB is gathering public input to redesign the framework to ensure consumer control, boost fintech innovation, and strengthen data protection. If adopted, the new rules could reshape the $23T U.S. financial services market.

The California Prison Industry Authority (CALPIA) has completed “Part One” of its enterprise resource planning (ERP) refresh, installing Sage X software to replace a decades-old “green screen” system. The upgrade enables incarcerated workers to use interfaces and tools more like those in the outside job market, for tasks such as production of clothing, license plates, furniture, as well as services like dental or optical work. The first facility to go live was Folsom State Prison (December 2023), and all state facilities followed by April 2025. The project emphasizes stakeholder input (including incarcerated workers), and upcoming Phase Two will use agile/scrum methods to iteratively add features. The aim is to improve operational efficiency and build technology skills in incarcerated people to aid in re-entry.
The Orange County Superior Court in California provides a useful example of how courts can carefully apply AI-assisted translation.

Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath inaugurated the AI-SPS (Artificial Intelligence – Smart Policing System) in Ghazipur. Developed by Ghazipur Police with iZil Technologies, the system integrates crime mapping, predictive policing, investigation tracking, and digital records to enhance police transparency and efficiency. It showcases how smaller districts can drive technological innovation in law enforcement.
Shanghai on Wednesday launched "Easy Go," an all-in-one platform to streamline digital services for international visitors, leveraging China's expanded visa facilitation and instant tax refunds.

Maryland launched a “one-stop digital benefits portal” allowing residents to apply for food, health, and energy assistance programs through a single mobile-friendly application. Covering Medicaid, SNAP, TANF, and WIC, the system simplifies processes, reduces repetitive paperwork, and aims to serve 1.3 million residents more efficiently.

The U.S. Patent and Trademark Office (USPTO) is scaling up AI adoption through tools like Scout, a large-language-model chatbot that helps examiners detect improper filings, aid cybersecurity compliance, and automate clerical work, and the PE2E Search Tool, an AI-powered patent data search system. Between March 2024 and Feb 2025, the PE2E tool was used ~850,000 times, with FY25 use projected to hit 1 million. These innovations aim to reduce backlogs, improve patent/trademark processing accuracy, and free examiners for higher-value tasks.

U.S. states are leveraging new disability population data to improve accessibility as the ADA turns 35. With a federal mandate requiring all digital government services to be accessible by April 2026, states like Washington D.C. and Arkansas are scanning websites, upgrading portals, and piloting AI tools for language access and usability. Programs also include digital navigators and public listening sessions to ensure services meet community needs.

The UK Government is launching trials of agentic AI helpers that could complete admin tasks and support citizens in key life events, such as finding jobs, applying for apprenticeships, or updating records when moving home. This marks the first “National AI Tender” under the AI Opportunities Action Plan, with pilots expected to run through 2027.

Kansas City, Missouri, is launching a new food waste recycling program that will place 50 food-scrap collection bins at public buildings and fire stations across the city to curb its dependence on landfills.

Singapore issued its first enforcement order under the Online Criminal Harms Act, requiring Meta to implement stronger anti-scam measures on Facebook and Marketplace. With impersonation scams nearly tripling in H1 2025 and losses rising to S$126.5 million, the government warned Meta it could face fines up to S$1 million if it fails to act.

Rhode Island Airport Corporation (RIAC) petitioned to join TSA’s Screening Partnership Program to replace federal TSA officers with private contractors at T.F. Green International Airport, citing long wait times. The move sparked union and congressional opposition, with critics warning about job losses and reduced safety, even though TSA data showed average waits were within targets.

TSA launched the “Families on the Fly” campaign at Salt Lake City International Airport, offering dedicated security lanes for families with children under 12. The initiative, already expanded to 10+ major U.S. airports, aims to ease travel challenges for parents. TSA also announced upcoming discounted PreCheck fees for families and expanded benefits for military travelers.

TSA opened a new checkpoint at Southwest Wyoming Regional Airport’s terminal equipped with Advanced Imaging Technology (AIT) and Computed Tomography (CT) scanners. AIT provides automated, privacy-friendly threat detection using generic outlines, while CT scanners deliver 3D imaging of carry-on bags so passengers don’t need to remove electronics or small liquids, improving security and efficiency.

Researchers at George Mason University, in partnership with DHS’s CINA Center of Excellence, are using AI, NLP, and graph mining to map and analyze human smuggling networks between Mexico and the U.S. Drawing on decades of public legal and media data, the project visualizes smuggling routes and organizational structures as knowledge graphs to reveal patterns, adaptations, and vulnerabilities. The approach may extend to drug, arms, and money-laundering networks.

DHS developed StreamView, an AI-powered digital forensic tool that scans livestreams in real time to help investigators detect and disrupt human trafficking and exploitation. Since deployment, it has enabled the rescue of 133 victims, the arrest of 124 traffickers, and dismantled 29 networks across the U.S. ICE HSI is expanding its nationwide use.

France’s privacy regulator CNIL launched an innovative education campaign by publishing a manga series titled The Shadow Network to teach teenagers about identity theft, hacking, and cybersecurity. Distributed free online and across schools and libraries, the project forms part of CNIL’s 2025–2028 strategic plan to protect minors’ data and digital rights.

The U.S. Department of the Treasury in partnership with the U.S. General Services Administration (GSA), today announced the launch of the Savings Award for Verified Efficiencies (SAVE) Program. This joint initiative empowers federal employees to identify and eliminate wasteful spending in federal contracts, delivering measurable savings for taxpayers while maintaining mission readiness

Portugal replaced its long-running Non-Habitual Residents (NHR) regime with NHR 2.0, a new tax incentive targeting expatriates working in scientific research, innovation, startups, and highly qualified professions. Eligible individuals benefit from a flat 20% income tax rate on qualifying employment and service income, plus exemptions for certain foreign-sourced income. The program is designed to attract global talent and boost Portugal’s innovation ecosystem.

The California Department of Tax and Fee Administration (CDTFA) deployed an AI-powered virtual assistant to respond to taxpayer inquiries. Handling over 42,000 calls per month, the assistant helps manage seasonal surges without diverting staff, improving efficiency and service quality. The project is part of California’s broader state-funded generative AI pilot program.

India’s Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG) is expanding AI- and ML-powered forensic audits to expose fraud in public finances. Already used to uncover fraudulent cases in state beneficiary schemes, the program will scale to nationwide remote audits covering GST, land records, e-procurement, and welfare schemes, aiming to improve transparency, accountability, and save significant public funds.

The article discusses how U.S. federal agencies are exploring AI and real-time data visibility to modernize auditing practices. The approach aims to shift from retrospective audits to continuous oversight, reducing fraud risks and improving transparency in federal spending.

The EU-funded ReconCycle project developed adaptable AI-powered robots capable of reconfiguring themselves to dismantle electronic waste, such as removing lithium batteries from smoke detectors and heat meters. The system addresses the challenge of varied product designs, improving recycling safety and efficiency while reducing reliance on hazardous manual labor.

The Government of Odisha is adopting AI and IoT-driven water management tools to improve forecasting of droughts and floods, optimize distribution networks, and reduce losses in water supply. The initiative marks a major step in applying predictive analytics to climate resilience and sustainable resource management.

San Francisco Police Department is piloting Draft One, an AI tool from Axon that converts body-worn camera audio into first drafts of police reports. With 54 officers participating, the program aims to reduce paperwork and return officers to the field faster. Officers must review and approve all AI-generated text, ensuring accountability. Civil liberties groups have raised concerns about accuracy and transparency.

Ho Chi Minh City launched a contactless bus payment system using NAPAS cards, allowing passengers to pay directly with domestic bank cards, smartphones, or smartwatches. Covering 28 banks, the system shortens queues, reduces cash dependency, and improves commuter convenience.

Since January 2025, Singapore fully implemented QR code clearance at Woodlands and Tuas land checkpoints, enabling travelers to pass immigration without passports. Features include group QR codes (up to 10 persons) and special assistance lanes. The system handled 50.3M travelers in its first year, cutting queues and boosting efficiency by 10%.

The UK government launched an AI-powered crime mapping project to predict and prevent crime by 2030. With £4M initial funding under the £500M R&D Missions Accelerator Programme, the system integrates police, council, and social services data to identify crime hotspots, forecast risks, and enable early interventions. The initiative aims to halve knife crime and violence against women and girls within a decade.

Rourkela Police launched Project SHIELD (Smart Habitual Offender Intelligence and Early Law Enforcement Detection), a tech-driven system to track habitual offenders and enhance early crime detection. The initiative aims to strengthen public safety and modernize policing through data-driven intelligence.

Three police departments in Oakland County, Michigan, proposed creating a $10 million self-governing authority to oversee the Courts and Law Enforcement Information System (CLEMIS). The new structure would shift oversight from county commissioners to participating agencies, allowing ~250 agencies across 10 counties to modernize data-sharing technology and sustain operations through a per-officer funding model.

In Kansas City, Missouri, Patmos Tech deployed “Lance,” a Knightscope K5 AI-powered security robot, to patrol its data center around the old Kansas City Star building. The robot records 360° video, recognizes vehicles, and has provided evidence for burglary investigations. While privately deployed, local police have acknowledged the footage could assist in criminal cases.

New York lawmakers introduced a bill requiring the digitization of all legal mail for state prisoners. The secure system will have law offices register with corrections to upload documents for inmate access via tablets or law library computers. The move targets contraband smuggling linked to paper mail and modernizes prison correspondence practices.
Box 6.3. Application of telematics in improving safety: Talabat in United Arab Emirates

The U.S. Treasury announced major IT modernization progress, including cloud migration, AI-enhanced customer support, and stronger cybersecurity for federal financial systems. These upgrades aim to save costs, improve efficiency, and deliver faster, more secure taxpayer services.

Pakistan’s Federal Board of Revenue launched a Lifestyle Monitoring Cell to scan social media posts on Instagram, TikTok, and YouTube for signs of tax evasion. A team of 40 investigators is compiling evidence on influencers, celebrities, and businesspeople displaying luxury spending that doesn’t match tax filings. The system builds digital profiles, maintains evidence databases, and supports tax and money-laundering probes.

Greece implemented a major tax system modernization led by the Independent Authority for Public Revenue. The reform introduced AI-powered fraud detection, mandatory e-invoicing, and real-time cross-checking of receipts, helping uncover €10B in undeclared income and achieve a record €63B in tax collections in 2024.

The U.S. Office of Personnel Management (OPM) launched the Online Retirement Application (ORA), the first fully digital federal retirement application system. Effective July 2025, all retirement applications must be submitted electronically, ending the long-standing paper process. The reform, part of the Department of Government Efficiency initiative, is expected to reduce delays, improve accuracy, and eliminate backlogs.

The Nashik Rural Police in India deployed AI-powered drones to monitor crowd density and conduct real-time headcounts during the Shravan Somvar pilgrimage at Trimbakeshwar, attended by over 200,000 devotees. The drones also acted as public announcement systems to guide pilgrims. The successful pilot will be scaled for the 2027 Simhastha Kumbh Mela, which attracts millions.

Governments and organizers of major events are deploying AI-powered risk detection platforms integrated with Esri’s GIS and digital twin tools to secure large-scale events. The system processes data from social media, sensors, and deep/dark web sources to identify emerging threats, visualize risks on dynamic maps, and guide security deployments. It has been applied successfully in international sporting tournaments and national elections to enhance real-time situational awareness and post-event analysis.

California’s Council on Science and Technology launched the CCST Legislative Academy on AI, a first-of-its-kind training program for state lawmakers and legislative staff. The academy will provide seminars, policy roundtables, and site visits on AI topics such as algorithmic bias, workforce impacts, and data privacy to guide evidence-based policymaking.

California lawmakers passed Senate Bill 243, creating the first state-level safeguards for AI companion chatbots. The bill requires bots to identify themselves, prevent sexual content exposure to minors, respond to self-harm cues by directing users to crisis hotlines, and mandates annual reporting on mental health impacts.

The Government of India’s IndiaAI Mission, in partnership with OpenAI, launched the AI Academy to expand access to AI education, tools, and global opportunities. The program aims to democratize AI skills, bridge the digital divide, and prepare India’s workforce for future innovation-driven growth.

Hong Kong’s Lands Department signed an MoU with the Hong Kong Polytechnic University to advance AI-driven surveying, mapping, and geospatial services. The collaboration enhances spatial data use in disaster response, environmental monitoring, infrastructure, and land management, supporting the city’s smart urban development.

Mali introduced several new digital public service platforms across transport, health, and administration. These include biometric driver’s licenses, a secure transport platform (Sigui-Dolo), digital toll gates (doubling revenue at one site), an integrated health information system (OpenClinic) linked to national ID, and an administrative system (SIGIP) to monitor public service workflows and staff attendance.

ClearGov introduced AI-powered budgeting tools for U.S. city governments to automate repetitive tasks, ensure compliance, and generate citizen-friendly “budget books” with charts and explanations. The system reduces workloads for finance teams and enhances public transparency.

Dallas launched an AI-powered procurement system to streamline vendor selection, reduce bias, and accelerate public service delivery. The platform analyzes bids more efficiently, helping the city cut bottlenecks in procurement and improve responsiveness to community needs.

U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) is piloting several AI-driven systems to enhance border security. These include AI-powered covert IoT sensors for situational awareness, vessel detection analytics, X-ray cargo commodity classification, and machine learning trade risk models, aimed at improving detection of illicit traffic while reducing manual workload.

The Oklahoma Department of Corrections is piloting AI-enhanced unarmed drones to monitor perimeters of Red Rock Correctional Center. Partnering with Skydio and Levatas, the drones use AI visual inspection to detect contraband such as weapons and phones, improving staff safety and operational efficiency.

Singapore is launching enhanced government support for SMEs to digitize more confidently via new and upgraded tools and programmes. Notably, IMDA has added a Go Digital Advisor AI tool to its CTOaaS platform to help firms identify priorities across sales, operations, HR, cybersecurity, sustainability, etc. The government is also expanding cybersecurity help (via the Cyber Protect Programme), and working with chambers like SCCCI to deliver AI training and access to approved digital / AI solutions. The goal is to make the transformation journey smarter, simpler, safer for SMEs.

Starting December 10, 2025, Australia is enacting legislation under the Online Safety Amendment (Social Media Minimum Age) Act 2024 requiring social media platforms to take reasonable steps to prevent under-16s from creating or maintaining accounts. The law delays the ability to register for social media until age 16 (instead of 13), and holds platforms accountable with civil penalties if they fail to enforce these rules.

The U.S. Treasury is advocating for a transformation of anti–money laundering (AML) compliance by leveraging AI technologies. The push includes encouraging financial institutions and regulators to adopt AI tools to detect illicit activity more efficiently, modernizing oversight, and improving outcomes in AML enforcement.

The European Parliament’s Research Service outlines the EU’s latest initiatives to strengthen security and defence innovation. The report highlights projects under the European Defence Fund and the EU Security Innovation Hub, focusing on AI-driven early threat detection, cyber-resilience, and rapid response capabilities across member states.

The Driver Alcohol Detection System for Safety (DADSS), a joint public-private project, is preparing to license its advanced alcohol detection technologies (both active breath-based and passive ambient systems) to vehicle manufacturers. These systems could prevent vehicles from starting if the driver is over the legal alcohol limit.

Ohio has launched a mobile app called RoadReady Ohio that allows learner drivers (under age 21) and their parents or guardians to log supervised driving time and receive feedback on driving behaviors (hard braking, acceleration, turns, speed). The app supports the new state law requiring 50 supervised driving hours (including night hours) before licensure.

Senegal’s tax authority is using satellite and drone imagery, along with an integrated software system called PAGCF, to modernize property tax collection. The system combines data from land registries, tax authorities, and the Treasury, and uses field surveys via tablets to map and value properties. Since its pilot launch (in Dakar) the reform has tripled compliance in some zones and yielded millions of euros in additional tax revenue.

The Pennsylvania Supreme Court ruled that Pittsburgh’s “jock tax” — a 3% tax on income earned by visiting athletes and performers in publicly funded stadiums — is unconstitutional because it discriminated against nonresidents who were taxed more heavily than city residents.

Hawaii has enacted a new “green fee” law that increases taxes on hotel stays and vacation rentals, and for the first time will impose an 11 % tax on cruise ship fares prorated by the days spent docked in Hawaii ports. The revenue is intended for climate adaptation and resilience measures (shoreline recovery, wildfire prevention, etc.). The measure is now being legally challenged by the cruise industry for alleged constitutional issues.

The Uttar Pradesh government (India) is launching a drive to identify senior citizens who qualify for pensions and other welfare programmes. The aim is to move towards automatic disbursement of old-age pensions without requiring yearly applications or in-person verification. Verification will be done through phone calls or digital tools (Jeevan Praman app) and by integrating data from state and central welfare schemes (Family ID, Zero Poverty).

Starting October 6, 2025, the Maharashtra government will make pension-related documents (e-PPOs, gratuity orders, etc.) digitally available via DigiLocker. Pensioners can access, download, or verify their documents instantly using their pension payment order number and treasury office details. This shift aims to increase transparency, convenience, and efficiency by removing reliance on physical documents and postal delivery.

The article describes how state audit and finance offices are beginning to adopt AI tools (from MindBridge) to enhance auditing capabilities. It proposes a “Central Insights Factory” model where AI continuously scans financial, procurement, and operational systems to detect anomalies, reduce errors, and provide real-time oversight rather than periodic audits.

The U.S. Department of Homeland Security’s S&T directorate, with MIT Lincoln Laboratory, has developed and field-tested DePLife, a radar-based “through-wall” sensing technology that can detect the presence of people through walls, even with minor motion. It’s being commercialized (via MaXentric) and tested by several U.S. law enforcement agencies, with plans to improve motion compensation, deploy via handheld devices or drones, and expand use in tactical operations.

The article explores how ChatGPT is evolving from a mere assistive tool to a “digital witness” in criminal investigations. It highlights a case in Florida where a teenager was arrested after posing violent queries to ChatGPT, flagged by monitoring software. It also describes how authorities used ChatGPT-generated images and dialogues in a high-profile fire case in California: the suspect had asked ChatGPT about liability for fire from a cigarette, and images of a burning forest produced by the model were used in prosecutors’ evidence. The piece warns that users should not treat ChatGPT as a private confidant, since conversations can be logged and used in investigations.

The State Supreme Court in Staten Island (Courtroom 410) has been transformed into a “Digital Jury Trial Courtroom” under New York’s court modernization initiative. The upgrades include integrated support for in-person and virtual hearings, improved evidence presentation systems, interactive features for attorneys and witnesses, wireless microphone systems, touchscreens, annotation tools, and mobility enhancements. It is one of 12 pilot courtrooms slated for upgrade across Staten Island.

The Rutgers Policy Lab published an April 2025 digest summarizing ongoing New Jersey state government policy actions. The update covers multiple legislative and executive developments such as education reform funding, environmental initiatives, and social welfare adjustments. The page serves as a tracking resource rather than a standalone government initiative, aiming to inform researchers and policymakers about state-level decisions.

Nagpur city police deployed an advanced security setup for safety at Deekshabhoomi, integrating AI with ~100 CCTV cameras linked to the SIMBA database to instantly identify potential criminals, monitor crowd density in real time, and detect suspicious activity like controversial banners or unattended items. Drones provide aerial surveillance, and footfall tracking helps with crowd control and deployment of police resources.

The Comptroller & Auditor General of India (CAG) will soon launch an AI-powered Large Language Model (CAG-LLM) as part of a broader push to modernize public audits. The system is designed to help auditors access institutional memory, analyze large datasets, detect anomalies, and generate improved insights. Simultaneously, the CAG-Connect Portal will serve as a unified interface for nearly 1 million auditee entities to respond to audit queries and track findings. The project also supports expanding remote and hybrid audits across India, leveraging risk-based planning and geospatial tools.

U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) has collected and uploaded DNA samples from migrants — including children as young as four — into the FBI’s CODIS criminal database, even in cases where individuals have not been accused of crimes. Since 2020, over 1.5 million profiles (including more than 133,000 minors) have been added, representing a massive expansion of genetic surveillance. Critics argue this practice raises serious legal and privacy concerns.

Several city halls (notably in Scotland) have introduced AI tools to function as “co-workers,” automating repetitive admin tasks, processing correspondence, preserving institutional knowledge, and enabling human staff to spend more time on substantive work (e.g. social services). One council reported avoiding about US$1.6 million in staffing costs by deploying AI to reduce paperwork burdens.

The New Jersey Office of Innovation and Department of Agriculture used AI / statistical pattern recognition across multiple state databases to detect children who were eligible for the NJ Summer EBT program but had not been enrolled initially. In 2024, this effort identified 106,000 additional children (about 15 % of total recipients), resulting in $12.8 million in benefits disbursed. In 2025, by mid-June, they had already identified and automatically enrolled 76,000 children (about 11 % of recipients), distributing $9.1 million.

The FCC has proposed new rules requiring wireless carriers and public safety answering points (PSAPs) to enhance location data for 911 calls. The key change: vertical (floor/level) location will be measured above ground level (AGL) rather than height above ellipsoid (HAE). This is critical for multi-story buildings. The proposal also demands creation of a central online system for carriers and dispatch centres to report location failures. While the technology is not yet widely deployed, industry and standard bodies like National Emergency Number Association (NENA) support the direction.

The California Department of Forestry and Fire Protection (CAL FIRE) has launched a new Aviation Tracking and Information System (CATIS), built in partnership with TracPlus, to manage its aerial firefighting fleet. The system enables real-time monitoring of aircraft across California, logs mission events such as water drops and pickups, and integrates secure data feeds into a central dashboard. The digital system improves coordination, transparency, and situational awareness during wildfire response.

The UK government is launching a consultation to reform the system of safeguarding for people who lack mental capacity (such as those with severe dementia or learning disabilities). The proposed “Liberty Protection Safeguards” will replace the current Deprivation of Liberty Safeguards (DoLS) system, which has become overly bureaucratic and has a significant backlog of cases. The reform intends to reduce intrusive, repetitive assessments, allow existing assessments to be reused, extend assessment validity beyond one year, and enable better focus on those most vulnerable. The consultation will invite input from families, carers, clinicians, social workers and other practitioners, ahead of changes to the Mental Capacity Act Code of Practice.

The Scottish Government is launching a pilot programme that will establish drug-checking facilities in selected locations (e.g., Glasgow, Dundee, Aberdeen). The facilities will enable people who use drugs to submit a small amount of a substance for analysis of content and contamination, with the goal of reducing harm and fatalities from unpredictable substances (such as synthetic opioids like nitazenes). A national research and testing laboratory will support the pilot.

VMRDA launched construction of a 2-acre anti-drug theme park titled “Yuvagalam Anti-Drug Glow Theme Park” at its Central Park in Visakhapatnam. The project is valued at ₹3.5 crore and aims to raise youth awareness about drug abuse, promoting a drug-free city. It is claimed to be “first-of-its-kind globally.”

Hale County, Texas, is integrating AI-powered firearm detection through the Angel Protection system across 18 security cameras in key government buildings to improve emergency response. The AI scans video feeds twice per second for brandished weapons and alerts a human monitor in Midland, who verifies the threat and notifies local authorities with precise GPS data. The system, costing $10,000 annually, aims to reduce response time and prevent shootings by engaging law enforcement before shots are fired.

India is reimagining its GST registration process through an AI-powered multi-agent system (MAS) that automates document verification and risk assessment. Currently, applicants like Rajesh spend days compiling and uploading documents, while officers like Priya manually cross-check data across multiple websites. The MAS framework introduces specialised AI agents to perform these tasks automatically—linking databases, verifying property and utility records, checking document authenticity, and providing a unified risk dashboard for officers. This system enhances efficiency, accuracy, and transparency without replacing human judgment.

The Utah Tax AI Pilot Project (July 2024–February 2025) tested generative AI for reliable and accurate use within the Utah State Tax Commission. Through a competitive “bake-off” between four vendor platforms, response accuracy rose from 73% in Phase I to 97% in Phase II, leading to the rollout of a production system. The project also created the Utah Division of Technology Services (DTS) AI Factory to streamline future AI deployments across state agencies. The pilot evaluated whether retrieval-augmented generation (RAG)-based AI could deliver trustworthy results while avoiding hallucinations—critical for maintaining public trust. It produced clear, comparative data on performance, cost, and implementation, confirming that AI can support call center agents effectively. The initiative demonstrated how careful design and testing can make generative AI dependable for government operations and paved the way for citizen-facing AI pilots in late 2025.

Europe’s €2.3 trillion public procurement system is being digitally transformed through the European Public Procurement Data Space (PPDS), which aims to standardize, open, and modernize how procurement data is shared and used. Initially focused on national and EU-level buyers, the open-source and interoperable platform will soon allow cities and local governments to connect and use shared infrastructure, tools, and insights to enhance their procurement strategies.

Starting today, the UK has banned “sneaky fees” — hidden mandatory charges estimated to cost consumers £2.2 billion annually — under the Digital Markets, Competition and Consumer Act 2024. Businesses such as travel sites, ticket agencies, and food delivery apps must now include all compulsory fees in the headline price, while fake reviews are also prohibited. Research showed hidden fees often add over 25% to product prices, with entertainment, travel, and retail sectors most affected. The law mandates transparency for unavoidable charges like booking or installation fees but excludes optional add-ons. It also holds businesses legally responsible for preventing and removing fake reviews, which account for roughly 10% of all online reviews. The reforms aim to protect consumers, ensure fair competition, and build trust in digital markets.

Senate Bill 12 will extend the ban on diversity, equity and inclusion policies to K-12 schools. In particular, it will prohibit school districts from factoring race, ethnicity, gender identity or sexual orientation into hiring decisions. It will also bar schools from offering instructions, programs and guidance that focus on sexual orientation or gender identity, including sponsoring student clubs such as Gender and Sexuality Alliance. The law’s backers said the legislation gives parents more control over their children’s education, while critics said it targets and censors marginalized groups, such as LGBTQ students. Some civil rights groups including the ACLU of Texas have launched a legal challenge against the law.

Vietnam’s government has directed ministries to complete the legal framework for digital transformation, data governance, personal data protection, and electronic identification by 2025, establishing the core foundation for national digital transformation. The Ministry of Public Security will define the national data architecture and governance framework and coordinate a decree on mandatory data sharing. Eleven key national databases—covering land, finance, health, education, agriculture, and more—are prioritized for completion in 2025. The Ministry of Science and Technology will also finalize the Vietnam Digital Government Architecture Framework to ensure system interoperability. A National Steering Committee on Databases, led by the Prime Minister, will oversee implementation. These efforts build on Vietnam’s 2024 achievements, including the launch of the National Population Database and a 15-place rise in the UN E-Government Index, positioning the country 71st globally.

Hale County, Texas, will integrate AI-powered firearm detection technology, known as the Angel Protection system, across 18 security cameras in government buildings, including the courthouse, justice center, tax office, and probation facilities. The system scans video feeds twice per second to detect brandished firearms and alerts human monitors in Midland, Texas, who verify incidents and notify local authorities with GPS-based alerts similar to Amber Alerts. Costing $10,000 annually, the system aims to shorten law enforcement response times and prevent potential shootings. County officials and law enforcement agencies are coordinating implementation, with a live demonstration planned at the new Juvenile Justice Alternative Education Program building

A study by the University of St. Gallen, commissioned by PensExpert, found that artificial intelligence (AI) could transform Switzerland’s retirement system, which faces pressure from rising life expectancy, low returns, and complex regulations. The research identified seven key areas where AI can drive change: automation and efficiency, financial education, digital pension advice, personalized pension plans, optimized investments, fraud prevention, and healthcare cost reduction. Experts believe AI can significantly cut costs and boost productivity, with nearly 80% of industry respondents expecting major efficiency gains. However, the study stresses that success depends on trust, transparency, and data protection. Researchers call for clear regulations, hybrid consulting models, and digital education to ensure ethical and inclusive use. AI, they conclude, could make retirement provision more efficient and fair, but it must be implemented responsibly to become a sustainable pillar of modern pension systems.

The U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) has launched a new mobile surveillance app called Mobile Fortify, enabling field agents to perform real-time biometric identity checks using facial recognition and contactless fingerprints

At the start of President Donald Trump’s term, federal agencies like ICE and Citizenship and Immigration Services have deployed advanced technologies to conduct mass deportations, spending $7.8 billion since 2020 on tools from 263 companies. These include facial recognition, voice and fingerprint analysis, location tracking, DNA testing, and AI-based predictive modeling to identify immigration violators. The Department of Homeland Security uses AI to cross-reference visa, criminal, and social media data, assigning “hurricane scores” (1–5) to assess flight risks. While some experts note AI can streamline enforcement and focus on high-risk cases, others warn of systematic bias and racial profiling

Colorado launched the Energy Savings Navigator, an online tool that helps residents find and apply for over 600 energy rebates and 18 assistance programs, saving money on rising energy costs. Developed by the Colorado Digital Service in partnership with state agencies and nonprofits, the tool simplifies access to benefits through a 10-minute questionnaire and personalized savings estimates. Built using the open-source MyFriendBen platform, it was delivered a year early and over $1 million under budget. The initiative supports the state’s goal that no resident should spend more than 6% of their income on energy, and other U.S. states are now exploring adopting similar tools.

George Mason University researchers Sungsoo Ray Hong and Yotam Gingold have developed ShadowMagic, a new AI-powered tool that helps professional cartoonists speed up the shadowing process—one of the most repetitive and time-consuming tasks in comic production. Built as an Adobe Photoshop plug-in, ShadowMagic uses human–AI collaboration to automate parts of colorization, allowing artists to focus on creative expression. The project builds on an earlier tool called FlatMagic and stems from interviews with professional cartoonists frustrated by tedious workflows. The system intelligently handles millions of pixels, updating lighting and shading automatically. ShadowMagic has already gained strong interest from digital artists, highlighting a growing movement toward AI tools that enhance rather than replace creativity.

The UK government is piloting a new system requiring certain offenders to perform remote check-ins via their personal mobile devices. The pilot includes features such as video recording of the offender, AI-based identity verification, and behavior-based questioning. If the system detects suspicious responses or attempts to defeat the identity checks, it sends an instant “red alert” to probation officers for intervention. The pilot is being tested across four probation regions in England (South West, North West, East of England, and Kent/Surrey/Sussex) as part of an £8 million tech initiative to enhance crime prevention.

The Crime Reduction Toolkit, developed by UCL’s Jill Dando Institute and partners, compiles evidence from hundreds of crime reduction studies and presents it in an interactive online format. Police and practitioners can filter by crime type, context, cost, and implementation details to see which interventions work best, under what conditions. The College of Policing built the user interface, and the tool has had over 500,000 views globally. UK police have applied its insights for initiatives against drink driving, shoplifting, and anti-social behavior.

As part of Operation Shakti to counter human trafficking and sexual exploitation, Nagpur City Police launched a citizen engagement initiative called Police–Samuday Samvad. It involves holding 50 community meetings across police station areas, training locals to recognize indicators of trafficking, spotting suspicious movements, and volunteering to assist anti-trafficking operations. Over 1,400 residents have participated so far. The approach aims to shift from purely enforcement to building a community network of vigilance against exploitation.

Researchers at George Mason University developed IMBWatch, an AI tool using graph neural networks to analyze patterns in geography, business data, online reviews, known raid data, and advertisements to identify illicit massage businesses (IMBs) that are often fronts for human trafficking. The approach models how these businesses interact with their surroundings and uses spatial/temporal patterns to distinguish them from legitimate ones.

The study “Unmasking Human Trafficking Risk in Commercial Sex Supply Chains with Machine Learning” applies AI to detect and map recruitment tactics used by traffickers. By analyzing millions of online ads (deep web commercial sex websites) and linking them with sales patterns, the researchers identify suspicious recruitment offers (e.g. “modeling job” scams) and infer connections to known trafficking networks. This enables early intervention before exploitation takes place. The work reveals that many recruitment operations occur in suburban or rural areas—contrary to expectations of urban origin—and offers law enforcement new leads for disrupting supply chains.

HMRC has released a new online tool that guides companies through the criteria to determine whether their projects qualify as R&D activities for tax relief. Users answer a series of key questions and receive an indication of eligibility. HMRC emphasizes that a “competent professional” should help with more technical questions, and that saving or printing the result can support a claim during compliance checks.

HMRC has updated the process by which businesses correct errors in VAT returns. As of July 2025, the traditional paper form VAT652 is being phased out for most errors, replaced by an online error correction form accessible via Government Gateway. Agents can also submit corrections digitally on behalf of clients. There are defined thresholds for using the simplified “adjust in the next return” method (errors under £10,000 or between £10,000 and £50,000 but less than 1 % of sales). Larger or more serious errors must still be reported directly.

The Welsh Government has launched a consultation to solicit views on how to improve the legislative process for its devolved taxes (Land Transaction Tax and Landfill Disposals Tax). Options include introducing a finance bill process in Wales or adopting a more frequent / streamlined tax bill mechanism. The aim is to make tax law changes more responsive and transparent, with proper scrutiny in the Senedd.

The Financial Action Task Force (FATF) has launched a National Risk Assessment (NRA) Toolkit to assist countries in identifying their most significant money laundering and predicate crime risks. The toolkit provides cross-country data (e.g. proceeds of crime estimates, common laundering methods), practical templates, and “quick guides” focused on high-difficulty domains like corruption, virtual assets, legal persons, and the informal economy. It is designed to be flexible and adaptable to different national contexts.

Sarasota (Florida) Police are implementing an integrated Real-Time Operations Center (ROC) that ties together live surveillance (intersection cameras, license plate readers, gunshot sensors, private cameras with permission) with field units. The SPD aims to deploy robotic dog “Spot”, drones as first responders, and smart glasses (heads-up display to read records, translate languages, scan IDs) to assist officers in real time. The center will enable technicians and officers to collaborate live, pushing alerts and intelligence to field officers.

At the Global Fintech Fest 2025, the RBI launched four new digital payments initiatives aimed at increasing convenience, security, and inclusivity. Key among them is AI-based UPI HELP, which uses a small language model (SLM) to assist users with payments, mandates, and dispute resolution. Other measures include IoT-based UPI payments, interoperable net banking, UPI Reserve Pay, and enhancements in biometric / face authentication for UPI.

Virginia’s Governor Glenn Youngkin signed Executive Order 51, authorizing a pilot program to use agentic / generative AI tools to review and streamline the state’s regulatory and guidance documents. The AI system will scan existing regulations to flag statutory contradictions, redundancies, and overly complex language, and suggest streamlined edits. The pilot seeks to push state agencies beyond prior goals of regulation reduction and make regulatory reviews more efficient and continuous.

The EU Data Act is a regulation that “enter[s] into application” as of 12 September 2025, formalizing harmonized rules across the EU for how data generated by devices and services may be accessed, shared, ported, and used. It mandates that connected devices enable data sharing, imposes obligations on data holders, clarifies users’ rights to data, and grants public bodies certain powers to request data in emergencies.

The NYPD is deploying 140 hybrid SUVs equipped with perimeter alert systems designed to warn officers of potential ambush or perimeter threats. The vehicles are also more fuel-efficient. The upgrade is intended to enhance officer safety in the field during patrols and confrontations.

Australia is piloting a digital incoming passenger card system, known as the Australia Travel Declaration (ATD), to replace the traditional paper Incoming Passenger Card (IPC). Eligible travellers on selected Qantas international flights into Brisbane (and now expanding to more flights/airports) can complete their border declarations via the Qantas app before travelling. Once they submit, they receive a digital pass (with QR code) to present to border and biosecurity officers upon arrival, speeding up the clearance process.

Many Americans lack access to retirement savings through their employers—estimates say over 56 million private sector workers have no plan. In response, states are creating automatic Individual Retirement Account (auto-IRA) programs: under these, employees are automatically enrolled via payroll unless they opt out, and employers (for example, with 6+ employees in Nevada) are required to participate unless they already offer a retirement plan. These state programs are mostly overseen by state treasurers or appointed boards, and use private contractors to manage the investments. As of mid-2025, 20 states have such programs. The approach aims to raise savings, reduce future public costs, and fill gaps in retirement coverage.

San José has launched an IT Innovation Hub, a portal where technology companies can continuously pitch their products and ideas to city government officials. Instead of relying on periodic solicitations, vendors can submit proposals any time; the city reviews them monthly against its strategic IT, data governance, AI, and cybersecurity criteria. Selected proposals may become pilots, part of procurement, or integrated into future budgets.

San José expanded its AI-based Road Safety Conditions Pilot, using cameras mounted on city vehicles to detect potholes, debris, and other hazards. The AI model achieved 97 % accuracy for potholes and 88 % for debris. In its next phase, the city will install cameras on street sweepers to cover travel lanes, sidewalks, and bike lanes. The system automatically reports issues to public works, reducing manual 311 complaints and enabling proactive maintenance.

ZeroEyes, a Pennsylvania-based public safety technology company known for its AI-powered gun detection systems, has launched a new product — the ZeroEyes Aerial Detection Kits (ZAD). Developed by its subsidiary ZE Government Solutions, ZAD is a drone-based AI threat detection system designed for law enforcement and public safety agencies. The system provides real-time video feeds capable of detecting guns, vehicles, boats, drones, and people, offering enhanced situational awareness in large or open environments that are difficult to secure

Researchers at Johns Hopkins University have developed an artificial intelligence system called SafeTraffic Copilot, designed to predict car crashes and evaluate how road design changes — such as adjusting traffic light timing or modifying signage — affect accident rates. The tool, powered by large language models (LLMs), analyzes diverse datasets including weather conditions, road designs, traffic patterns, driver behaviors, satellite imagery, and accident reports.

The City of Memphis, Tennessee, is leveraging AI to strengthen its cybersecurity, particularly in defending against phishing attacks. The city uses the Themis AI Copilot, an AI-powered email assistant developed by IRONSCALES and integrated with Microsoft Outlook, to help employees identify and report suspicious emails in real time.

Maryland is giving cybersecurity researchers and residents alike a chance to help defend the state’s digital infrastructure, through a new initiative that encourages responsible reporting of online vulnerabilities

The Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification (CMMC), developed by the U.S. Department of Defense (DoD), offers valuable lessons for state and local governments aiming to strengthen cybersecurity. Originally built upon the NIST SP 800-171 standard, the CMMC provides a tiered compliance framework that ensures vendors safeguard controlled and sensitive data

Shanghai has introduced its first humanoid traffic police robot, nicknamed “Xiao Hu” (Little Tiger), as part of a real-world trial in the city’s bustling Huangpu District. The robot, dressed like a traffic officer with LED lighting and reflective gear, directs cars and pedestrians, gives voice commands such as “Red light, please stop,” and performs hand gestures modeled after standard Chinese traffic police movements.

The Inland Revenue Authority of Singapore (IRAS) has launched new digital tax e-services as of October 8, 2025, marking a major step toward simplifying and modernizing tax compliance. The initiative introduces user-friendly, real-time dashboards for both businesses and individuals, enabling faster, more accurate, and transparent tax filing.

These examples illustrate how a government tax authority uses artificial intelligence (AI) to improve accuracy, efficiency, and fraud prevention across its operations:

Tax Time Nudging – AI models analyze taxpayer data in real time to detect inconsistencies in online tax returns (via the myTax platform). When amounts entered differ from expected values based on similar taxpayers or past records, the system prompts users to review and correct entries before submission — helping taxpayers “get it right from the start.”

HMRC has launched an enhanced version of its compliance interactive guidance tool, first introduced in April 2025, as part of the UK government’s Plan for Change to support economic growth. The upgraded tool provides a more personalized and user-friendly experience, helping businesses and individuals better understand HMRC’s compliance checks and manage their tax affairs more confidently.

When the Mississippi Public Employees’ Retirement System (PERS) faced a 300% increase in software costs, it chose to modernize rather than pay unsustainable fees. Partnering with Mythics, PERS migrated its mission-critical infrastructure to an open-source Oracle virtualization platform, cutting software expenses by two-thirds, improving system performance, and gaining the flexibility to move to the cloud in the future. This transformation serves as a model for other public agencies dealing with escalating costs, vendor dependency, and modernization challenges, demonstrating how strategic IT reform can drive both efficiency and sustainability.

The Swedish National Financial Management Authority (ESV) has developed an innovative GDP forecasting application leveraging explainable ML to enhance both accuracy and transparency in economic predictions.

The Town of Vail, Colorado, has become the first U.S. municipality to implement Hewlett Packard Enterprise’s (HPE) new Agentic AI Smart City Solution, developed in partnership with NVIDIA and several leading technology firms. The initiative aims to transform Vail into a sustainable, AI-powered smart city by enhancing public safety, automating city services, and improving quality of life for both residents and visitors.

UrbanLogiq has launched an AI-powered Global Foundation Model that enables governments to gain a unified digital view of how land use, infrastructure, and policy decisions interact across communities.

Cumberland County, Pennsylvania, is introducing artificial intelligence (AI) into its Public Defender’s Office to help manage an increasing caseload. The county commissioners approved a $173,000 contract with JusticeText, a company specializing in AI-powered discovery review software used in criminal defense.

The JusticeText platform allows attorneys to quickly analyze hours of video evidence within minutes, identifying key moments and reducing the time needed to prepare cases. According to Chief Public Defender Michael Halkias, this tool will help attorneys process cases more efficiently, while Commissioner Chairperson Kelly Neiderer emphasized that the AI points investigators “in a productive direction.”

The Washim sub-division police have rolled out a groundbreaking initiative — ‘Direct Dialogue with ASP' — that allows residents to connect directly with the Assistant Superintendent of Police (ASP) through AI-assisted video conferencing

Their robotic sorting system processes materials up to four times faster than manual methods. AMP Vision captures images and sends them to AI, which identifies each item based on material type, shape, color, polymer, and even brand. The AI then directs the robot to sort the waste with precision!

AI is helping Brazilian government companies cut costs and speed services: the National Treasury slashed COFOG tagging from 1,000 hours to 8 hours with >97% accuracy, PBIA earmarks ~R$23 billion through 2028, and INSS automation raised automated decisions ~17%→36%.

California is expanding its digital identity initiatives through new pilot programs and interagency collaborations, according to Chief Technology Officer Jonathan Porat. Building on successes like the mobile driver’s license and Login.gov pilot for Cal-ITP transportation benefits, the state aims to extend digital ID use beyond basic age or identity verification. The pilots now enable automatic eligibility verification for programs such as veteran, disability, and senior discounts via contactless payments, in partnership with the VA and Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services (CMS). California is also developing a digital portal with the Public Utilities Commission to help residents check eligibility for state and local benefits. To protect privacy, the initiative aligns with the Delete Act and the California Privacy Protection Agency, ensuring residents control their data and choose what to share. Porat emphasized that the approach minimizes government data storage while promoting secure, citizen-centered digital verification.

Starbridge, an AI-driven procurement technology company, has raised $42 million in Series A funding, led by Craft Ventures, following a $10 million seed round earlier in 2025. The company’s platform uses artificial intelligence to analyze procurement data and signals from public agencies, allowing technology vendors to identify opportunities, understand agency needs, and automate outreach. For example, a user can query “cities struggling with street cleanliness” and instantly receive a list of relevant municipalities, along with contact information for key officials and auto-generated personalized messages. Over 160 enterprise public-sector sales teams currently use Starbridge. The new funding will support product development, hiring, and expansion. This investment underscores the growing trend of AI integration into government procurement, as state CIOs and officials nationwide push for greater efficiency, flexibility, and modernization in public-sector contracting amid economic and tariff-related uncertainties.

The Chula Vista Police Department in California has become one of the first in the U.S. to adopt AI-generated police reports through Axon’s Draft One software, which uses a modified version of OpenAI’s ChatGPT to transcribe body camera audio into report drafts.

Germany’s Fraunhofer Institute for Wood Research has developed a smart fabric technology under its SenAD-2 project, embedding electrically conductive flax-fiber sensors within road pavement to continuously monitor road conditions. The sensors use AI algorithms to analyze stress and predict damage or repair needs, allowing authorities to assess pavement health without drilling or disrupting traffic. The system is currently being tested on an industrial road in Germany.

India’s Vehicle Scrappage Policy 2025 aims to phase out old and polluting vehicles to promote cleaner, safer, and more efficient transportation. Under the policy, private vehicles over 20 years and commercial vehicles over 15 years must pass automated fitness tests; unfit vehicles are deregistered and scrapped.
Benefits include: scrap value (4–6% of vehicle price), road tax rebates (up to 25% for private and 15% for commercial vehicles), and manufacturer discounts on new purchases. The policy reduces emissions, boosts the automobile industry, and supports a circular economy. Applications are fully digital, requiring submission at an authorized Vehicle Scrapping Facility, verification, deregistration, and issuance of a scrappage certificate for claiming incentives.

Idemia Public Security has launched LiveScan IntelliBook – Stand Alone (SA), a next-generation biometric platform designed to enhance the speed and accuracy of criminal and civil biometric processing for Canadian law enforcement. Presented during the “LiveScan 2.0: Modernizing Biometric Identification in Canadian Law Enforcement” webinar, the system integrates seamlessly with Canada’s criminal justice databases. It simplifies fingerprint and biographic data collection, reduces manual navigation, and increases operational efficiency for police and civil agencies.

India’s Environment Protection (End-of-Life Vehicles) Rules, 2025, issued by the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MOEFCC), introduce a centralized online portal to oversee the recycling and scrapping of all vehicle types, including electric and battery-powered ones. Managed by the Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB), the portal will handle registration, tracking, and Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) compliance between producers and registered scrapping facilities. A multi-agency committee will monitor implementation, ensuring coordination among ministries, regulators, and industry. The rules set EPR targets for producers based on vehicle type and lifespan, mandating responsible recycling of steel and components, aligning with existing rules for batteries, tyres, and used oil.

Paris has launched a trial car-sharing lane on its heavily congested ring road (périphérique) to curb traffic and pollution. Starting March 3, 2025, the outer lane is reserved during rush hours (7–10:30 a.m. and 4–8 p.m.) for vehicles with at least two occupants, as well as public transport, taxis, emergency, and disabled vehicles. The initiative aims to encourage ride-sharing and improve urban air quality on Europe’s busiest urban motorway.
India will introduce a simplified Goods and Services Tax (GST) registration framework effective November 1, 2025, to make tax compliance faster and more transparent

Mozambique’s 2028 roadmap places AI-driven VAT engines, e-invoicing validation, and real-time reporting at the core of its tax transformation strategy. The plan includes deploying machine learning for transaction monitoring, NLP for automated document review, predictive analytics for risk-based audits, and digital twins to simulate tax impacts.

Singapore Police Force has introduced R-COP, an AI-powered chatbot that helps the public lodge police reports more quickly and accurately at self-help kiosks starting 1 October 2025. R-COP guides users step-by-step, asks case-specific questions, and automatically drafts the police report for review. It reduces missing information, minimizing follow-up calls from Investigation Officers. The system includes safeguards like location verification via OneMap, security guardrails, and encrypted government data storage. Officers remain available to assist, and the initiative aims to free police time for frontline duties.

The Miami-Dade County Public Defender’s Office in Florida is using AI to manage its massive workload, including over 15,000 open cases and 75,000 cases per year. With the rise of digital evidence (texts, videos, audio), the office adopted CoCounsel, an AI legal platform, to help build timelines, summarize complex records, draft briefs, scan documents, and automate workflows

The Rourkela Police in Odisha has launched a pilot digital patrolling initiative called “E-Beat”, covering 100 beats across 12 police stations and over 600 sensitive locations such as ATMs, markets, parks, religious sites, and senior-citizen homes. 
 The system includes geo-mapping of beat locations, real-time mobile app tracking of officers, mobile attendance, digital patrol logs, and automatic alerts for missed rounds

Singapore FinTech Festival (SFF) 2025 will spotlight AI, tokenisation and quantum computing as the technologies shaping the next decade of global finance. The event focuses on building an open, trusted and interoperable financial ecosystem, covering AI-driven risk management and inclusion, programmable tokenised assets, CBDCs, and quantum-resilient systems. New initiatives include a 10th-anniversary tech gallery, Time Capsule 2035, Next Gen Leaders Programme, SME Sustainability Barometer, Innovation Lab Crawl, and deep-dive policy discussions. The goal: redefine how financial services are delivered and expand access worldwide.

Selangor’s 2026 Budget will boost public welfare and economic growth by accelerating digital transformation, AI adoption, and smart city development. Through the new Second Selangor Plan (RS-2) and the creation of the Selangor Metropolitan Corporation, the state aims to streamline governance, enhance service delivery, and strengthen high-tech industries such as semiconductors and AI. The budget supports major development projects, smart urban initiatives, and digital tourism strategies, while pursuing UNESCO World Heritage status for Gombak-Hulu Langat Geopark. Overall, Selangor aims to remain Malaysia’s economic leader through innovation, sustainability, and improved quality of life.

AI is reshaping global immigration systems by improving case processing, accuracy and fraud detection. Governments now use tools such as AI chatbots, automated document checks, predictive analytics, and triage algorithms to speed up applications and help applicants navigate complex rules. However, risks remain significant— including biased algorithms, oversimplified legal interpretations, data privacy concerns and security vulnerabilities. To ensure fairness and compliance, organisations must maintain human oversight, update AI systems regularly, audit for bias, protect sensitive data and ensure legal expertise remains central. The goal is a balanced model where AI enhances efficiency without compromising justice, equity or accountability.
