ICE has deployed Mobile Fortify, a new smartphone app that enables agents to perform real-time biometric identity checks using facial recognition and contactless fingerprints. The tool integrates with DHS databases containing over 270 million biometric records, extending border-style surveillance into U.S. streets and neighborhoods.

The Danish government has announced a landmark move to combat the rise of AI-generated deepfakes by amending its copyright law to grant individuals ownership rights over their own body, facial features, and voice. The change—believed to be the first of its kind in Europe

The city of Durham, North Carolina, through its public transit agency GoDurham, is piloting an AI-powered initiative called “Traffic Service Priority” aimed at enhancing bus performance, reducing travel times, and improving rider experience.

Researchers at the University of Maryland developed VoiceSecure, an AI-powered system that protects users from voice-based surveillance and biometric theft. It disguises vocal features that AI systems use to identify people—like tone, emotion, and accent

IRAS ensures corporate tax compliance through a mix of risk-based and random audits across industries. It uses data analytics and profiling tools to assess companies’ compliance risks and maintain broad oversight of the corporate sector.

The government of Punjab has introduced a new scheme called “Bill Liyao Inaam Pao” aimed at promoting tax compliance among citizens. 
Under this scheme, there will be a quarterly bumper draw that offers cash prizes: first prize ₹1,00,000; second prize ₹50,000; third prize ₹25,000.

Vietnam’s Ministry of Finance has proposed major amendments to its Tax Administration and Personal Income Tax laws to simplify procedures, enhance fairness, and stimulate economic growth. The draft introduces taxpayer classification, performance-based incentives for tax officials, and compliance relief measures. It raises the personal income tax exemption threshold to VND 200 million (≈ US$8,000) annually for individuals, increases family deductions, and reduces salary tax brackets from seven to five. Tax rates on digital and entertainment income will rise from 2% to 5%, while exemptions for prizes, royalties, and gifts double to US$800. Real-estate and capital transfer taxes remain largely unchanged. The reforms, expected to take effect from July 2026, aim to modernize tax administration, support small businesses, and promote transparency and innovation in Vietnam’s economy.

The Department of Pension & Pensioners’ Welfare (DoPPW) has reminded pensioners that they must submit their annual life certificate (Jeevan Pramaan) to continue receiving pension payments without interruption.

The Australian Capital Territory (ACT) has become the first jurisdiction in Australia to pass laws expanding institutional liability for child sexual abuse crimes committed by individuals such as clergy, volunteers, or coaches — even if they are not formal employees.

The UK Home Office has announced that seven police forces in England will be equipped with 10 new Live Facial Recognition (LFR) vans to help trace suspects involved in serious crimes such as murder and sexual assault. The technology—already in use by the Metropolitan Police in London—captures facial images in real time from public areas and matches them against a database of wanted individuals

SmarterPay Limited is helping UK public sector organisations such as councils, NHS trusts, and government bodies modernise their payment and collection systems through secure, cloud-based solutions that enhance efficiency, reduce fraud, and improve citizen services. Its platform simplifies financial operations—covering payroll, direct debits, supplier payments, and card transactions—by integrating multiple finance systems into one unified platform.

The Northern Territory Government (NTG) has launched a suite of procurement reforms to make it easier for businesses to work with the government, emphasizing a more business-friendly, efficient, and transparent procurement environment.
The government also introduced a new role, the Territory Procurement Champion, appointing Tom Harris, CEO of the Civil Contractors Federation NT. He will handle procurement complaints independently and collaborate with businesses and agencies to expand local contracting opportunities.

Law enforcement agencies in the U.S. and the U.K. are increasingly adopting live mobile facial recognition technology, known as Operator-Initiated Facial Recognition (OIFR), to identify criminal suspects and undocumented individuals during field interactions.

The Colorado Governor’s Office of Information Technology (OIT) has been on a mission in recent years to expand access to a digital tool known as Aira ASL, which provides real-time digital interpretation services with a live American Sign Language (ASL) interpreter for individuals who are deaf or hard of hearing

Google is extending its India-developed AI tools for agriculture — namely the Agricultural Landscape Understanding (ALU) API and the Agricultural Monitoring & Event Detection (AMED) API — to select countries in the Asia-Pacific region: Malaysia, Vietnam, Indonesia and Japan. 
These tools use machine learning and remote-sensing (satellite imagery) to map agricultural fields, identify water bodies, vegetation boundaries (via ALU), and monitor crop type, sowing & harvest events, and field-level changes (via AMED). Data refreshes every ~15 days

At the CoMotion LA 2025 conference in Los Angeles, transportation technology leaders highlighted how innovation teams are enabling agencies to explore unconventional mobility solutions such as portable restrooms at transit stations, tethered drones for lighting highway work zones, and zero-emission delivery zones.
A new app called Oculus Rail, created by former Norfolk City Council member Andria McClellan, alerts drivers when railroad crossings in Virginia’s Hampton Roads region are blocked

San Anselmo, California, is expanding its AI-driven traffic signal system after a successful pilot reduced wait times at the town’s busiest intersection by 25 to 30 percent. The Town Council approved a five-year contract with Roundabout Technologies, DC Electric and Parametrix to install the system at nine additional intersections in San Anselmo and one in Fairfax, supported by a $250,000 grant.

The government has notified the Digital Personal Data Protection (DPDP) Rules, operationalising the DPDP Act, 2023, to create a citizen-focused and innovation-friendly framework for managing digital personal data. The Rules, shaped through wide public consultation, provide an 18-month phased compliance period and require clear consent notices, verifiable parental consent for children, security measures such as encryption, prompt breach notifications, and accessible contact points like Data Protection Officers

Raleigh, North Carolina is piloting an AI-driven traffic management system that uses real-time data from rotating sets of 10–12 traffic cameras to analyze vehicle counts, turning movements, and pedestrian activity, feeding insights into the city’s GIS-based digital twin. In partnership with NVIDIA, Microsoft and Esri,

AI-based safety system on long-distance trains (East Central Railway)
The East Central Railway introduced an AI-powered system at Ara coaching depot that:

Automates coach cleaning and water refilling

Uses smart sensors on each coach to detect fire, brake binding, alarm chain pulling (ACP) and other hazards in real time

UK “See it. Say it. Sorted” campaign upgrade + £17m for station CCTV
The UK government refreshed its long-running rail security campaign with:

A new design that makes the British Transport Police 61016 text number more visible

Createc’s AI-powered system Situate, led by innovator Rosie Richardson, uses anonymous tracking and LIDAR to monitor crowd behaviour in train stations, detecting hazards such as running, overcrowding, unsafe platform activity, or loitering in restricted areas, and alerting staff in real time to improve passenger safety. The system assigns dots—not identities—to passengers, ensuring privacy while enabling targeted alerts and surveillance when needed

Greece will launch a pilot project at the Acropolis metro station using AI-powered cameras to detect ticket fraud by identifying multiple entries through the same gate and alerting staff in real time.

Micro, small, and medium enterprises (MSMEs) in Kerala can now register for professional tax through the KSWIFT single-window online platform, eliminating physical visits and simplifying the process. By uploading necessary licences and certificates, businesses can manage registration entirely online, easing compliance with mandatory professional tax requirements levied by local bodies.

The Inland Revenue Authority of Singapore (IRAS) is advancing digital transformation in tax administration to simplify processes, enhance efficiency and improve taxpayer experience through initiatives such as the GST InvoiceNow Requirement, which enables GST-registered businesses to submit invoice data directly to IRAS.

The Directorate of Treasury and Accounts in Punjab has launched major digital reforms including the SNA-SPARSH fund flow mechanism for centrally sponsored schemes, the Pensioner Sewa Portal for online pension services, and a new Audit Management System to offer real-time audit access and oversight, as part of efforts to modernise financial administration, boost transparency and efficiency across government departments. The SNA-SPARSH system integrates PFMS, state IFMS and RBI’s e-Kuber to increase cash liquidity and reduce parked funds, with the state targeting a Rs 350 crore incentive under SASCI 2025-26; the Pensioner portal enables e-PPO delivery, real-time tracking, grievance handling and life-certificate integration; and the Audit Management System gives stakeholders live access to audit reports and plans to integrate the Accountant General’s reports, while other initiatives include an e-voucher system for bills and a Non-Treasury Module for departmental deposit works accounting.

The Pensions Regulator (TPR) has introduced a new support service to help innovators develop solutions that could improve UK pension outcomes by removing unnecessary regulatory barriers and enabling early collaboration

The Philippines has launched a digital transparency portal and technology-driven oversight reforms to curb corruption and strengthen accountability in infrastructure projects by giving the public real-time access to data on contractors, agencies, locations and project status. The reforms improve project design, procurement and payment systems while enhancing data security and using AI and smart technologies to monitor construction quality, detect anomalies and ensure integrity

USConveyor, with extensive expertise in custom scrap metal recycling systems, works with ZenRobotics to integrate AI-powered robotic solutions into both new and legacy processing lines, boosting efficiency, safety and purity in metal recovery. Their first joint project supplied three Heavy Pickers capable of autonomously separating copper meatballs, wires and trash from ferrous metals, helping steel producers meet strict purity standards such as maintaining copper content below 0.1%.

The World Shipping Council (WSC) has launched the industry’s first Cargo Safety Program to prevent ship fires by detecting misdeclared and undeclared dangerous goods, combining AI-powered cargo screening with common inspection standards to identify high-risk shipments before loading

Canada introduced Bill C-15, the Budget 2025 Implementation Act, No. 1, to advance key “Canada Strong” priorities aimed at building a unified, resilient economy by investing in housing, clean electricity, productivity, transportation, and research, while also making the tax system fairer and strengthening the financial sector. The bill includes measures to double affordable homebuilding through Build Canada Homes; deliver clean electricity investment tax credits; introduce a Productivity Super-Deduction for new capital investments; accelerate construction of the Alto High-Speed Rail; and enhance scientific research support. It proposes tax fairness measures such as exempting the Canada Disability Benefit from income, expanding disability-related deductions, creating a temporary PSW tax credit, increasing the Lifetime Capital Gains Exemption, and eliminating the Underused Housing Tax. Financial-sector reforms include requirements for banks to combat consumer fraud, faster access to cheque deposits, easing federal entry for credit unions, completing the consumer-driven banking framework, and regulating stablecoins. The bill also introduces an Early Retirement Incentive Program to support public service workforce renewal.

The Washington Legislature passed several new laws in 2025 to strengthen consumer protections, including right-to-repair requirements for electronics and mobility devices, banning medical debt from credit scores, ensuring property owners’ rights to appraisals, requiring auto insurance policies to include appraisal provisions, restricting sales of sodium nitrite under “Tyler’s Law,” updating WA Cares safeguards, improving safety standards for electric vehicle charging station installation, adding textured-hair training in cosmetology programs, enabling multi-state professional licensing, setting strict limits on lead in cookware, increasing the bank account exemption for individuals facing wage garnishment, and requiring that documents shared with federal oversight agencies also be made available to the state attorney general for antitrust enforcement.

The Global Innovation Lab for Climate Finance endorsed nine innovative financial instruments designed to address major climate investment barriers in emerging markets and unlock USD 425 million through tools such as parametric insurance, carbon credits, and structured equity, targeting sectors including agriculture, renewable energy, and first-of-its-kind climate technologies. These solutions aim to expand clean energy access, strengthen climate resilience, support sustainable land management, and improve financial stability for vulnerable farmers, with pilots planned across Asia, Africa, and Latin America

A new integrated payments platform has been launched to help cities manage, track, and reconcile public funds more simply and transparently by providing a single view of payments across services such as parking, transport, permits, and enforcement. The system connects with existing municipal infrastructure to unify payment and reconciliation processes, with CTO Gene Rohrwasser stating that Passport Payments simplifies one of the most complex and critical city functions: the movement of money.

Canada is launching a fast-track immigration pathway for H-1B visa holders as part of its 2025 Federal Budget strategy to attract global talent, address labour shortages, and strengthen its innovation ecosystem, particularly in healthcare, research, and advanced technology. The plan includes a one-time initiative to recruit over 1,000 international researchers supported by up to CA$1.7 billion for research chairs, infrastructure, relocation support for PhD students and postdoctoral fellows, and hiring international assistant professors. The budget also proposes a CA$97 million Foreign Credential Recognition Action Fund to streamline licensing in priority sectors such as healthcare and construction. These measures align with Prime Minister Mark Carney’s commitment to targeted talent recruitment and broader reforms to the Temporary Foreign Worker Program, positioning Canada as a stable and attractive destination for skilled professionals amid tightening U.S. visa policies.
ECOWAS is integrating artificial intelligence into its early warning systems to strengthen crime analysis, prediction, and prevention across West Africa

Oklahoma has launched a 45-day pilot program at Red Rock Correctional Center to test AI-equipped drones from Skydio as a new tool to combat rising prison contraband, including weapons, cellphones, drugs, and tobacco
The UK Ministry of Justice has launched a new Counter-Drone Innovation Challenge to address the sharp rise—770% —of drones being used by organised crime groups to smuggle contraband into prisons.

The UK government has opened HMP Millsike in East Yorkshire, the country’s first “green” prison and one of its largest, adding 1,500 new places to help ease overcrowding in the prison estate of England and Wales.

Costa Rica will begin building a new maximum-security prison this year, inspired by El Salvador’s CECOT mega-prison, to address surging gang-related violence and severe overcrowding in existing facilities

Amazon has proposed a major reform to the UK’s VAT system for online marketplaces by extending the “deemed reseller” model to all third-party sellers—UK-based or overseas—so that marketplaces, not sellers, collect and remit VAT on every sale.

Ghana’s Sustained National Tax Education Programme (2025–2028) aims to improve nationwide tax awareness and voluntary compliance by delivering continuous education through media, schools, communities, and multilingual outreach. The initiative seeks to build trust in the tax system, expand the tax base, and ensure that citizens and businesses understand and fulfil their tax responsibilities, working in partnership with government bodies, civil society, and the private sector.
Belgium is introducing a new capital-gains tax on financial assets — sometimes called the “solidarity contribution.
The system uses facial recognition to authenticate inactive members, allowing them to file retirement, separation and life insurance claims securely

As fraud in public programs becomes a major political concern, states are increasingly adopting AI and data analytics for early detection, yet experts warn that technology alone cannot solve the problem without structural reforms, cross-agency coordination, and clear fraud definitions. Examples include California Community Colleges using AI to detect fake student enrollments—where 31% of aid applicants were fraudulent—and Minnesota’s Housing Stabilization Services program, where sophisticated provider fraud exploited oversight gaps. States like Louisiana are using AI to verify Medicaid eligibility, while CMS is piloting WISeR to target low-value services at high fraud risk. However, the full scale of fraud remains unknown, since improper payments often reflect administrative errors rather than criminal activity. Ultimately, restoring public trust requires combining AI-driven real-time detection with stronger governance, ethical oversight, and balanced scrutiny of both providers and beneficiaries.

El Paso, Texas modernized its 911 emergency network by replacing outdated infrastructure with a cloud-based, AI-enabled system that improves speed, accuracy, and resilience across public safety services. The county introduced network segmentation, zero-trust architecture, and real-time monitoring to reduce congestion and cybersecurity risks, while deploying AI tools that transcribe calls, summarize conversations, and provide real-time language translation
GREEN$ ePIS is designed to encourage cleaner recycling habits by offering incentives to residents who use the EPD’s community recycling network, known as GREEN@COMMUNITY.

Virginia enacted several impactful new laws, including a seat-belt law requiring all adult occupants of a vehicle — front and back seats — to wear a seat belt (previously only front-seat adults were required).

The Superior Council of Labor Justice (CSJT) launched, last Monday (February 3), the Labor Justice Artificial Intelligence project and, with it, the first generative AI tool (Chat-JT), which was developed to contribute to the work of magistrates, employees and interns of the institution in a safer and more efficient way.

A workshop hosted by the U.S. National Renewable Energy Laboratory (NREL) gathered more than 50 experts who concluded that artificial intelligence and autonomous experimentation could dramatically accelerate materials discovery while reshaping the entire pipeline from research to industrial deployment.

Indonesia has launched QRIS Tap In–Tap Out, a new NFC-enabled digital payment system that allows commuters to pay for public transport by simply tapping their mobile phones, completing transactions in just 0.3 seconds. Initially used on Jakarta’s MRT, it now covers LRT, commuter trains, buses, and will expand to ferries and retail payments nationwide. The initiative is part of the Indonesia Payment System Blueprint 2025–2030, aiming for an inclusive, efficient national payment ecosystem with zero merchant fees. With 58 million users and extensive cross-border QRIS integration, Indonesia is positioning itself as a regional digital payments leader. Bank Indonesia stresses that collaboration, public trust, and AI-powered risk management are essential for securing the system and supporting Indonesia’s broader “Golden Indonesia 2045” digital transformation vision.

U.S. state procurement offices are beginning to adopt artificial intelligence to modernise purchasing processes, improve efficiency, and strengthen risk management. Early AI applications include automated document drafting, contract analysis, fraud detection, and spend analytics, helping procurement teams handle increasing workloads with limited staff

Indonesia has launched a new integrated platform for international arrivals that centralises immigration, customs and quarantine processes into a single unified system to speed up border procedures and enhance national security
San Diego plans to introduce predictive analysis to identify pothole hotspots in underserved neighborhoods

New York City launched two new Smart City Testbed pilots to analyse pedestrian movement in public spaces and to let residents visualise a major new community facility using augmented reality. These pilots aim to improve street safety, enhance infrastructure management, and increase community engagement before scaling citywide.

Researchers at NYU Tandon School of Engineering have created SeeUnsafe, a multimodal AI system that analyses existing traffic-camera footage to automatically detect collisions and near-misses. The tool uses multimodal large language models (MLLMs) to review long-form video, eliminating the need for manual monitoring and enabling cities to extract continuous road-safety insights rather than relying solely on crash reports. The system received New York City’s Vision Zero Research Award

Securus Technologies has developed an AI system trained on years of recorded prison phone and video calls to detect conversations where crimes may be planned or “contemplated.” The company has been piloting the model since 2024, scanning inmates’ real-time calls, texts, and emails to flag suspicious patterns for human review.

Malaysia is launching a nationwide cybersecurity upgrade by integrating MyDigital ID authentication across all telecommunications platforms. Starting tomorrow, every mobile number—existing and new—must be linked to a verified digital identity, significantly reducing fraud, SIM misuse, and identity spoofing.

Selangor is positioning its technology-driven sectors—particularly aerospace, advanced manufacturing, and digital transformation infrastructure—as central engines for investment and economic growth in the coming year. The state aims to strengthen high-tech industries such as aerospace MRO, component manufacturing, electrical and electronics, machinery, transport systems, and Industry 4.0–aligned smart factories powered by robotics, automation, AI, and data analytics. Supported by national incentives for automation and innovation-led growth, Selangor is advancing regulatory reforms, streamlined approvals, and targeted innovation programmes to attract investors, accelerate commercialisation, and enhance industrial competitiveness. With RM3.23 billion allocated for development and innovation-linked initiatives, the state seeks to improve ecosystem readiness, promote regional and international collaboration, and solidify its role as Malaysia’s leading hub for high-value, technology-intensive industries.

Malaysia has launched a national–regional investment partnership to accelerate high-value investments, support technology adoption, and enhance industrial competitiveness. The initiative provides structured financing, cross-border advisory services, and ESG-aligned funding to help businesses scale and integrate into regional value chains. SMEs benefit from targeted support in digitalisation, automation, and supply chain optimisation. Advanced analytics and digital platforms guide investment decisions, while green-transition financing promotes sustainable industrial development. The partnership strengthens regional integration and positions Malaysia as a leading hub for technology-driven, high-impact investments.

Vietnam has launched a US$10 million Smart City Operation Centre in Tam Ky ward, Da Nang, funded mainly by KOICA, to enhance digital urban governance. The centre integrates traffic cameras, flood-warning systems, and unified data platforms to support e-government services, tourism management, environmental monitoring, and traffic oversight. It is the first large-scale digital transformation project in the locality, developed through strong Vietnam–Korea cooperation, and will expand smart services over time

U.S. cities are increasingly adopting interactive digital signage—from AI-enabled birdwatching displays in Sandy Springs, Georgia, to multifunction kiosks in major cities like Houston, Chicago, Dallas and Seattle—to improve public engagement, accessibility and real-time information sharing. These digital tools support services such as wayfinding, event updates, emergency alerts and free public Wi-Fi, while some kiosk programmes even generate revenue through advertising at no cost to the city. Governments see the technology as a way to reach residents more effectively, modernise communications and enhance urban experiences, with future plans exploring AI integration for real-time analytics and smarter city services.

China has introduced new tax reporting requirements for internet platform companies under the 2025 Provisions on the Submission of Tax-Related Information, obliging platforms to submit basic business details, as well as the identity and income information of operators and employees, with the first quarterly submission covering Q3 2025 due by October 31.

The UK government has announced a new VAT relief to take effect on 1 April 2026, removing VAT charges on goods donated by businesses to registered charities. The measure aims to reduce waste, support the circular economy, and encourage companies to donate surplus or unused goods instead of sending them to landfill.

The UK government will update the sugar tax (Soft Drinks Industry Levy) in 2028. The sugar threshold will drop from 5g to 4.5g per 100ml, meaning more drinks will be taxed. The levy will also extend to milk-based drinks and milk substitutes, removing previous exemptions.

Rajasthan Police is establishing a dedicated digital forensic unit to tackle the growing threat of AI-driven crimes such as voice spoofing, deepfakes, and automated calling scams. The new unit aims to enhance the force’s technical capabilities in detecting, analysing, and prosecuting cyber- and AI-enabled offences — a response to the rising sophistication of criminal activity. The move comes as part of a broader modernization effort to bolster cybercrime response and protect citizens in the digital domain.

The European Commission has unveiled the Digital Justice Package 2030, a strategic roadmap to transform and digitalise justice systems across the EU. The package includes two core pillars: the DigitalJustice@2030 Strategy and the European Judicial Training Strategy 2025–2030. Together, they aim to modernise justice through advanced technologies—including artificial intelligence—improving efficiency, reducing costs, increasing transparency, and strengthening access to justice for citizens and businesses.

Greece has announced a major digital transformation initiative for its judicial system through a collaboration between the Ministry of Justice and the Ministry of Digital Governance. The project introduces new AI tools designed to increase court efficiency, accelerate case processing, and reduce operational costs. The suite includes automatic document translation between Greek and English, Italian, Chinese, and Arabic; real-time interpretation of foreign witness testimonies; and automated transcription of court proceedings. These tools address chronic delays caused by high translation workloads and limited availability of specialized translators. The systems are being developed in partnership with the National Infrastructures for Research and Technology (GRNET) under a formal cooperation agreement.

Sri Lanka has approved key amendments to its Personal Data Protection Act (PDPA), creating a more flexible and innovation-friendly regulatory environment. The changes allow institutions to make judgment-based decisions on cross-border data storage and processing, enabling the use of resident, sovereign, or public cloud platforms depending on data sensitivity.

The Philippines is strengthening digital inclusion through two major initiatives targeting underserved populations. The Department of Social Welfare and Development (DSWD) rolled out the Digital Financial Inclusion Initiative to equip 4Ps beneficiaries—especially in geographically isolated and disadvantaged areas—with smartphones, e-wallet skills, and safe digital transaction practices, reaching more than 32,000 households and integrating financial literacy into Family Development Sessions

Batac City in the Philippines has launched the Paleng-QR Ph Plus Programme at its public market to promote financial inclusion and modernise local commerce by enabling vendors, tricycle drivers and consumers to use fast, safe and convenient QR-based digital payments

New Zealand is streamlining the way government agencies procure digital identity services by launching a new Digital Identity Services channel on the Department of Internal Affairs’ (DIA) Marketplace platform next month

Sweden has launched two major AMIF-funded integration projects: a new Centre for Migration and Integration at the Stockholm School of Economics to generate research on how policies and labour conditions affect migrant integration, and a national model—run by Kompis Sverige—for supporting newly arrived third-country nationals through language learning, civic education and social participation in at least 40 municipalities. New research highlights widespread ethnic discrimination in recruitment and recommends stronger diversity measures and standardised hiring processes. Additional Nordic initiatives showcase successful integration practices, while new studies reveal the negative mental-health impact of temporary residence permits. Sweden is also developing an integration barometer to better measure migrants’ democratic, social and cultural integration, supported by a Nordic Council report reviewing current integration indicators.

Researchers at the Hong Kong University of Science and Technology (HKUST) have developed a new class of programmable soft composite materials that exhibit direction-dependent mechanical behavior, marking a major breakthrough in mechano-intelligent systems. The innovation integrates shear-jamming transitions—a phenomenon where materials stiffen under deformation—into soft polymer matrices, enabling materials that can shift between flexible and rigid states on demand. Unlike traditional metamaterials that rely on complex and fragile architectures, these composites maintain toughness and resist fractures while offering non-reciprocal motion, directional force control, and shape-memory capabilities. The materials can also be programmed and customized for stiffness, shape retention, and responsiveness, supporting applications in soft robotics, adaptive structures, microfluidic smart valves, and next-generation smart devices. HKUST researchers further demonstrated motion control by pairing the composites with spatially modulated magnetic fields, enabling bio-inspired soft robots capable of navigating constrained environments. This development represents a new paradigm for intelligent, autonomous, and adaptable material systems.

The EU-funded Sawian project in Finland works to prevent youth crime, violence, and radicalisation among 10–22-year-olds with migrant backgrounds by improving their well-being, integration, and family support. Through collaboration with schools, police, and local communities, the project has reached youth in 28 schools, offering individual and group activities, native-language support, and 424 counselling sessions for parents who struggle to help their children navigate between two cultures. Sawian helps young people build positive routines such as sports, strengthens peer relationships, reduces bullying and gang risks, and improves school performance. The project is run by the Finnish Refugee Council and Aseman Lapset, co-funded by STEA and the EU Internal Security Fund.

Delhi Metro Rail Corporation (DMRC) has installed AI-powered X-BIS baggage scanners at major metro stations to strengthen passenger security. The scanners use advanced imaging and automatic threat detection to identify dangerous items in real time. DMRC is also upgrading older metro trains with modern features such as live route maps, real-time ETA information, new CCTV systems, charging points, and improved interiors. These upgrades aim to improve safety, travel comfort, and overall commuter experience across the network.

The U.S. Federal Railroad Administration has approved a waiver allowing freight railroads to reduce human track inspections from twice weekly to once a week, relying more on automated inspection technology that uses cameras and lasers to detect alignment and geometry defects. Rail companies argue the technology is more sensitive and finds far more problems than manual checks, citing multi-year tests by BNSF and Norfolk Southern. However, the inspectors’ union warns that machines cannot detect critical issues like shifting ballast, rotting ties, cracks, or combined small defects that humans spot through experience, and says reducing inspections will increase derailment risks. The FRA did not allow longer repair timelines—serious defects must still be fixed immediately—and emphasized that human inspections and storm-related special inspections will continue. Railroads claim the policy will let inspectors focus more on components that still require hands-on assessment.

The U.S. Air Force is testing wearable biometric devices to enhance in-flight safety by monitoring pilots’ respiration, detecting hypoxia, and measuring cabin altitude in real time. The 428th Fighter Squadron plans to procure 30 wearable sensor systems—including biometric earcups, respiration sensors, and analysis laptops—integrated into standard aircrew gear. The initiative aims to improve physiological awareness, prevent hypoxia-related incidents, and support post-flight debriefings. Small business vendors are being surveyed for potential contracting, and all work must meet strict Air Force security protocols. If successful, the program could lead to wider adoption of biometric monitoring across military aviation.

The U.S. Navy is expanding its cybersecurity modernization by integrating AI into zero trust authentication, aiming for continuous, behavior-based identity verification across its enterprise and operational systems. AI models are being piloted to analyze login behavior, device usage, and contextual patterns to detect anomalies and dynamically score access risks. The Navy’s Flank Speed Microsoft 365 cloud environment—supporting 750,000 users—has already met nearly all DoD zero-trust technical requirements and serves as a key testing ground for advanced authentication and monitoring tools. Efforts are also underway to extend zero trust to operational technology, including ship control and weapons systems, requiring AI systems that can operate reliably in contested environments. The Navy emphasizes explainable, auditable AI with human oversight to counter risks such as spoofing and data poisoning. These initiatives align with DoD strategies and reflect a long-term shift toward adaptive, identity-centric cybersecurity.

The Harvard duo known for hacking facial recognition into Meta’s smart glasses has launched a new startup, Halo, developing Halo X, a pair of AI-powered smart glasses that continuously records, listens, and transcribes conversations, providing real-time answers, translations, memory recall, and data summaries through an invisible display. Using LLMs like Google Gemini and Perplexity, the glasses aim to give users “superhuman intelligence.” Priced at $249 and shipping in Q1 2026

British Transport Police (BTP) will begin a six-month pilot of live facial recognition at major London railway stations, aiming to identify high-risk offenders passing through crime hotspots. The rollout—part of a broader UK expansion of police use of LFR—will involve temporary cameras scanning crowds and matching faces against a watchlist, with unmatched images deleted automatically. Although the pilot follows a recent mass stabbing on a train, BTP says the project was already planned and is not a direct response to the incident. The force pledges ethical deployment with clear signage, public information, and a full evaluation after the trial to determine future use, amid ongoing debate about balancing safety with privacy concerns.

The Internal Revenue Service Math and Taxpayer Help Act (H.R. 998) has been signed into law, delivering major reforms to strengthen taxpayer rights and improve IRS transparency. The law requires the IRS to clearly explain exactly what error was made, specify the line number on the tax return, state the reason for the adjustment, and prominently inform taxpayers of their 60-day right to request abatement. Math error notices have long confused taxpayers—many were vague or missing the 60-day warning—leading people to lose their right to challenge IRS changes in Tax Court. The Act also launches a pilot program requiring certified or registered mail for these notices to ensure proper delivery. The bipartisan legislation aims to make IRS communication clearer, protect due process, reduce taxpayer frustration, minimize errors, and enhance trust in the tax system.

Canada’s 2025 Budget introduces wide-ranging tax reforms affecting individuals, workers, businesses, and investment rules. Key measures include a new Personal Support Workers Tax Credit, CRA authority for automatic tax filing for low-income non-filers, a temporary Top-Up Tax Credit to prevent tax increases from the middle-class rate cut, and major simplification of qualified investment rules for registered plans. The budget tightens anti-avoidance rules for trusts, improves information sharing to address worker misclassification, ends double-claiming between medical and home-accessibility credits, and eliminates the Underused Housing Tax starting 2025 while removing the luxury tax on aircraft and vessels. Businesses benefit from immediate expensing for manufacturing buildings, enhanced SR&ED credits, expanded tax incentives for critical minerals, clean technology manufacturing, and carbon capture (CCUS). The budget strengthens anti-deferral rules for tiered corporate structures, updates transfer pricing rules to OECD standards, and ensures foreign affiliates’ investment income related to Canadian insurance risks is fully taxable. New GST/HST rules target carousel fraud, clarify taxation of manual osteopathic services, and adjust various technical provisions. Overall, Budget 2025 aims to modernize the tax system, close loopholes, promote clean growth, support workers, and simplify compliance.

The Taxation (Annual Rates for 2025–26, Compliance Simplification, and Remedial Measures) Bill focuses on making New Zealand’s tax system more “migrant-friendly” and easing some compliance burdens, without delivering the major FBT simplification previously signalled. It introduces a new “non-resident visitor” category aimed at digital nomads, exempting certain remote workers from NZ tax residence, NZ-source services income, and some PE/residence risks for foreign companies, provided strict conditions are met. A new Revenue Account Method (RAM) is created for new/returning residents with unlisted offshore shares, taxing dividends and 70% of realised gains/losses instead of deemed FIF income, mainly deferring tax until cash is available. For employee share schemes, the Bill allows unlisted companies to designate “employee deferred shares” so tax is triggered only at a liquidity event (listing, sale, or dividend), but it also unexpectedly moves the taxing point to when employees have an “unconditional right to presently receive shares,” which may tax them before they actually receive them and breaks symmetry with employer deductions. In FBT, the big reforms are absent; instead, all gift cards are brought clearly into FBT (no de minimis), treatment of reimbursements and global insurance allocation is clarified, and some formula/technical fixes are made. Other measures include: allowing GST flow-through for unincorporated joint ventures, exempting income from selling excess residential electricity back to retailers, expanding information-sharing powers, repealing specific trust disclosure provisions (with IR still able to collect data via general powers), and significantly raising cash-basis thresholds to reflect that they haven’t been updated since 1999.

The UN Joint Staff Pension Fund (UNJSPF) and the UN International Computing Centre have introduced a major breakthrough in digital identity verification by deploying a blockchain-based Digital Certificate of Entitlement (DCE), replacing decades of paper-based pension verification for over 70,000 beneficiaries in 190 countries. The system uses blockchain, biometrics, AI, and geo-location to securely validate pensioners, reducing paper processing by 40%, archiving costs by 95%, overtime expenses by 76.5%, and achieving a 99.96% digital user retention rate. A new DCE Consortium will offer the solution as a service to other UN bodies, aligning with broader UN initiatives such as the UN Digital ID — a portable, interoperable identity system integrating blockchain and biometrics for staff across more than 30 UN organizations, aiming to build a borderless, unified digital ecosystem.

Australia’s major banks report significant success in preventing fraud after joining the BioCatch Trust Network, a real-time behavioral biometrics intelligence-sharing system now covering over 85% of the country’s banked population. In Q3 2025 alone, the network analyzed 180 million payments worth $330 billion and detected more than $60 million in attempted fraud, successfully retrieving beneficiary profiles in over 70% of transactions to assess risk before money moved. Despite a 20% drop in money-laundering activity, threats such as account-takeover fraud have surged 47%, driven by organized crime groups. Experts emphasize the need for “Safety by Design” in payment systems, while banks praise the network’s ability to disrupt mule accounts through real-time collaboration.

The Kerala High Court has mandated the use of the Adalat.AI speech-to-text tool for recording witness depositions in all courts across the state starting November 1. According to an official memorandum, depositions must be recorded primarily using Adalat.AI; if technical issues occur, courts may use alternative tools only with prior approval from the High Court’s IT directorate to ensure data security. Once recorded and signed, depositions will be uploaded to the District Court Case Management System (DCMS) so parties and lawyers can access them digitally. This move aims to reduce delays and modernize evidence recording. The tool was earlier piloted in select courts in Ernakulam beginning February 1, following the High Court's administrative decision to introduce AI-based transcription across all courts.

New York City has passed the GUARD Act, creating an independent Office of Algorithmic Accountability to audit, monitor and regulate the use of AI systems across city agencies. The office will investigate public complaints, enforce standards for fairness, privacy and transparency, and publish assessments of AI tools before deployment. Alongside this oversight effort, the city launched a Grassroots AI Education and Engagement Initiative, funding 22 community organizations to train over 400 community leaders and host more than 100 multilingual AI education sessions by 2026. Together, these initiatives aim to ensure responsible government use of AI and improve public understanding as automated systems increasingly influence housing, policing and public services.

U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) has launched a new mobile facial-recognition app called Mobile Identify for local police participating in the federal 287(g) immigration enforcement program. The app allows officers to scan faces in the field and receive instructions from ICE based on biometric matches—but without providing names or technical transparency. The tool expands DHS’s biometric surveillance deeper into everyday policing, raising serious concerns about privacy, accuracy, civil rights, and oversight, especially because DHS released it without a required Privacy Impact Assessment or data-retention disclosures. Evidence suggests the app may rely on CBP’s Traveler Verification Service—the same massive facial recognition database used at airports—extending border biometric systems into interior policing. Critics warn that the system risks false matches, racial bias, mistaken detentions, and warrantless surveillance, especially since people cannot opt out and local officers may act on opaque federal determinations. The rollout comes amid rapid expansion of the 287(g) program, despite long-standing federal findings that oversight and officer training remain inadequate.

A new report from the Privacy and Civil Liberties Oversight Board (PCLOB) reveals that the FBI has become heavily dependent on three commercial surveillance tools—Clearview AI, Babel Street, and ZeroFox—to power its open-source intelligence (OSINT) investigations. These tools enable rapid facial identification, large-scale analysis of social media and online activity, and real-time threat monitoring across the open web, deep web, and dark web. Although PCLOB confirmed the FBI’s extensive use of these systems, most operational details were withheld in a classified annex, highlighting both their importance and sensitivity. The report warns that aggregating massive amounts of “public” data can still pose major civil liberties risks, especially since the FBI’s use lacks public transparency. Together, these tools now form the core of the bureau’s investigative workflow, allowing agents to link identities, map networks, and monitor threats in ways far beyond traditional OSINT, raising urgent questions about privacy, oversight, and the handling of First Amendment-protected activity.

Ant International has unveiled Alipay+ GlassPay, a new smart-glasses payment solution that introduces iris biometric authentication for the first time in AR-based commerce. Developed with Xiaomi and Meizu, the glasses use AI-powered iris recognition with over 260 biometric feature points and robust liveness detection to prevent spoofing. This enhances security alongside existing voiceprint authentication and supports seamless AR shopping experiences such as instant try-ons and frictionless checkout. The solution is built on Ant’s secure gPass framework, offering end-to-end encryption and compliance for global markets. Following successful trials on AlipayHK, the system will be rolled out across the Asia Pacific. Ant continues expanding multimodal biometrics, including palm-scanning payments and deepfake-resistant eKYC tools.

Web3 companies are accelerating the adoption of biometric and decentralized digital identity technologies, led by IOST’s launch of its Signet Ring—a wearable device that links a user’s physical presence to an on-chain identity using heartbeat-based biometrics, enabling payments, KYC-free verification, PoP, and access to tokenized ecosystems. InterLink Labs also received Google for Startups funding to scale its facial-biometric decentralized ID system, which has already registered over one million scans. Meanwhile, crypto platform Mercuryo introduced biometric passkeys for secure fiat-to-crypto transactions, and Eicol Exchange launched a decentralized digital ID system enabling cross-platform authentication, governance, and secure interaction across Web3. Collectively, these developments reflect a growing push to combat AI-driven fraud, enhance security, and support real-world asset tokenization through next-generation digital identity tools.

Iasi County in Romania used public procurement to promote inclusive employment by launching a reserved contract for bookbinding and archival services specifically for sheltered workshops and social enterprises employing people with disabilities. Using Romanian laws that allow such reserved contracts, the county consulted the market and designed criteria requiring bidders to prove their protected-unit status and rewarding those employing more vulnerable workers. One eligible social enterprise applied, engaging 10 employees with disabilities and hiring two more to deliver the contract. This approach strengthened local social inclusion, supported sustainable development, and demonstrated how procurement can directly create job opportunities for people with disabilities.

The TSA and DHS Science & Technology Directorate are developing a new wearable device called the WSCPA (Wearable Sensor for Contactless Physical Assessment), which aims to replace invasive airport pat-downs with touchless, privacy-preserving screening. Using radar, ultrasound, and 3D sensing, the device can detect the shape, density, and composition of concealed items and translate that information into haptic feedback that TSA officers can “feel” without physical contact. Still in early development, WSCPA could improve safety, accuracy, and public health protections while reducing civil liberties concerns, and may eventually be used beyond airports by law enforcement, customs officers, and first responders. However, the technology faces challenges related to accuracy, usability, training, data governance, and large-scale deployment.

Indian Railways is advancing the use of artificial intelligence to improve safety and predictive maintenance, including deploying an AI-enabled Intrusion Detection System using Distributed Acoustic Systems to detect elephant movement along railway tracks. The system is currently operational across 141 route kilometers on the Northeast Frontier Railway, with additional tenders awarded to expand coverage to 981 route kilometers nationwide, providing real-time alerts to loco pilots, station masters and control rooms to prevent collisions. Alongside this, Indian Railways is piloting AI-based predictive maintenance for signaling systems, adopting technologies such as Online Monitoring of Rolling Stock Systems and Wheel Impact Load Detectors, and signing MoUs to introduce AI-driven machine vision inspection for moving trains and automatic, non-contact wheel profile measurement to enhance operational safety, reliability and efficiency.

Indian Railways has installed 112 AI-powered facial recognition cameras across 21 major stations under the East Central Railway to strengthen passenger safety and deter crime. The system automatically identifies individuals with criminal records and triggers real-time alerts for immediate action by railway security forces, supported by a dedicated 24/7 monitoring “war room” for rapid coordination with law enforcement. High-traffic and security-sensitive stations in Bihar and Jharkhand, including Patna Junction and Rajendra Nagar Terminal, are now under constant surveillance, with officials describing the initiative as a major step toward modernizing railway security while maintaining privacy safeguards.

As Victoria prepares to open the West Gate Tunnel, a new state-of-the-art road network control centre will play a pivotal role in real-time smart traffic management across Melbourne. The high-capacity facility will monitor and manage around 38 kilometres of major arterial roads, integrating nearly 900 cameras, automated incident detection, intelligent transport systems, variable speed and lane controls, and over-height vehicle detection to improve safety, reduce congestion, and enable rapid incident response. Operating continuously and coordinated with Transport Victoria’s wider network operations, the centre has undergone extensive testing to ensure operational readiness. By optimising traffic flow and diverting thousands of trucks from local roads, the system is expected to enhance travel reliability, improve road safety, and support economic and environmental benefits, demonstrating how digital control and automation can significantly extend the performance of urban transport infrastructure.

Google has introduced Emergency Live Video on Android, a new feature that allows people calling or texting emergency services to share live video directly with 911 dispatchers and first responders upon request. With a single tap, users can stream encrypted real-time footage from their smartphones, helping emergency operators better assess situations such as medical emergencies, fires, or crimes, while retaining full control to stop sharing at any time. Supported by major public safety technology providers Motorola Solutions and RapidSOS, the tool aims to improve response speed and accuracy by giving dispatchers visual context, marking a significant step in the evolution of emergency communications alongside broader trends such as AI, livestreaming, and drone integration.

Since its launch in March 2022, Vietnam’s eTax Mobile application has achieved significant success, recording over 13 million downloads, processing more than 17.2 million transactions, and collecting over 26.5 trillion VND (about USD 1.1 billion) for the state budget. Usage surged in 2025, with over seven million new users and 13.3 million transactions, driven by continuous upgrades based on a “one-stop, one-touch” model and integration with VNeID for full digital tax services anytime and anywhere. Recent enhancements, including speech-to-text, text-to-speech, and a new AI-powered Chatbot launched in December 2025, have improved accessibility, real-time support, and user experience, reinforcing public trust and positioning eTax Mobile as Vietnam’s leading business application while advancing digital transformation in tax administration.

Singapore’s Inland Revenue Authority (IRAS) has transformed tax compliance through a fully digital, AI-enabled ecosystem aligned with the Smart Nation initiative. At its core is the myTax Portal, a secure one-stop platform that allows businesses to file corporate and GST returns, make payments, access correspondence, and apply for schemes entirely online

The Pensions Scams Action Group (PSAG), working with The Pensions Regulator (TPR), has developed a new AI-driven tool that uses machine learning and real-world data to detect and combat fraudulent pension-related websites amid a growing threat of online scams. So far, the initiative has reviewed 830 websites, taken down 29 high-risk sites, and made 94 referrals to partner agencies, helping protect thousands of savers. This effort is supported by closer intelligence-sharing with key bodies such as the City of London Police, which is developing a new national fraud and cybercrime reporting and analytics service, and by embedding TPR experts within critical agencies to strengthen coordination, speed up investigations, and enhance the UK’s overall pension scam prevention framework.

Fujitsu has begun developing a new generative AI–powered chatbot for the Japan Pension Service, set to launch in April 2026, to enhance user experience, response quality, and operational efficiency in pension-related consultations. The upgraded chatbot will use Fujitsu’s Uvance generative AI to automatically draft Q&A responses when pension system updates occur, significantly reducing staff workload while maintaining human review for accuracy. It will also introduce multilingual support in six additional languages alongside Japanese, expand digital consultation channels, and enable more pension procedures to be completed online, building on the success of the existing chatbot that already serves around 600,000 users annually.

The UK government has launched an AI Crime Prevention Challenge to develop a nationwide, real-time interactive crime map across England and Wales that can predict where crimes such as knife crime, theft, anti-social behaviour and violent offences are most likely to occur, enabling police to intervene before harm happens. Backed by an initial £4 million investment and delivered through UK Research and Innovation, the project will combine data from police, councils and social services to identify crime concentrations and early warning signs, with prototypes due by April 2026 and full deployment targeted for 2030. The initiative supports the government’s Safer Streets Mission and Plan for Change, aiming to halve knife crime and violence against women and girls within a decade by using AI-driven intelligence to improve prevention, resource allocation and community safety.

Maharashtra police are expanding use of an AI-powered platform called MahaCrimeOS across all 1,100 police stations in the state to tackle rising cybercrime and support victims more efficiently. The system, initially piloted in Nagpur district, uses Microsoft Foundry-based AI to automate tasks such as complaint processing, data extraction, and investigation workflows, significantly speeding up cases that previously took months. It can process diverse digital evidence — including scam details, social media data, and screenshots across multiple languages — dramatically improving investigation capacity, freeing officers from manual work, and enhancing overall cybercrime response and citizen support.

The UK government has announced plans to expand the use of facial recognition technology across police forces to help identify and apprehend criminals, while proposing the creation of a new oversight body to regulate its use and ensure public confidence. The technology, already used by London’s Metropolitan Police, has led to around 1,300 arrests in the past two years and helped track offenders who breached licence conditions. While ministers describe facial recognition as the biggest policing breakthrough since DNA matching, civil liberties groups have raised strong concerns, warning that widespread deployment threatens privacy and risks mass surveillance. In response, the government said it will launch a 10-week consultation to assess safeguards, privacy protections and governance arrangements for the technology’s expanded use.

Tyler Technologies has strengthened its justice and public safety technology portfolio by acquiring CloudGavel, a Louisiana-based company specializing in electronic warrant software. The acquisition adds capabilities such as anytime, anywhere e-warrant submissions, rapid on-scene approvals, real-time warrant status updates, improved tracking for officer safety, and reduced courthouse visits and manual data entry. CloudGavel, which has partnered with Tyler since 2023, will now operate within Tyler’s Courts and Justice Division, reflecting Tyler’s continued strategic focus on justice systems and public safety as key drivers of growth in government technology.

Lawmakers reviewing the amended draft Law on Technology Transfer stressed the importance of stronger oversight, transparency, and post-implementation review mechanisms to prevent misuse in technology valuation and transfer. While supporting provisions that allow technology to be used as capital contributions and grant ownership rights to organisations creating innovations, deputies warned that allowing parties to freely determine technology value could lead to inflated valuations, virtual capital, or transfer pricing abuses. They called for clearer regulations, independent valuation for high-value transactions, accountability for fraudulent assessments, and streamlined “one-stop” digital processes linking technology transfer, investment, and intellectual property laws. Legislators also highlighted the need to regulate emerging technologies such as AI, semiconductors, and big data, protect national interests, and strengthen IP frameworks to ensure innovation is effectively commercialised while safeguarding strategic technologies.

The UK government has introduced the Cyber Security and Resilience (Network and Information Systems) Bill to strengthen national cyber defences and better protect essential public and digital services from cyber attacks by criminals and hostile states. First presented to Parliament in November 2025, the Bill updates and expands the existing NIS Regulations 2018, aiming to improve the security and resilience of critical services such as energy, water, healthcare and digital infrastructure. The legislation is intended to enhance national security, reduce economic disruption caused by cyber incidents, lower business costs, and support long-term economic growth and investment, underpinned by extensive research, impact assessments and alignment with the UK’s broader cyber resilience strategy.

The European Innovation Council (EIC) is inviting public administrations to take advantage of final opportunities under two major innovation procurement initiatives, SPIN4EIC and InnoMatch, designed to strengthen innovation-driven public purchasing. SPIN4EIC offers public buyers free, tailored expert support—coordinated by ICLEI and partners—to design and implement innovation-oriented procurement through modular assistance covering needs analysis, business cases, market consultation and tender drafting. In parallel, InnoMatch connects public and private buyers with EIC-funded start-ups to co-develop and pilot cutting-edge solutions, providing up to €60,000 in funding per project and dedicated matchmaking support. Together, these programmes enable public buyers to experiment with innovative solutions in a low-risk, well-supported environment.

Copenhagen has set ambitious goals for sustainable and healthy food procurement through its SchoolFood4Change initiative, ensuring that food served in municipal institutions supports both public health and climate objectives. Procurement tenders require compliance with Danish Dietary Guidelines while rewarding suppliers for offering a wide variety of healthy products, using green delivery vehicles, and employing people distant from the labour market. This approach has driven suppliers toward greener and more innovative practices, reduced food waste, and strengthened sustainable supply chains. As part of its climate strategy, Copenhagen has removed red meat from school meals and secured 100% organic, high-quality food, including more than 150 varieties of seasonal fruits and vegetables, benefiting school children and the wider community.

Pakistan’s Federal Board of Revenue (FBR) has launched a generative AI-powered chatbot on its official website to provide 24/7 taxpayer assistance on general tax-related queries. This marks the first public-facing AI service by any government agency in Pakistan. Currently available in beta mode, the chatbot can generate tailored responses, handle both basic and technical questions, and is expected to gradually reduce reliance on manual call centres. The initiative is part of the FBR Transformation Plan approved by the prime minister and federal cabinet, aiming to modernise taxpayer services and expand AI use across government. FBR has clarified that the chatbot provides general information only, does not constitute legal advice, and carries no legal liability.

The Australian Taxation Office (ATO) is trialling large multimodal AI models to audit taxpayer-submitted documents, including images, as part of its long-term strategy to “industrialise” ethical, scalable AI across the agency by 2030. Building on five years of AI use for reading and classifying text-based documents, the new approach expands document understanding beyond plain text to improve audit efficiency for work-related expense claims. The system operates with strong human oversight through an “enterprise learning loop,” where case officers validate outputs and provide continuous feedback to improve accuracy. AI is also used earlier in the process to flag abnormal or high-risk claims and issue proactive nudges to taxpayers. These tools support several high-value enterprise use cases, including client risk profiling, fraud disruption, and legal analysis, with the ATO deliberately focusing on business value rather than specific AI technologies to remain adaptable in a rapidly evolving AI landscape.

The European Commission has proposed a legislative amendment to strengthen cooperation between Eurofisc, the European Public Prosecutor’s Office (EPPO), and the European Anti-Fraud Office (OLAF) to better combat cross-border VAT fraud, particularly large-scale MTIC and carousel schemes that cause annual losses estimated between €12.5 billion and €32.8 billion. The proposal creates a clear legal basis for direct, centralized, and EU-wide access to VAT data and real-time information exchange, addressing current fragmented, bilateral approaches that hinder effective investigation of complex multi-jurisdictional fraud. Recent major cases, including EPPO investigations uncovering billions in losses, demonstrate that faster, coordinated access to VAT information is essential to close enforcement gaps, reduce financial damage to EU budgets, and ensure fair competition, with the proposal now submitted to the European Parliament and Council for adoption.

The General Department of Taxation under the Ministry of Finance has launched a new Taxpayer Support Portal as part of its administrative reform and digital transformation agenda, aligned with Resolution 68-NQ/TW, to provide individuals, household businesses, and enterprises with clear, fast, and practical access to tax policies and procedures. The portal offers regularly updated, step-by-step guidance on registration, tax declaration, payment, accounting, and the transition of household businesses into enterprises, while also integrating an AI-powered advisory chatbot to support entrepreneurs in management, finance, and operations. The initiative reflects a shift toward a taxpayer-centric service model and is supported by a strategic partnership with MISA JSC, which will deliver technical development, digital learning content, and system maintenance to enhance compliance, reduce costs, and improve the overall taxpayer experience.
NSW announced it will share tender and procurement data with the ACCC and use AI to detect suspicious patterns
India’s CAG (national auditor) publicly emphasized using AI and digital tools to strengthen audits and detect fraud in government schemes/spending.
Announced plan to integrate an AI assistant into the National Digital Investment Platform, alongside digitization/CRM enhancements for investor servicing.
Invest Hong Kong highlighted adoption/use of AI technology in investment promotion

The UK has become one of the first countries to formally recognise cryptocurrencies and certain digital assets as personal property after the Property (Digital Assets etc) Act received Royal Assent in December 2025. The new law clarifies that assets such as crypto tokens and NFTs can be treated like traditional property, strengthening legal protections against theft and fraud, enabling inheritance and recovery in bankruptcy, and reducing uncertainty in disputes. This reform supports victims of digital crime, provides certainty for businesses and fintech firms, and reinforces the UK’s position as a global leader in legal innovation and fintech, contributing to growth in the £42.6 billion legal services sector.

Nagpur Police has launched “AI Nirikshak,” Maharashtra’s first AI-based crowd management pilot, deployed during the 2025 Winter Assembly Session to enhance public safety amid risks of stampedes and security threats. Developed in partnership with a local tech firm and Microsoft, the system uses Azure cloud services, computer vision, and real-time analytics from CCTV cameras, drones, mobile vans, and road sensors. It enables live crowd density monitoring, predictive surge alerts, facial recognition against watchlists, detection of suspicious behavior and objects, and restricted-zone violations. A built-in Police AI Agent chatbot supports instant searches across FIRs, incidents, and vehicle data, enabling faster decision-making. Designed with low-latency alerts, privacy safeguards, and scalability, AI Nirikshak aims to prevent overcrowding, optimize police deployment, protect VIP routes, and serve as a model for statewide and national adoption.

The U.S. Transportation Security Administration (TSA) will introduce Confirm.ID from February 1, 2026, a technology-enabled identity verification option for air travelers who arrive at airport checkpoints without an acceptable ID, including non-REAL ID licenses. Passengers will be required to either present a REAL ID–compliant credential or pay a fee to verify their identity using biographic and/or biometric data, which is checked against TSA watchlists. The service is intended as a last-resort option, may cause delays, and shifts verification costs from taxpayers to users, while TSA continues urging travelers to obtain REAL ID in advance.

The Copenhagen has set ambitious goals for sustainable food procurement through its SchoolFood4Change team, using public purchasing to promote healthy diets, reduce food waste, and support climate objectives across municipal kitchens. Procurement tenders require compliance with Danish Dietary Guidelines while incentivizing suppliers through scoring systems that reward delivery of diverse healthy food groups, use of green delivery vehicles, and social inclusion of people distant from the labour market. Aligned with SchoolFood4Change, the city has eliminated red meat from school meals, serves 100% organic food, and secured over 150 varieties of seasonal fruits and vegetables, demonstrating how innovative procurement can simultaneously improve child health and build more sustainable food systems, with further details shared via Procura+.

Public administrations are invited to make a final call to join innovation procurement opportunities under the European Innovation Council (EIC) through two flagship projects, SPIN4EIC and InnoMatch, with coordinated support from ICLEI and expert partners. SPIN4EIC offers public buyers free, tailored assistance to design and implement innovation-oriented procurement across four modular stages, providing up to 20 days of expert input, while InnoMatch connects public or private buyers with EIC-funded start-ups to co-develop and pilot innovative solutions over 12 months, supported by matchmaking services and up to €60,000 in funding per selected project. Together, these initiatives enable public buyers to test and adopt innovative solutions with reduced risk, expert guidance, and strong alignment with EU innovation ecosystems.

The UK Ministry of Justice has launched a Counter-Drone Innovation Challenge through His Majesty’s Government Communications Centre (HMGCC) Co-Creation to address the rapidly escalating use of drones to smuggle contraband into prisons, with incidents rising by more than 770% between 2019 and 2023. The challenge invites industry to develop legally compliant, easy-to-use solutions capable of detecting advanced criminal drones that evade existing systems, offering £60,000 to successful applicants to build proof-of-concepts over 12 weeks. The initiative complements a wider £40 million government investment in prison security, including £10 million for anti-drone measures, and reflects the government’s strategy—highlighted by Lord Timpson—to harness innovation to protect staff, disrupt organised crime, and support rehabilitation.

the strategy focuses on building “smart prisons” through two main initiatives: a technology-driven security network using cloud-based surveillance, facial recognition, and electric perimeter fencing to enhance monitoring and reduce patrol burdens, and digital systems that streamline staff workflows and inmate services, such as kiosk-style purchasing systems for prisoners. Together, these measures aim to improve resource allocation, boost staff efficiency, and modernize correctional management amid sustained operational pressures.

A Marshall Project report examines the growing interest in using AI and robotics in U.S. prisons to address chronic staffing shortages, highlighting how ideas inspired by technologies like Tesla’s Optimus robot—showcased by Elon Musk—are being considered for correctional tasks such as medicine distribution, searches, and other hazardous or routine work. Delinia Lewis of the California Institution for Women argues AI could allow staff to focus on higher-value duties, though budget constraints may delay adoption. While robots remain a long-term prospect, prisons have rapidly adopted AI tools like call-monitoring software from companies such as LeoTech, using cloud services from Amazon, and increasingly standard offerings by Securus and Global Tel Link. Critics, including the Electronic Frontier Foundation, warn these technologies raise serious concerns around privacy, bias, opaque data practices, and breaches of attorney-client privilege, even as states continue to expand their use.

The Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN) of the U.S. Department of the Treasury has launched a first-of-its-kind, data-driven enforcement operation targeting more than 100 money services businesses operating along the U.S. southwest border to address potential money laundering and illicit finance risks. Enabled by Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent’s technology-modernization push, the operation analyzed over one million Currency Transaction Reports and 87,000 Suspicious Activity Reports, resulting in six notices of investigation, dozens of referrals to the Internal Revenue Service (IRS), and more than 50 compliance outreach letters. FinCEN is coordinating with federal and state partners to pursue penalties, examinations, and criminal referrals where warranted, underscoring that failures to comply with AML obligations threaten national security and that advanced analytics are now central to protecting the U.S. financial system.

The International Rescue Committee (IRC) and Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE) have launched AntiTraffickingResponse.org, an AI-powered platform designed to support first-line responders and survivors in combating human trafficking, one of the world’s fastest-growing crimes affecting up to 50 million people globally. The platform centralizes multilingual training and resources and features two AI-driven chatbots—one to help practitioners identify and respond to trafficking cases, and another to provide survivors with trauma-informed guidance toward safe employment and recovery—addressing rising global trafficking trends and offering a secure, anonymous, and accessible pathway to protection, economic empowerment, and long-term resilience.

Singapore’s Gambling Regulatory Authority (GRA) is strengthening its data-driven oversight by working with licensed casinos to collect and analyse data on new bet types, including baccarat side bets enabled by smart gaming tables, to assess whether strategies to channel illegal gambling into regulated markets are effective. According to Chairman Tan Hee Tow, the regulator is enhancing analytics and visualization tools, exploring generative AI under its Digitalisation Masterplan 2.0, and using AI to detect regulatory anomalies and at-risk behaviour—while stressing that human judgement remains essential. The approach coincides with a 5% decline in local casino visitation in 2024 (about 94,000 adults; 2.8% of the adult population) and fewer entry levies purchased, while problem gambling rates stayed low at 1.1%, reflecting coordinated harm-mitigation efforts. The GRA says it will continue to recalibrate its framework with technology and data to keep regulation relevant, effective, and aligned with global standards.

The Valero Alamo Bowl has introduced optional facial biometric entry for fans at the Alamodome in San Antonio, using technology from Wicket, to deliver faster and more seamless stadium access. Through Wicket’s QuickLane Entry system, registered fans aged 18 and over can link their ticketing accounts and enter the venue simply by walking through dedicated lanes for facial authentication, eliminating the need to scan physical tickets. Organizers say the deployment enhances fan experience while maintaining strong security and privacy standards, reflecting a broader trend of biometric access control adoption across major sports venues in the U.S. and internationally.

The UK Home Office has launched the Deepfake Detection Challenge 2026 to address the growing misuse of generative AI, which the government has identified as an urgent national priority due to its links to disinformation, financial crime, and policing risks. Delivered in collaboration with the Alan Turing Institute, the Department for Science, Innovation and Technology (DSIT), and the government’s Accelerated Capability Environment, the challenge will use large-scale biometric datasets, benchmarking tests, and a live scenario-based hack event in January 2026 to accelerate practical deepfake detection solutions. Building on the 2024 challenge, which produced promising prototypes from industry and academia, the initiative emphasizes real-world training data and cross-sector collaboration as critical to strengthening the UK’s defenses against deepfake threats.

The UK government has announced urgent measures to curb mistaken prisoner releases and restore public confidence, with the Ministry of Justice, HM Prison and Probation Service, and Deputy Prime Minister David Lammy committing up to £10 million over six months to deploy AI-powered tools, modernize paper-based systems, and support frontline staff in accurately calculating sentences. The package includes a fast-track courts hotline, a new monthly Justice Performance Board, expanded independent review led by Dame Lynne Owen, and dedicated data scientists to analyse all historic release errors, following figures showing 91 mistaken releases between April and October 2025. Together, these actions aim to tighten safeguards, improve data transparency, and stabilize a prison system under severe strain while longer-term capacity and sentencing reforms are implemented.

Spotlight, a nonprofit partner of the National Center for Missing & Exploited Children (NCMEC), uses advanced technology to rapidly compare online escort ads with missing-children data to generate actionable leads for law enforcement, often enabling child recovery within 24 hours.
