Since its prototype debut during the 2015 Super Bowl, Spotlight has evolved into a free, donor-supported tool used across the U.S. and Canada, producing 541 positive matches in a single year and helping identify more than 26,000 trafficked children over the past decade by reducing identification time from months to minutes—particularly for victims not previously suspected of being trafficked.

Traffik Analysis Hub (TA Hub) is a UK-registered, not-for-profit collaborative platform that brings together governments, financial institutions, businesses, NGOs, law enforcement agencies, and academia to combat human trafficking by creating a single, trusted global intelligence source. Powered by a secure, AI-enabled technology suite developed by IBM, TA Hub enables authenticated partners to share non-personal data, jointly analyse large datasets, and identify trafficking patterns, networks, financial flows, and hotspots, addressing the fragmented global response to a crime that generates an estimated US$498 billion annually in illicit proceeds. Through collaborative data pooling and advanced analytics, TA Hub aims to disrupt trafficking and associated money laundering more effectively than isolated efforts, delivering actionable insights with real operational impact.

Data-driven intelligence combined with innovative technology has become a powerful tool in preventing human trafficking, as demonstrated by Love Justice’s transit monitoring work across regions such as South Asia and Africa. By systematically collecting data from victim and trafficker interviews, police reports, investigations, and informants, and applying machine learning to weight region-specific “red flags,” trained monitors can identify high-risk situations in real time and intervene before exploitation occurs. These data-informed approaches enable responders to recognize vastly different trafficking patterns—such as romantic deception of young women in South Asia or labor exploitation of boys in Africa—while also generating insights into broader trends and networks that can be shared globally to strengthen collective anti-trafficking efforts.

The Inter‑Agency Coordination Group Against Trafficking in Persons (ICAT) issue brief Human Trafficking and Technology: Trends, Challenges and Opportunities explains how rapid technological development has both fuelled and helped combat human trafficking. It highlights that traffickers increasingly misuse digital tools at all stages of the crime—recruiting through fake social media profiles, using encrypted communications and dark-web services to hide identities, and moving illicit profits via cryptocurrencies—making exploitation more sophisticated and harder to detect. At the same time, technology offers opportunities to strengthen anti-trafficking efforts by aiding investigations, improving prosecutions, raising awareness, providing victim services, and revealing the structure and operations of trafficking networks. The brief stresses that future success in eradicating human trafficking depends on how well countries and stakeholders harness technology ethically and effectively in their responses.

Italy has introduced an AI-powered chatbot, developed by Agenzia delle Entrate with Sogei and the Ministry of Economy and Finance, to work alongside the VeRa fraud-detection system to identify VAT fraud in real time by scanning VAT returns and transactions and flagging anomalies such as mismatched invoices, undeclared income, inconsistent financial activity, and other suspicious patterns for rapid review by tax officers. The chatbot complements VeRa’s broader data cross-checking across e-invoicing, banking, customs, and property sources—reported to have identified over one million suspect filings in 2022—while emphasizing that effective enforcement depends on high-quality, consistent taxpayer data, since poor master data can cause false alerts and unnecessary audits; as a result, businesses are encouraged to strengthen data governance through accurate identifiers, proper classifications, centralized master data, real-time validation, and clear ownership of tax records.

Ghana’s Ministry of Finance plans to launch a National VAT “Reward Scheme” next year to boost compliance by entering receipts collected by tax-compliant citizens into nationwide prize draws, encouraging more people to demand VAT receipts and thereby reducing leakages in the VAT chain and improving revenue performance. Announced after Finance Minister Dr Cassiel Ato Forson met the Large Taxpayer Office team in Accra, the scheme is part of a broader package of tax administration reforms due to start next year, including a redesigned VAT system and the rollout of fiscal electronic devices to strengthen compliance, transparency, and data accuracy, supporting the government’s agenda of “Resetting for Growth, Jobs, and Economic Transformation.”

From 1 January 2026, Italy introduces mandatory electronic storage and fiscal reporting for all EV charging transactions, requiring charging station operators and e-mobility service providers to record every charging session and prepare data for transmission to the Agenzia delle Entrate.

IRS is rolling out Salesforce’s AI agent program, Agentforce, across several divisions (including the Office of Chief Counsel, Taxpayer Advocate Service, and Office of Appeals) to help with tasks like document search and case summarization as part of modernization after major staffing cuts, especially among revenue agents. While the AI is described as having guardrails and not making final decisions or paying out funds, it is expected to strengthen enforcement by rapidly matching and cross-checking data—particularly relevant for Americans abroad—by comparing FATCA-reported foreign account information against filings like FBAR (FinCEN 114) and Form 8938, and spotting inconsistencies across common expat forms such as Form 2555 (FEIE), Form 1116 (FTC), and complex foreign business reporting like Form 5471. The main message is that accurate, complete filings should simply process faster, but omissions, mismatches, and unreported foreign accounts/assets will be easier to detect, so taxpayers with gaps are urged to correct them proactively using available IRS compliance pathways; AI doesn’t change tax obligations, it improves verification.

New York City’s Smart City Testbed Program (launched in 2023 by the NYC Office of Technology and Innovation) is rolling out new pilots focused on street and infrastructure safety, including a project that uses sensors and anonymized Wi-Fi-based signals to better measure pedestrian activity across six public spaces, and another that uses augmented reality plus a community engagement platform to let residents scan a QR code and view a 3D, perspective-aware rendering of a planned recreation building in Queens before construction begins. The program functions as an early-stage experimentation “incubator” rather than a procurement channel, supported by public engagement sessions at local libraries and continued vendor participation, building on earlier pilots such as AI-assisted facility condition reports and lidar-based traffic analysis. In parallel, NYC is deploying a “first-of-its-kind” Emergency Communications Vehicle (ECV-1) for the Thanksgiving Day Parade, designed to act as a mobile command post for police and firefighters by extending network connectivity and replicating citywide radio communications with interoperability for state and federal partners, helping maintain communications and dispatch capability during disruptions.

Ubicquia, a Florida-based “intelligent streetlighting” provider, says it has expanded its streetlight technology ecosystem by launching UbiScout, an AI video accessory that pairs with its streetlight controllers to generate insights on pedestrians, vehicle traffic, road conditions and related activity, alongside a new UbiCell Micro universal controller designed to meet strict utility requirements for metering, surge protection, power quality and physical stability. The company also upgraded its UbiVu management platform—used by 1,000+ clients—adding native integration with third-party sensors, work order and inventory management, and a redesigned outage-reporting interface, supporting broader use of streetlights for smart infrastructure functions like traffic analytics and adaptive lighting. As adoption grows, Ubicquia notes public-sector use cases beyond lighting (such as connectivity projects) and highlights deployments supporting law enforcement surveillance networks, including in San Diego.

Ascensus and CalSavers (California’s state-sponsored auto-IRA program) launched CalSavvy on Sept. 16, 2025, describing it as the first AI-powered chatbot built specifically for state auto-IRA programs to support more than 600,000 employers required to register with CalSavers or offer a qualified plan by the end of 2025. The bilingual (English/Spanish) tool provides 24/7 answers on account setup, contributions, investment options, and retirement planning, drawing initially from the CalSavers public website and the California State Treasurer’s Office site, and is intended to complement existing supports like webinars, videos, and guides while reducing wait times and improving onboarding. CalSavers leadership and the State Treasurer emphasized its role in widening retirement access and closing the savings gap, and Ascensus noted future upgrades for more personalized support and additional languages, alongside its broader role administering major auto-IRA programs including CalSavers and Illinois Secure Choice.

The Government of Delhi is preparing to roll out DARPAN 2.0, an advanced, real-time digital governance dashboard developed by the National Informatics Centre (NIC) under India’s Ministry of Electronics and IT, designed to improve transparency, accountability, and decision-making by providing policymakers and government departments with a unified, data-driven view of key government schemes, services and performance indicators. The platform integrates data from multiple departmental management systems into one interface, enabling live tracking of progress, comparative analytics, early-warning alerts and KPI-based scorecards to identify bottlenecks and accelerate corrective action, with phased roll-out expected over the coming weeks and future upgrades planned for predictive analytics, AI insights and public-facing dashboards.

CONSIP, Italy’s national central purchasing body, has launched a pilot to incorporate gender pay equality scoring into competitive tendering, aligning with EU rules that require pay-gap reporting for employers with over 100 staff and allow exclusion of firms with unjustified gaps above 5%. CONSIP’s method assesses bidders using a weighted combination of the gender pay gap plus indicators for women’s overall representation and their share of management roles to enable fair comparisons across companies; it was tested in a €9 million consulting services tender involving 20 offers from 22 firms, where all bidders ultimately submitted the required data and results showed wide variation, while CONSIP itself scored near full equality. Presented during a BBWT Community of Practice study visit on Social Procurement, the pilot sits within CONSIP’s broader Socially Responsible Public Procurement agenda, with next steps focused on analyzing results, testing feasibility across markets, extending criteria to other procedures, and embedding gender equality scoring within a wider sustainability framework, while strengthening transparency, risk management, and market co-design to better measure social value beyond cost savings.

New York State Police (NYSP) is building a dedicated technology team as part of New York’s Office of Information Technology Services (ITS) push to better tailor tech support to each agency’s mission, with the unit led by Deputy Commissioner for Technology Mike Harrigan (an ITS staff member embedded in NYSP) and focused on mission-critical public safety systems and NYSP-specific operational needs. The approach keeps statewide shared services—such as information security, AI, and broader technology offices—while adding an agency-aligned team whose responsibilities will evolve as hiring continues and priorities are set jointly with NYSP leadership. Early work already underway includes modernizing the NYSP trooper entrance exam application website, especially improving mobile usability and accessibility to support recruitment, reflecting a broader shift toward a hybrid model that combines centralized shared services with embedded, agency-focused expertise.

Susquehanna Kids is bringing a free “Hour of AI” workshop to schools across five Pennsylvania counties, offering 30 one-hour sessions that introduce students to age-appropriate, hands-on AI and coding fundamentals using lessons from trusted providers like LEGO Education, Google and Minecraft Education curated on Code.org. Supported by DegenSTEAM Academy (a new initiative of the Charles B. Degenstein Foundation) and a PA Smart grant, the program aims to ensure broad student exposure to what AI is (and isn’t), how it’s used in everyday life, and why creative problem-solving still drives innovation, while also showing educators that AI learning tools can be user-friendly. No devices are required because equipment is provided, and the sessions emphasize safe, responsible AI use; one example event at the Lewisburg YMCA drew 12 students, including kids already interested in coding and robotics.

Researchers at IIT Madras have developed and patented a redesigned continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) device that aims to make diabetes monitoring more comfortable, accessible and affordable while maintaining accuracy, addressing the invasiveness of finger-prick SMBG and the high cost and extra-device dependence of many current CGMs. Their solution uses a modular design combining a disposable microneedle sensor patch with reusable electronics and an ultra-low-power electro-thermochromic display that shows glucose readings directly on the patch, enabling immediate viewing without a smartphone or reader and extending battery life by using power mainly when updating. With India facing an estimated 101 million people living with diabetes (ICMR INDIAB 2023), prototypes have been bench-tested for stable, accurate sensing and protected by multiple Indian patents plus an international PCT filing; the team has launched a startup at the IIT-Madras Research Park to refine the product, run clinical trials and prepare for market entry, alongside plans to license the technology with established manufacturers to scale production, distribution and local economic benefits.

China has officially adopted a new Hazardous Chemicals Safety Law, effective 1 May 2026, significantly strengthening regulation across the full lifecycle of hazardous chemicals. The law introduces dynamic catalogue management based on intrinsic hazards, tighter workforce qualification and training requirements, mandatory public disclosure of safety assessment reports every three years, stricter Chinese-language SDS and labeling obligations, clarified registration exemptions for low-risk R&D use, clearer rules distinguishing hazardous chemicals from dangerous goods in transport, expanded digital supervision with electronic identification and lifecycle tracking, and comprehensive regulation of chemical industrial parks. It also encourages public reporting through rewards and imposes tougher penalties for non-compliance, signaling a shift toward more transparent, data-driven, and risk-based chemical safety governance.

In November 2025, the EU Joint Research Centre released new guidelines outlining practical methods to identify and track Substances of Concern (SoC) in products across their full lifecycle, directly supporting implementation of the Ecodesign for Sustainable Products Regulation (ESPR). The guidance expands substance information requirements to include intentionally added substances, recycled content, lifecycle stage, function, and even substances used during manufacturing or transport, enabling tools like the Digital Product Passport to share data across value chains. It also introduces performance-based criteria linking SoC to product sustainability aspects such as durability, recyclability, carbon footprint, and overall environmental impact, signaling a shift from purely chemical hazard control toward integrated lifecycle and environmental performance management, with Life Cycle Assessment (EF3.1) likely becoming standard practice for products placed on the EU market.

Uzbekistan has announced a tax-free zone in Karakalpakstan focused on AI and data center projects to attract large foreign investors. Under the plan, foreign companies investing $100 million+ can receive broad tax and duty exemptions until 2040, while the government commits to building key infrastructure and offering discounted electricity to qualifying projects. The initiative is framed as part of Uzbekistan’s wider push to position itself as an investment-friendly reform economy, with a stated goal to attract over $1 billion into AI and digital infrastructure by 2030, while also targeting development in one of its poorest regions, heavily impacted by the Aral Sea environmental crisis

The 2025 review shows Indian Railways shifting into a data-driven, technology-led system, where digital tools and early AI are central to safety, operations, passenger services, and station upgrades. It highlights wider rollout of the indigenous Kavach automatic train protection to prevent collisions and overspeeding, emerging AI-based alerts to support loco pilots, expanded digital platforms for passenger services, stronger station connectivity (Wi-Fi), and modernised “smart” stations—together aiming for safer, more efficient rail operations while strengthening domestic tech capability.
The Financial Advice Association Australia (FAAA) launched SafeID, a client identity verification tool to help financial advisers meet AML/CTF requirements.

South Korea has passed a new law imposing heavy punitive damages on media outlets and large online platforms for spreading false information, including deepfakes, prompting criticism from journalists, civil society and the United States. The law allows courts to award up to five times proven damages and enables regulators to levy fines of up to 1 billion won, aiming to curb disinformation after YouTube-driven falsehoods contributed to the 2024 martial law crisis. Critics warn the law’s vague definitions could encourage self-censorship, while the U.S. has expressed concern that it threatens free expression and technological cooperation, framing it as part of a broader global tension between combating disinformation and protecting online freedoms.

Seyond has signed a $2.6 million deal to deploy its lidar-based Simpl traffic detection technology across key traffic infrastructure locations in Sweden, via integration into Aventi Sweden’s (formerly Blinkfyrar) infrastructure portfolio. Using typically two sensors per intersection

Malaysia’s Online Safety Act 2025 (ONSA) has just come into force (effective Jan 2, 2026) and shifts responsibility for protecting children online from parents/users to digital platforms.

Core shift: Platforms must take proactive action to prevent and reduce child harm online, rather than relying mainly on user reports.

Scope: Licensed service providers under the Communications and Multimedia Act 1998 (including social media and messaging services) must manage and remove content linked to child sexual abuse material (CSAM), pornography, incest, and self-harm-related content.

Required measures: Platforms are expected to implement early prevention, ethical algorithm monitoring, rapid response protocols, and clear support pathways for users.

Cardiff has become the first UK local authority to introduce higher parking charges for larger vehicles, approving a parking permit surcharge for cars weighing over 2,400kg (to be lowered to 2,000kg for non-electric vehicles) in order to discourage the growing use of heavy SUVs. The policy responds to evidence that larger vehicles take up more space, increase road wear, produce more pollution, and pose greater safety risks—particularly to children—and follows public consultation in which 66% supported higher charges for bigger cars. City officials stress the measure is not a ban but a nudge toward smaller vehicles, aligning Cardiff with cities like Paris, where similar policies significantly reduced SUV parking.

Greece’s Independent Public Revenue Authority (AADE) is escalating its tax-evasion crackdown by adding three EU-supported digital tools (with support/partnership from the Swedish Tax Authority) to make audits more targeted and data-driven:

AI-powered case selection (pilot): ML models rank cases by probability of tax evasion, so auditors focus on the highest-risk files first.

Unified risk analysis methodology: A standardized, centralized approach that cross-checks data from Taxisnet, myDATA, banks, GEMI, EFKA and other sources to improve consistency and transparency, while keeping random sampling to maintain unpredictability.

E-commerce & crypto audit manual: A practical guide to standardize audits for digital platforms and crypto markets, closing gaps created by fast-growing online transactions.

AADE also emphasizes continuous monitoring using streams from myDATA, digital registers, shipping labels and e-invoicing to flag anomalies in near real time, and a centralized multi-criteria platform that blends predictive models (e.g., decision trees, neural networks) with traditional random checks to detect new “hotspots.”

the National Pension System (NPS) of the Republic of Korea installed KIOSKs equipped with AI agents in Customer Centre to provide general counselling and institutional promotion; provided the first real-time interpreter service in the Republic of Korea for foreigners using the National Pension Administration service so that they can use it conveniently without communication difficulties
Odisha Vigilance announced a dedicated AI cell to support anti-corruption efforts through analytics/pattern recognition.

California became the first U.S. state to require disclosure when police use generative AI to draft reports after Gov. Gavin Newsom signed SB 524 on Oct. 10, 2025. Starting Jan. 1, 2026, any AI-assisted report (e.g., using Axon’s Draft One) must carry a written disclosure on every page, and departments must preserve audit trails—including the original AI draft and the body-camera/audio sources used. Supporters say it addresses concerns about AI shaping legal narratives, while some law enforcement groups warn of added administrative burden; early adopters like Fresno PD say they already follow most of these practices, and Axon says it will comply.

Washington County Sheriff’s Office in Oregon is piloting Axon’s “Draft One,” an AI tool that transcribes bodycam footage and generates draft police reports to reduce paperwork time—report writing that used to take about 90 minutes can drop to roughly 15–20 minutes. Deputies must review and edit every draft, manually changing at least 20% to confirm accuracy, and the system intentionally includes small errors to keep officers actively checking the content. Officials stress that human judgement is still needed for interpreting context and emotions, data is stored securely within Axon’s network, and the agency will decide with the district attorney after the 60-day trial whether to adopt it permanently.

In Germany, the Federal Ministry for Economic Affairs and Energy is strengthening this ecosystem through a draft Regulatory Sandboxes Act adopted by the Federal Cabinet on May 19, 2025, new expectations to check draft laws for experimentation clauses from May 2025, and the Regulatory Sandboxes Innovation Portal launched in pilot on May 22, 2025 to provide advice, networking, knowledge transfer and a national map of sandboxes. The approach is supported by multi-ministry and federal-state coordination, links to EU frameworks (including the EU AI Act’s AI sandboxes), and international guidance such as the OECD’s 2025 toolkit, alongside resources like a handbook and data protection guide and a biennial innovation prize to showcase best practices.

Virginia will begin enforcing a new rule on January 1, 2026 that, by default, limits users under 16 to one hour per day per social media service unless a parent increases the limit through verifiable parental consent. Added to the Virginia Consumer Data Protection Act (VCDPA), the law requires platforms to use commercially reasonable age-determination methods (including neutral age screens and certain device “minor” signals), restrict use of age-check data to age-related purposes, and bars platforms from degrading service or raising prices because a minor can’t exceed the cap. The statute defines covered “social media platforms” with profiles, social connection lists, and user-generated feeds, while carving out email/direct messaging, primarily news/entertainment/ecommerce sites with incidental interaction, and many gaming platforms. Enforcement is by the Virginia Attorney General with a 30-day cure period and penalties up to $7,500 per violation, but the law is already being challenged in court by NetChoice on First Amendment and privacy grounds, leaving major uncertainty about how (or whether) it will operate in early 2026.

Copenhagen’s SchoolFood4Change team is using public food procurement to advance healthier diets and climate goals across municipal kitchens, requiring compliance with Danish Dietary Guidelines while targeting lower food waste and more sustainable supply chains. Tenders reward suppliers with points for offering a wider range of healthy product groups, using greener delivery vehicles, and supporting social inclusion by hiring people who are farther from the labor market—creating incentives for greener, more innovative supply. As part of its emissions-reduction agenda, schools have moved away from serving red meat and instead provide high-quality, 100% organic meals, supported by contracts that secured over 150 varieties of seasonal fruits and vegetables to expand choice and reduce climate impact.

The article highlights how airports and border authorities in Africa and Asia are accelerating digital border control using passenger data, biometrics, and digital ID to handle rising travel volumes. Angola has deployed SITA’s API/PNR Gateway at Luanda’s Dr. António Agostinho Neto International Airport, backed by a new monitoring center and data center to analyze travel data in real time, flag suspicious patterns, and block unauthorized passengers before departure in line with UN/ICAO/EU requirements. In India, SITA is discussing AI-driven biometric baggage identification that links bags to bookings to reduce mishandling even when tags fail, building on Digi Yatra’s large-scale biometric adoption and broader plans for interoperability. The piece also surveys regional rollouts: the Philippines’ NAIA is activating Amadeus facial-biometric e-gates to cut queues, Malaysia’s KLIA is using QR-based Datasonic autogates to slash wait times, and Vietnam is expanding biometric and digital-ID flows via VNeID, adding automated border control, self-service check-in, and biometric gates to move passengers from minutes to seconds while keeping hybrid/manual options.

Linxens introduced “Hint,” a new inlay-embedded security feature for electronic ID documents that detects chip-tampering attempts involving magnetic, electrical, or physical interference. Unveiled at Trustech 2025 in Paris, Hint is meant to address a common fraud tactic where criminals deliberately damage or disable a document’s chip to bypass electronic verification. Linxens says the feature gives border and law-enforcement officers an immediate signal that a chip has been manipulated, improving the speed and reliability of checks at airports and border crossings, and it can be integrated into e-passports, national ID cards, residence permits, and driver’s licences.

The Rockefeller Foundation and the Center for Civic Futures (CCF) launched the AI Readiness Project to help U.S. states, territories and tribal governments build capacity to use AI responsibly through convenings, knowledge sharing and pilot programs. The initiative will expand CCF’s nonpartisan State Chief AI Officer Community of Practice—which already connects AI and tech leaders from 30+ states—with a goal of reaching all 50 states plus territories and tribal nations by 2026. It will offer workshops and working groups, provide low-risk environments to test AI and evaluate outcomes, and support at least 10 new state-level public-sector AI pilots, with results feeding into shared frameworks, policy templates and model practices. A State AI Knowledge Hub is planned for 2026 to publish lessons learned, case studies and tools, and current monthly groups focus on agentic AI guardrails, AI workforce policy, and AI evaluation/monitoring to strengthen accountability.

The article highlights Tianjin Port’s Second Container Terminal, described as the world’s first smart zero-carbon terminal, where blue AI-powered automated transport robots (ART) operate to move containers around the site. Developed by Tianjin Port Group, ART is presented as a fully autonomous container-transport system that boosts terminal efficiency and supports greener port operations, with a video explaining its advantages and overall benefits to port performance.

In Xiong’an New Area near Beijing, a five-story cultural center called Xiong’an Wings is being built with giant 3D printers as one of the world’s largest 3D-printed buildings, combining a dramatic swan-like design with eco-focused construction. Engineers used precision 3D-printed panels made from modified plastic to create its complex double-curved “wings,” a method that can cut material use by 20–30%, avoid polluting molds, and reduce waste at the source, while tests suggest the panels retain 80%+ performance after 20 years outdoors. The project also uses a fully digital workflow (BIM across the lifecycle), drone laser scanning to detect even 5 cm deviations for rapid correction, topology optimization to reduce unnecessary steel, and smart insulation/management systems expected to lower annual energy consumption by 30%+. Developed by Power Construction Corporation of China and a Tongji University-led team, the project is being used to create Xiong’an’s first local technical standards for 3D-printing construction, positioning it as a replicable model for smarter, greener city-building.

The Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar police range in Maharashtra has established dedicated war rooms in all four of its districts — Sambhajinagar Rural, Beed, Jalna and Dharashiv — as part of a major technological upgrade to improve crime monitoring and law enforcement coordination. Led by Range IGP Virendra Mishra, these facilities serve as central hubs for real-time data and analytics on crime, enabling swift decision-making across 21 sub-divisional offices and 91 police stations. Equipped with interactive displays, AI video tools, crime maps and analytical software, the war rooms have already helped solve 75 offences, including murder, robberies, house break-ins and thefts, and recover stolen property worth over ₹61 lakh. Officials say the initiative marks a shift toward faster, analytics-driven policing and is expected to continue evolving in scale and capability.

Malaysia is strengthening its position as a leading smart green and clean-tech investment hub in Southeast Asia, driven by strong 2025 momentum from its flagship green technology exhibition, which generated proposed investments of RM7.3 billion (US$1.6 billion). Led by the Malaysian Investment Development Authority (MIDA), the country is advancing an integrated policy and facilitation approach aligned with the MADANI Economy Framework, New Industrial Master Plan 2030, National Energy Transition Roadmap, and Green Investment Strategy. Key initiatives include structured business matching through the Biz Bridge platform, enhanced green financing partnerships, attractive tax incentives for sustainable technologies, and end-to-end investor facilitation, collectively reinforcing investor confidence and positioning Malaysia as a regional hub where industrial growth, clean energy deployment, and sustainability objectives converge.

The Karnataka government has introduced a new Single Window System to streamline investment procedures and improve business efficiency. This digital platform integrates over 150 services from 30+ state departments, simplifying approvals and enhancing transparency, making Karnataka an attractive investment destination.

Indonesia’s Ministry of Communication and Digital Affairs (Kemkomdigi) will roll out phased biometric SIM registration in 2026 to strengthen digital security, after pilots since 2024 and expanded trials in 2025. The plan starts at mobile-operator outlets to support users and public awareness, with a six-month transition period after a new regulation where people can still register via NIK + Family Card (SMS 4444/web) or choose biometric registration. The policy begins Jan 1, 2026 as a voluntary “hybrid” option for new customers (NIK or face biometrics), then becomes mandatory for all new users from July 1, 2026, aiming to reduce scams that rely on phone numbers (e.g., spoofing, smishing), address reported losses exceeding Rp7 trillion, and help clean up inactive numbers in a market with 310+ million circulating phone numbers versus ~220 million adults; it also updates the older 2021 rules that were more vulnerable to misuse.

Taixing city in Jiangsu, China is using advanced 3D geological radar to run “physical examinations” on urban roads to reduce the risk of collapses. A radar detection vehicle scans beneath the road surface by sending high-frequency electromagnetic waves to “see” underground structures and identify hazards such as cavities, voids, looseness, or detachment. When defects are found, the system records their exact location, size, and depth to support targeted maintenance plans, and technicians say the results will be compiled into a detailed report to guide repairs. So far this year, Taixing has inspected about 18 km of vehicle lanes, non-motor lanes, and sidewalks using this void-detection technology.

A year after Brazil’s regulated online betting market opened on Jan. 1, 2025, the country is being positioned as a regional model for combining legalization with stronger KYC—especially mandatory selfie-based biometric verification for online betting/casino (and referenced crypto) platforms—while acknowledging major gaps in enforcement. Operators say early user “friction” eased within the first months as people understood verification and processes became faster, but inconsistent interpretation of rules still affects standardization. The biggest challenge remains the illegal market, estimated at 41–51% of online gambling, despite actions like 18,000+ illegal site IP blocks in 2025; industry voices argue that cracking down on payments (via PSPs) is essential, and warn growing risks like deepfakes. The market is also expected to consolidate toward fewer large operators, while Brazil’s data protection authority (ANPD) is preparing for expanded age-assurance/online safety responsibilities under the Digital ECA taking effect March 17, 2026, as other jurisdictions like Buenos Aires move to require face biometrics for online gambling to curb underage access.

The article argues that broad property-tax cuts are politically popular but often regressive and can worsen inequities over time, citing how parcel-specific limits like California’s Proposition 13 shift tax burdens to new homeowners and create large disparities between similar properties. Instead, it proposes targeted tax relief to ease the housing “logjam” for two groups: younger first-time buyers and older homeowners who want to sell and downsize but are deterred by capital gains taxes. For first-time buyers, it suggests time-limited property-tax exemptions on a primary residence (with income/asset limits), an additional federal mortgage-interest deduction even for non-itemizers, and incentives for builders to produce more starter homes (tax credits and construction-period property-tax rebates credited to buyers). For older owners, it recommends a temporary, once-in-a-lifetime higher capital gains exclusion (up to $1M or a benchmark tied to state medians) and simpler assessment-transfer options to encourage downsizing, while noting states must offset local revenue losses and that permitting reforms are still essential to increase housing supply.

New guidance on advance tax certainty service
HMRC has published draft guidance for the new advance tax certainty service to be launched in July 2026. The service will be open to businesses undertaking major investment projects and is intended to provide “certainty on complex tax issues”. The draft guidance is based on legislation included in Finance Bill 2025-26 (cl263-271) and will be finalised ahead of the formal launch of the service in July 2026.

Alaska is considering adding agentic AI modules to the myAlaska app/portal so the system can autonomously complete multi-step government transactions for residents (not just chat or answer questions). The state issued an RFI on Nov. 25, 2025 to gather industry input on feasibility, cost, timeline, and implementation. Proposed capabilities include dynamic form filling, document retrieval, eligibility checks, and personalized notifications. The state also emphasizes the need for strong safety/security testing (misuse, AI hallucinations), breach response plans, and human oversight with override/correction mechanisms. The app currently supports about 50 services and is expected to grow to 200+ services.

Selangor launched an initiative to deploy AI-powered safety devices in elderly care centres, formalized through an MoU signed at the Selangor International Care Summit. In partnership with South Korean and Malaysian collaborators, the state will equip care facilities with infrared sensor + AI systems that detect hazards (e.g., falls/unsafe movements) and send alerts so caregivers can intervene quickly. The first rollout targets 100 care centres, planned to begin by year-end after local safety certification. The project supports Selangor’s Care Economy Policy 2024–2030, aiming to reduce preventable injuries, ease caregiver workload, and modernize welfare infrastructure through digital technology and international innovation partnerships. If successful, Selangor may expand similar tech to home-based care and assisted living.

The Philippines’ Department of Trade and Industry (DTI) is using digital tools to empower both consumers and businesses through initiatives that blend education, standards and SME support. In Tarlac, DTI and 27 partner establishments launched Consumer E-CONnect Programme 1.2 (“Learn While You Shop”), using in-store LED screens and TV monitors to share guidance on consumer rights, fair trade and product standards, building on earlier digital price-watch and advocacy materials. Nationally, DTI is strengthening e-commerce trust through PNS 2155:2020, a standard covering the full online transaction journey from browsing to returns and support, promoting transparency and accountability and drawing on Singapore’s TR 76. DTI is also boosting MSME digital capacity via programs like E-Taas ang Pinay MSMEs, which trained women entrepreneurs and provided digitalization kits to expand online presence and resilience.

Hong Kong’s “iAM Smart” has become a central gateway for digital government services, with over four million users and integration across 1,300+ online services through a single secure login. The platform streamlines resident interactions by reducing multiple apps and paper processes, using biometric authentication, encryption and layered verification for services like taxes, permits and utilities. New features include a Mini-program Platform that lets departments deliver services inside iAM Smart without separate downloads, plus an upgraded Personal Assistant dashboard and QR-based Personal Code for easier ID verification with less data exposure. The government is also exploring step-up authentication with financial institutions for high-risk transactions and plans to add an AI assistant by end-2026 to provide real-time guidance and personalized support, strengthening smart city goals and digital inclusion.

Minnesota passed a new pension law that improves how the state plans to pay down unfunded retirement liabilities by adopting “layered amortization,” a best-practice approach recommended by a legislative working group and supported by actuarial research. Instead of treating pension debt as one rolling balance, layered amortization breaks liabilities (and surpluses) into annual “layers” with closed pay-off periods, helping the state balance two goals: reaching full funding on a predictable timeline while avoiding sharp swings in required yearly contributions. The law also strengthens transparency by requiring annual reviews of projected amortization payments, aligning Minnesota with a growing number of states using this method to better control volatility, improve accountability, and sustain long-term pension stability.

As concerns grow that millions of Americans are unprepared for retirement, more states are launching “auto-IRA” programs that automatically enroll private-sector workers who lack employer-sponsored plans, funded through payroll deductions with an opt-out option. Nevada’s newly launched program (created in 2023) requires employers with six or more employees to participate unless they already offer a retirement plan, and it could cover about 500,000 workers; overall, 20 states have established similar programs and more than 1 million people have enrolled, though about 56 million private-sector workers still lack workplace coverage. States are also collaborating to cut costs (Nevada joined a Colorado-led consortium), and early results from Colorado suggest higher participation among lower-income workers and even an increase in employers offering 401(k)s. Supporters argue these programs are simple, portable and could reduce future public assistance costs, while opponents—some small business and financial industry groups—say they burden employers and compete with private options, as advocates push for wider adoption and potentially federal action.

The UK’s Department for Work and Pensions (DWP) is seeking a contract to deploy a conversational AI system in benefits call centres to better understand callers’ intent, route them to the right human agent, and offer personalised self-service options that can reduce call volumes and costs. The project budget is up to £23.4 million (incl. VAT), higher than a previous £10.8 million estimate, and would require UK-based hosting on a dedicated cloud while complying with GDPR/DPA and the UK government’s Security Policy Framework. The planned delivery window runs from 6 July 2026 to 5 July 2030, with optional extensions that could take it to July 2032. The push comes as benefit claimants increased by 11.8% from 2019 to 2023 (around 2.4 million more people), and a National Audit Office finding that 31.6 million call minutes in 2022–23 might have been avoidable, adding pressure for broader government tech modernisation.

Louisville Metro Government has launched its first AI pilot by partnering with Govstream.ai to test an AI-assisted permitting process focused on new residential construction (including multifamily). The pilot aims to shorten permit review timelines, reduce bottlenecks, and make approvals more predictable—supporting the city’s push to expand housing supply, especially affordable units. The city is gathering real-world feedback from builders and developers and notes this is its first AI-focused RFP. Louisville is also building AI capacity internally, including appointing its first Chief AI Officer (Pamela McKnight) and allocating $2 million in the IT budget for AI work.

Hong Kong’s Civil Engineering and Development Department is using AI, robotics and automation on the Trunk Road T2 and Cha Kwo Ling Tunnel project to boost efficiency, safety and precision while cutting costs and manpower needs. A major innovation is an autonomous air-ground tunnel inspection system that pairs a drone (upper tunnel) with an unmanned ground vehicle (lower tunnel) to achieve 360° coverage; ultra-HD images are analysed in real time by onboard AI to spot defects with millimetre-level accuracy, making inspections over 20 times faster at about half the cost compared with manual methods, and earning awards and patents. CEDD also introduced a robotic drilling system for ventilation duct slab works, using laser scanning to position and install anchor bolts while extracting dust, which reduces risky elevated manual work; the robot is reported to cut on-site labour by around 60% and shorten related construction time by roughly 40%. These deployments align with a wider government push to pilot, incentivise and ultimately require suitable construction robots in public works, with subsidies to accelerate adoption across the private sector.

Researchers at the University of Surrey built an AI speech-recognition tool tailored to UK Supreme Court language, trained on 139 hours of hearings plus legal texts. They say it cuts transcription errors by up to 9% versus leading commercial tools, making hearings easier to record and access. A second AI component links judgment paragraphs to the exact video timestamp where each argument occurred, improving traceability. The university says the UK Supreme Court and the National Archives have shown interest.

The New York state court system on Friday set out a new policy on the use of artificial intelligence by judges and other court staff, joining at least four other U.S. states that have adopted similar rules in the past year.

Tencent is integrating Mastercard’s Click to Pay into its cross-border payment ecosystem MIDAS (including Midasbuy), aiming to make mobile game and digital-entertainment purchases faster and safer for tens of millions of users. Click to Pay reduces checkout friction by avoiding manual card entry and instead using transaction tokenization plus on-device biometrics (fingerprint/face) to confirm payments. Mastercard says this supports its broader goal of replacing manually entered card details with biometrics and tokenization over the coming years, building on earlier Tencent–Mastercard work on fraud management and promotions.

Google Pay is expanding its financial services in India with Flex, a UPI-powered, RuPay-based co-branded digital credit card launched first with Axis Bank and rolling out via an in-app waitlist, letting users apply digitally, manage repayments, earn rewards, and convert eligible purchases into 3- or 6-month EMIs after comparing plans in-app. It also introduced Pocket Money, built on UPI Circle, which gives children supervised payment access while parents set monthly limits up to ₹15,000, approve transactions, receive instant alerts, track activity, and pause access anytime. For merchants, Google Pay added post-transaction ratings tied to Google Maps listings and a GenAI ad-creation tool in Google Pay for Business to generate and launch campaigns quickly. On security, the company says it blocked ₹13,000 crore in attempted fraud in the past year, issued 41 million scam warnings since Oct 2024, added Android alerts for risky screen-sharing situations, and expanded an agentic AI chatbot for fraud reports that reportedly improved scam detection by 21%.

NSW and the ACCC formed a partnership to detect and deter bid rigging/cartel conduct in government tenders. NSW will share tender and contract data, and use AI to process large volumes of documents and spot suspicious bidding patterns for referral to the ACCC, which can investigate, prosecute, and trigger supplier suspension. NSW highlights potential savings (OECD suggests up to 20% from stronger competition) and points to overseas screening tools (e.g., South Korea flagging ~80 cases/month and fines in 2018–2021).

Glass has upgraded and redesigned its G-Commerce marketplace into an AI-driven procurement platform that automates key public-sector purchasing steps such as product discovery, vendor eligibility checks, compliance validation, and access to purchasing records. Government buyers can describe needs in natural language (budget, delivery timelines, location, policy constraints) and the system recommends compliant products and vendors, while also offering conversational access to order status, shipment tracking, invoices, and payment confirmations. Glass says the marketplace supports 18,000+ government users across 124 agencies, connects to about 8.5 million products via APIs plus 5 million more via punch-out catalogs, and embeds procurement rules and policy enforcement directly into the platform. Reported outcomes to date include over $8 million in purchases processed, 6 million+ products delivered, and $4.6 million+ directed to small businesses, alongside support for programs like AbilityOne, HUBZone, veteran-owned and women-owned suppliers, and U.S.-made products.

As state budgets tighten, many U.S. states are accelerating government modernization to deliver services faster and at lower cost by redesigning processes, digitizing operations, and increasingly using AI (including generative AI). Some states focus on cutting waste and improving accountability, while others prioritize better digital service delivery to rebuild public trust. Results often come from combining people, process change, and technology—such as Maryland saving money through smarter statewide purchasing, Colorado reducing unemployment call wait times with an AI virtual agent and staffing changes, and Arizona saving staff time with AI-assisted casework. States are also forming in-house digital service teams and piloting AI carefully to avoid risks, while tackling chronic bottlenecks like permitting backlogs and slow hiring through more transparent tracking and faster recruitment.

Australia’s competition watchdog (ACCC) warns that major government tenders—such as Brisbane 2032 Olympics projects, big state infrastructure and defence contracts—face high risks of bid rigging and cartel collusion that can inflate public costs by over 20%, and it wants governments to share full tender data (including losing bids) so algorithms, and eventually AI, can detect suspicious pricing and “turn-taking” patterns among bidders. NSW and South Australia have already agreed to share procurement data, with the ACCC seeking broader federal and state participation as it builds an Australian screening tool modeled on Spain’s highly predictive system. Recent and ongoing enforcement includes civil cartel proceedings tied to Defence maintenance services and past actions in other public projects, while whistleblowers remain critical for proving cases. The ACCC is also strengthening its data/AI capability with the appointment of a former chief data scientist, noting that procurement transparency can paradoxically make collusion easier by giving bidders the same information and timelines.

Indonesia is modernising border management at Tanjung Priok Port (Jakarta) by deploying a package of AI- and data-enabled customs technologies to strengthen surveillance, speed up clearance, and detect fraud earlier. The rollout includes (1) X-ray container scanners with Radiation Portal Monitors to detect nuclear/radioactive materials without opening containers, (2) a Self Service Report Mobile feature within CEISA 4.0 Mobile that uses geotagging, real-time activity logs and AI risk analysis to track cargo movements and flag irregularities, and (3) “Trade AI” to improve import analysis and identify under/over-invoicing and potential trade-based money laundering, with planned expansion into valuation, classification and document verification. In parallel, Indonesia has rolled out the “All Indonesia” digital immigration platform nationwide (airports and seaports), integrating immigration, customs, health and quarantine through biometrics, real-time data sharing and AI coordination to cut waiting times, improve security and support trade/tourism.

Dallas Police are considering a major expansion of their facial recognition use with Clearview AI, extending searches from serious felonies (like murder and rape) to lower-level offenses such as trespassing and package theft (Class B misdemeanors), which has sparked criticism from civil liberties advocates who argue the broad database and wider use increase risks. Dallas says it began contracting for the tool around mid-2024, has used it 156 times, and claims it contributed to 25 arrests, calling it “vital” in those cases. In a separate development, Clearview AI won dismissal of a lawsuit brought by Vermont Attorney General Charity Clark after a judge ruled Vermont courts lack jurisdiction because Clearview has no local contracts/business in the state; Clark said the decision shows technology is outpacing the law.

Cambodia’s General Department of Taxation (GDT) launched an AI-powered tax chatbot called “Beauramei”, starting with Khmer-language support and planned upgrades over time. The chatbot provides text-based guidance on tax matters—covering tax laws, regulations, and supporting documents—to reduce reliance on in-person visits and manual replies. The initiative aligns with the government’s public-service modernization agenda and supports domestic revenue mobilization by improving access to accurate information, which is expected to strengthen voluntary tax compliance, especially among SMEs.

HMRC confirmed it uses AI to help monitor social media posts as part of criminal investigations into suspected tax evasion, not to track “everyday taxpayers.” HMRC says AI won’t replace human decision-making and is used with legal oversight, aiming to target fraud/evasion more effectively and free staff from admin work so they can help taxpayers. Experts caution the approach carries risks such as mistaken identity and fake/hacked accounts, so human review remains essential. The report notes HMRC has used data-analysis software for years, plans more AI to help people navigate extensive online guidance, and the government says HMRC is adding 5,500 compliance staff.

South Korea’s National Tax Service (NTS) said it will open its “Simplified Year-End Tax Settlement Service” on Jan. 15 to let workers bulk-check income and tax-credit proof documents needed for the 2025 year-end tax settlement. Year-end settlement recalculates the final income tax based on annual earnings and eligible deductions/credits—employees may receive a refund or owe additional tax.

Malaysia is accelerating smart city development through large-scale investment in AI and robotics, built around a robotics-as-a-service (RaaS) model and AI-driven city platforms. The initiative aims to use purpose-built urban developments as testbeds (“living laboratories”) where automation and data platforms improve city operations and enable new resident services across healthcare, education, entertainment, retail, facilities, and logistics.

The Philippines’ DILG is mandating nationwide use of LGUSS-BIMS, a web-based Barangay Information Management System that digitizes and standardizes local records (residents, assets, finances, ordinances, disaster data) through 11 integrated modules. It enables real-time reporting and secure data sharing with higher LGUs, improving efficiency, transparency, accountability, and faster service delivery. The system is free, supported by training, and emphasizes data privacy/security via controlled access. Current uptake: 9,774 of 42,011 barangays (23%) actively using it, and 14,008 (33%) have completed orientation.

Hong Kong has launched the CorpID Sandbox Programme (run by the Digital Policy Office with Cyberport) to let public/private providers test corporate digital identity functions via a simulated API and build proof-of-concept apps. The full CorpID Platform is planned for end-2026, enabling businesses to do corporate authentication, digital signing, form pre-filling, and storage of licences/permits. Businesses can apply through the CorpID Platform or a CorpID mini-program inside iAM Smart (Hong Kong’s biometric digital ID).

Utah’s Department of Commerce Office of Artificial Intelligence Policy (OAIP) is using its Learning Lab / regulatory sandbox model to test AI in real-world services under state oversight. OAIP (opened July 2024) signs regulatory mitigation agreements that reduce regulatory friction while keeping consumer protections.

Uzbekistan’s Presidential Decree (Dec 26, 2025, No. UP-259) sets new measures to strengthen competition and transparency in public procurement as part of anti-corruption efforts. It assigns the Ministry of Economy and Finance a core role in building a modern, service-oriented e-procurement ecosystem with widespread AI adoption, and sets 2030 targets including 80% competitive procurement, savings of 25 trillion UZS, doubling business participation, at least 85% domestic content, and 98% of procurement staff trained. From March 1, 2026, an AI-based portal module will calculate average market prices; buyers must use it before procurement, and deals showing significant deviation from the module price will be flagged as high-risk for priority inspection, while direct agreements generally cannot exceed the module’s market price (with legal exceptions). The decree also expands competitive procedures by introducing “request for proposals” from Jan 1, 2026, approving related lists and processes, and cancelling a prior list that allowed certain purchases via direct agreements—shifting those items to competitive methods except where the law permits otherwise.

Haryana Chief Minister Nayab Singh Saini launched an AI-based portal called “Haryana Budget Janbhagidari” to let citizens, experts, and stakeholders submit suggestions directly for the state’s budget-making process. The portal supports Haryanvi, Hindi, and English to broaden participation, and was introduced during a pre-budget session in Gurugram as part of Haryana Vision 2047. The government framed it as a move toward greater transparency and continuous, dialogue-driven governance, with the portal expected to go live late Tuesday night or by Wednesday.

IATA leads global safety for air transport of dangerous goods by setting standards, coordinating with ICAO and governments, and providing regulations, training, and industry tools to ensure hazardous materials are handled safely and consistently.

Singapore will tighten penalties for scams from 30 Dec 2025 under the Criminal Law (Miscellaneous Amendments) Act 2025 (passed 4 Nov 2025). Key changes:

Mandatory caning (minimum 6 strokes) will apply to certain remote-communication scam cheating cases under Penal Code s420, alongside up to 10 years’ jail and possible fines.

Mandatory caning also applies to members/recruiters of organised scam groups if they knew the group’s purpose was to benefit from scam offences.

Harsher penalties for recruiters who target vulnerable people or those under 21: up to 7 years’ jail, plus mandatory caning and fines (up to S$350,000).

Discretionary caning (up to 12 strokes) may be imposed on scam “enablers”, including offences involving SIM cards, Singpass credential disclosure, and certain money-laundering offences—especially where there was intent/knowledge (or reasonable grounds to believe) the tools would be used for scams and insufficient steps were taken to prevent misuse.

Separate changes taking effect the same day: the Youth Court framework for offenders 16 to below 18 will be operationalised, with serious/repeat cases potentially transferred to higher courts where stronger sentences can apply.

The Province of Buenos Aires will require biometric ID and facial recognition for all authorised online gaming and sports betting platforms to help prevent underage gambling and stop access using relatives’ data. Minister Carlos Bianco said the seven licensed platforms have 60 days to implement identity verification with a “proof of life” at login, which may limit use on devices without cameras. The province is also cracking down on illegal betting, citing 300 complaints filed in one week, and noted it has a mental health support network for gambling addiction. Separately, the lotteries and casinos institute is preparing stricter advertising rules—including limits on timing and messaging—to better protect minors.

New York State is exploring biometrics (facial recognition or fingerprints) as a possible way to verify age and block under-21 users from accessing online sports betting accounts. Gaming Commission Chair Brian O’Dwyer said the Commission supports Gov. Kathy Hochul’s push to strengthen protections and will consider steps such as biometric requirements for account access and penalties for adults who share accounts with minors. The Commission also plans to keep working with the state’s addiction services office to integrate technology that can connect people to help for gambling-related harms.

The memo sits alongside a wider package of proposed gambling changes in New York, including bills focused on tighter advertising rules, creating a problem-gambling advisory council, limiting push notifications/text promotions, introducing default betting limits (with opt-out), and other consumer-protection adjustments

DHS has created a new Program Executive Office dedicated to deploying drones and countering malicious drone use, and it is finalizing a $115 million investment in counter-drone technology. The office will help protect major events such as the FIFA 2026 World Cup matches hosted across North America and U.S. 250th anniversary (July 4) celebrations. DHS notes drones are increasingly used for crimes and disruptions (including near airports and stadiums), and recent actions—such as renewed federal counter-drone authorities through 2031 and large grant funding for state/local efforts—are meant to strengthen detection and response nationwide.

This opinion article argues that Flock Safety license-plate reader (LPR) cameras are becoming a valuable force-multiplier for Colorado police departments (including Aurora, Denver, Colorado Springs, and Douglas County) as agencies face staffing strain and high crime workloads. It claims the cameras help identify vehicles linked to crimes by reading plates and capturing details like make/model/color and plate anomalies, and it cites examples of arrests and recoveries tied to Flock alerts. The piece also points to Denver’s pilot as evidence of impact, noting reported reductions in auto thefts alongside arrests, recovered vehicles, and firearms—while framing the technology as a modern “Neighborhood Watch.”

Indonesia is ramping up child protection and “digital resilience” by combining law-enforcement monitoring with school- and community-based prevention. Police highlight strong security outcomes (no terror attacks reported in 2023 and 2025), while Densus 88 warns that some minors (ages 11–18) have been exposed online to extremist content through certain online communities. In response, education authorities—particularly in East Java—are strengthening reflective digital literacy (critical thinking, spotting manipulation), counselling and early intervention, plus practical rules on device use and reporting mechanisms, supported by coordination among schools, families, ministries and child-protection bodies.

The article explains that the IRS is expanding AI and data analytics to modernize taxpayer services, compliance, and investigations—using tools like chatbots to reduce call-center demand, advanced models to improve audit selection and detect fraud, and analytics platforms (including Palantir tools) to speed up criminal investigations. It notes that progress is happening under tighter budgets and staffing constraints, with the IRS’s RAAS (Research, Applied Analytics and Statistics) office coordinating analytics across the agency. At the same time, it flags concerns about transparency (AI use-case inventories), bias and fairness in audit targeting, privacy risks when using external data/tools, and the need for strong human oversight—citing examples like Australia’s “Robodebt” as a cautionary tale.

In October 2025, the Dominican Republic’s tax authority (DGII) issued Notice No. 22-2025 clarifying how the country’s territorial income tax applies to tax residents. Under this approach, residents are generally taxed on Dominican-source income and certain foreign-source investment earnings, while most other foreign-source income is not taxed initially and becomes taxable starting in the third year of residence.

Kenya Revenue Authority (KRA) has launched a WhatsApp chatbot that provides 15 tax services 24/7, including guidance for tax return filing, PIN management, tax queries, eTIMS invoicing and digital self-service. Users access it by saving +254 711099999 and messaging “Hi” or “Menu,” then verifying identity to view service options. KRA says the bot gives step-by-step instructions for filing via the iTax portal, and the move supports a broader IT upgrade to expand AI, machine learning and data analytics for tax administration. KRA also recently rolled out a *USSD option (222#) to help taxpayers without smartphones or reliable internet access.

The Economic Times article argues that India’s Union Budget 2026 (to be presented on 1 Feb 2026) can significantly improve taxpayer experience as a “bridge” to the new Income Tax Act 2025 (effective 1 Apr 2026). It highlights six priorities: focus on administrative improvements (e.g., faster refunds and simpler compliance), strengthen the digital framework (improving AIS/TIS accuracy and transparency), use AI-enabled tools for pre-filling and error reduction plus real-time refund tracking, accelerate resolution of tax litigation backlogs, clarify rules for virtual digital assets (VDAs), and extend ESOP tax deferral beyond eligible start-ups to all employees.

India’s national auditor (CAG) urged stronger audit institutions for local governments (PAIs) to close capacity gaps and improve transparency. A national workshop highlighted the need to modernize local fund audits using standardized methods, better planning/reporting, stronger follow-up, and more tech-enabled (including remote/virtual) audits to improve accountability and public spending oversight.

India’s Institute of Chartered Accountants of India (ICAI) and the Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG) are jointly exploring autonomous auditing systems that use blockchain + AI to improve audit accuracy and enable better end-to-end transaction traceability.

The first phase is expected to begin with audits of public sector undertakings (PSUs).

The idea is that transactions become linked “blocks” that can be traced across stakeholders (and potentially connected to regulators such as income tax/GST), while AI supports deeper checks—scrutinising ledgers, flagging risks, generating working papers, and helping with early fraud detection.

The Auditor-General of South Africa (AGSA) describes moving beyond sample-based audits to AI-supported analysis across transactions, with direct access to financial systems and earlier identification of high-risk items before year-end submissions

UK lawmakers on Parliament’s Treasury Committee warned that Britain’s financial regulators are being too passive about AI risks in finance, and urged them to move away from a “wait and see” approach.

They called on the Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) and the Bank of England (BoE) to start running AI-specific “stress tests” so firms can prepare for market shocks or incidents triggered by automated/agentic systems.

Treasury says it is shifting federal payments from a “pay-and-chase” approach to proactive prevention, using better data and modern screening so incorrect or fraudulent payments are stopped before money goes out.

Do Not Pay (DNP) modernization: Treasury is expanding and improving Do Not Pay (authorized under the Payment Integrity Information Act of 2019) to help agencies and states screen for key improper-payment drivers (e.g., deceased individuals, ineligible entities, invalid bank accounts). Treasury says DNP has been underused (only ~4% of federal programs completed legal requirements to access all DNP databases in FY2024) and is working to reduce sign-up barriers and speed up adding (“designating”) new databases

India’s EPFO is preparing an “EPFO 3.0” tech overhaul to move its provident fund services toward a core banking–style backend, with a new portal, faster grievance handling from any office, and AI language/translation support (e.g., Bhashini) to serve members in regional languages. A major member-facing change is UPI-based EPF withdrawals via BHIM/UPI, expected to show balances and eligible amounts, with discussions indicating an initial ₹25,000 per-transaction cap and a target go-live around April 2026. EPFO is also nearing completion of remaining EPFO 2.0 modules, and has already enabled self-correction of personal details, processing 32.23 lakh corrections in 2025.

The UK Cabinet Office confirmed the refreshed Civil Service Pensions website and a new Member Portal went live on Monday, 1 December (from midday). Members can register via civilservicepensionscheme.org.uk using a personal email and National Insurance number, but administrators stress there’s no immediate rush—pensioners will receive registration details from April 2026 with their Pension Increase letter and P60, with reminders thereafter. The portal lets members update personal details, use a secure mailbox (including uploading forms), access and print payslips/P60s, and manage death benefit nominations; previous portal payslips/P60s will be migrated. Next updates include a new mobile app in Spring 2026, a chatbot from April 2026, and multi-account viewing from April 2026; the old app is discontinued

The article explains how Prepared by Axon’s AI-enabled 911 platform aims to improve “situational clarity” from the moment a call comes in to officers arriving on scene. It uses an AI voice assistant to triage non-emergency calls (freeing human call-takers for urgent incidents), and for emergencies it provides real-time transcription, fast multilingual translation (30+ languages), and prominent keyword/critical-data highlights (e.g., addresses, plates, “gunshot,” “unconscious”) to reduce missed details. For dispatch, it transcribes radio channels, flags urgent keywords (like mayday), and generates searchable, time-stamped summaries that both call-takers and dispatchers can view, improving coordination; the article cites examples like improved location/GPS “breadcrumbs” aiding a Lake Erie rescue. After calls, automated QA and analytics review interactions against protocols to identify training needs and performance improvements.

Indonesia plans to ramp up digital infrastructure investment in 2026 to accelerate its digital economy agenda and support long-term growth under the “Golden Indonesia 2045” vision, alongside new biometrics procurements such as an ABIS upgrade. The article highlights rising interest from global tech players (e.g., AWS) and policy discussions on data governance, connectivity, security and partnerships. It stresses that Indonesia’s Digital Public Infrastructure (DPI) depends heavily on its national digital ID (IKD), already issued to at least 17 million people, and notes Indonesia’s intent to host the Global DPI Summit. The piece also situates Indonesia within a wider Global South trend (Brazil, India, Nigeria, South Africa) where DPI is treated as a tool of governance and economic inclusion—while warning about the risks of dependence on foreign platforms.

OSHA’s updated Hazard Communication (HazCom) Standard (29 CFR 1910.1200), aligned with UN GHS Rev. 7, took effect in July 2024, but OSHA has extended the initial compliance deadlines. For manufacturers/importers/distributors, full compliance for chemical substances is now due May 19, 2026 (extended from Jan 19, 2026), and for mixtures Nov 19, 2027. For employers, the deadlines are Nov 20, 2026 (substances) and May 19, 2028 (mixtures). The revision adds/updates hazard classification criteria, SDS/label content (including small-container labeling options), trade secret disclosure rules, pictograms, and precautionary statements; employers must manage updated SDSs/labels and update their written HazCom program and training accordingly.

California DTSC adopted EPA’s Generator Improvements Rule and, starting July 1, 2024, formally added the Very Small Quantity Generator (VSQG) category (≤100 kg/month non-acute HW and ≤1 kg/month acute HW). The key twist is that California did not adopt the federal VSQG exemptions, so VSQGs in California generally must still follow Small Quantity Generator (SQG)-level requirements (e.g., ≤180-day accumulation and ≤6,000 kg onsite cap, plus the annual eVQ), even though they’re now “defined” as VSQGs. One limited relief: VSQGs don’t have to re-notify every four years using EPA Form 8700-12, unlike SQGs/LQGs.

A new two-year pilot in the English Commercial Court and Financial List (Practice Direction 51ZH), running from 1 Jan 2026 to 31 Dec 2027, makes “open justice” more practical by requiring parties to re-file key hearing documents in a public section of CE-File when they are used or referred to in public hearings. This can make skeleton arguments, written submissions, witness statements, expert reports and other “critical” documents much easier for the public to access, unless confidentiality is protected through existing orders or by seeking Filing Modification Orders (FMOs) (e.g., redactions, restricting access, narrowing/waiving filing). The change increases transparency but also raises confidentiality and reputational risks, meaning parties should plan early, tighten drafting, and consider venue/arbitration choices.

Singapore partners led by NTU have piloted a data-driven rehabilitation robot (DRBA) in neighbourhood active ageing centres to help seniors with mobility challenges stay active and independent. The robot supports standing and walking, continuously monitors movement, and intervenes when instability is detected to reduce fall risk and caregiver burden. Early community trials (e.g., Tampines) showed it can restore confidence without limiting independence, and it is now being commercialised with a next-generation mobile version targeted for 2026.

A four-student University of Michigan team won $15,000 at the 2025 MiSpace Hackathon for IceScope GL, a machine-learning tool that combines satellite radar and weather data to produce four-day forecasts of Great Lakes ice buildup (type, concentration, thickness) displayed on a map. The U.S. Coast Guard is interested, and the team plans to further improve the model into a usable product.

The UK Government’s GDS AI Engineering Lab (run by the Engineering Excellence team) is a 2026 initiative to help public-sector software teams adopt AI practically and responsibly, building on the 2025 AI Coding Assistant trial. It will support AI across the software lifecycle by integrating tools into workflows, upskilling staff, and evaluating real service impact. From early 2026 it will offer time-limited (up to six months) licences for tools like Microsoft Copilot, Gemini, Amazon Q/Kiro and Claude, alongside setup help, training, hackathons and community events, with teams encouraged to join early due to limited licences.

NADRA has launched its first Bug Bounty Challenge 2026 to strengthen Pakistan’s digital ID infrastructure against cyber threats. Run with the Higher Education Commission and the National Cyber Emergency Response Team, the team-based competition invites ethical hackers, students and cybersecurity professionals to responsibly find vulnerabilities, with regional rounds starting Jan 27, 2026 at major universities (including GIKI, NUST, UET Lahore, NED University and BUITEMS). The initiative supports “security-by-design” as Pakistan Digital Authority backs the program and NADRA modernizes identity verification, including adding contactless fingerprints, iris scans and face biometrics, with the final ceremony planned at its HQ in Islamabad.

China’s Wuhu city has deployed an AI-powered humanoid “Intelligent Police Unit R001” to assist traffic officers. Integrated with the city’s traffic signals, it performs standard directing gestures, uses cameras and voice alerts to spot violations by pedestrians and cyclists, and can move autonomously for tasks like monitoring roads and identifying illegal parking. The rollout reflects a wider trend in Chinese cities adopting robotic policing tools to support 24/7 operations and reduce workload.

Police agencies in the U.S. and Canada are increasingly adopting “robot dogs” like Boston Dynamics’ Spot to handle high-risk situations such as armed standoffs, hostage rescues and hazardous materials incidents, where sending people or K9s could be dangerous. Supporters say Spot’s agility (stairs, doors, indoor work) and live video/sensors can improve safety and situational awareness. Critics and civil liberties groups warn that semi-autonomous robots could normalize more militarized policing and expand surveillance, arguing for clear public rules, oversight and transparent, limited use cases.
City of Tampa details VR pods where AI virtual characters respond in real-time to an officer’s voice and tone, enabling repeatable de-escalation practice; plus 360° scenario training
Australia rolling out mandatory cybersecurity standards for consumer smart devices starting 4 March 2026 (IoT baseline security requirements

From 11 September 2026, manufacturers of products with digital elements must report actively exploited vulnerabilities and severe security incidents. They must submit an early warning within 24 hours, a full notification within 72 hours, and then a final report within 14 days once a corrective measure is available for exploited vulnerabilities (or within one month for severe incidents). Reporting is done once via the CRA Single Reporting Platform (SRP), addressed to the CSIRT in the manufacturer’s main establishment and shared with ENISA; CSIRTs normally share notifications with other affected CSIRTs, with limited exceptions under a Commission delegated act (adopted 11 Dec 2025)

English: HSBC UK has partnered with Sage to help sole traders and small landlords prepare for the UK’s upcoming Making Tax Digital (MTD) changes. The new “My Business Finances” capability will embed Sage’s accounting tools inside the HSBC app/banking experience so users can track income and expenses, create invoices, and support digital tax submission to HMRC in one place—aiming to reduce admin time and improve readiness. Reports linked to the launch cite research indicating around 70% of sole traders aren’t ready, and about one in three still use pen and paper to manage finances.

India’s Economic Survey 2025–26 says the Income Tax Department is shifting from audit-and-penalty enforcement toward behavioural “nudges” and data analytics to boost voluntary compliance. The core tool is the NUDGE framework (Non-intrusive Usage of Data to Guide and Enable), which uses large-scale data to spot likely non-compliance and send timely, gentle prompts so taxpayers can correct filings before audits or litigation.
