BLS International says it has strengthened cybersecurity and AI-enabled systems supporting visa services in Mauritania to protect applicants and improve reliability during peak demand, adding a multi-layered setup that includes advanced application firewalls, OTP verification, appointment validation and tighter security controls aimed at stopping fraud and automated/bot abuse across booking, document submission and biometric enrolment; the company frames this as part of its wider modernization effort across 46+ partner countries to provide a secure, transparent and fair digital application experience.

Tonga launched the e-Passport project through its first Project Steering Committee meeting on 27 February 2026 in Nuku‘alofa, chaired by HRH Crown Prince Tupouto‘a ‘Ulukalala, bringing together 14 government agencies plus Japan’s embassy and IOM to begin a multi-year rollout of electronic passports that will align Tonga’s travel documents with international standards, strengthen border security against identity fraud and transnational crime, and modernise public services by streamlining issuance, improving data integrity and expanding access to reliable legal identity; the project is funded by the Government of Japan, with IOM providing technical support to design, procure, deploy and pilot an integrated, secure and compliant e-passport issuance system.

Shanghai launched a cross-border digital ID system letting eligible foreign firms (starting with Singapore investors) register online using DID/VC and blockchain checks, cutting setup from about a week to a few days; the first case finished in 2 days.

The EU-funded SUPREME project is redesigning PEM electrolysis for green hydrogen by replacing PFAS “forever chemicals” in membranes with safer alternatives and cutting reliance on scarce iridium catalysts by about 75%. The project also targets circularity by developing processes to recover up to 90% of iridium from end-of-life equipment, while partners work on PFAS-free microporous membranes, improved electrolyser engineering (including a rotating design), and industrial-grade membrane-electrode manufacturing. The aim is to lower green hydrogen costs and make it viable for hard-to-electrify industries like steel, ammonia and methanol, while reducing environmental and health risks from persistent chemicals.

Inert cryogenic liquids (e.g., liquid nitrogen) require baseline safety everywhere (pressure-relief devices, good ventilation, clear door signage, compatible vessels like dewars, and proper PPE during dispensing), but New York City adds specific FDNY fire-code triggers for non-production labs: if a lab unit stores more than 60 gallons, it must install and maintain an oxygen sensor (NYC Fire Code 5006.6.10.2) — meaning a single standard 63-gallon (240 L) LN₂ tank typically triggers this. NYC also treats larger storage as a “bulk inert gas system” by referencing CGA P-18 (NYC Fire Code 5501.3.3): if the inert gas storage capacity exceeds 20,000 cubic feet, which roughly corresponds to more than four 63-gallon LN₂ tanks, FDNY considers it beyond normal lab-permit controls and usually requires a Technology Management (TM) Variance before issuing or renewing the Non-Production Laboratory Unit Permit. TM submissions generally need plans and documentation showing code-compliant ventilation (NYC Mechanical Code), properly designed/installed manifolds and piping by licensed personnel, and sometimes proof that oxygen sensors are hard-wired into building systems. The stricter approach reflects NYC’s common lab conditions: small spaces in dense, multi-tenant high-rises where an oxygen-deficiency incident can affect more people.

India says it will accelerate AI adoption while managing risks through a multi-layered governance approach that combines law, oversight and public education—especially to protect children and vulnerable groups. The government points to existing legal controls under the IT Act 2000 and IT Rules for rapid takedown/blocking of unlawful content (including stricter response for non-consensual intimate material) and mandatory reporting under laws such as POCSO (2012) and Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (2023). In parallel, the DPDP Act (2023) and 2025 rules strengthen children’s data protections by requiring verifiable parental consent and prohibiting profiling, tracking, behavioural monitoring and targeted ads for minors. India is also expanding awareness and capacity-building via CERT-In guidance and the ISEA programme, alongside AI governance guidelines promoting risk assessment, transparency and accountability, plus product/online safety standards and cybercrime coordination—aiming to “democratise” AI access while maintaining safety, privacy and trust.

India is strengthening flood and cyclone preparedness through district-level early warning systems that speed up and sharpen alerts for high-risk areas. The IMD now issues district-specific forecasts four times daily, with outlooks up to seven days, shared through apps, websites, social media, SMS and the Common Alerting Protocol, helping authorities and communities plan and coordinate. For floods, the Central Water Commission (CWC) provides forecasts from 350 stations (including dam inflow and river level sites), using models to generate 7-day advisories and up to 24-hour lead-time short-range forecasts. Tools like C-Flood add two-day village-level inundation forecasts (using satellite, hydrology and rainfall data) with colour-coded severity alerts, while the Flood Watch India app (launched 2023) offers forecasts, real-time monitoring and reservoir storage information. Cyclone alerts are delivered via multiple channels including broadcasts, SMS and NAVIC, supported by state networks for last-mile reach, plus awareness campaigns, better connectivity and siren systems—aiming to cut losses of life, property and livelihoods through faster action and better coordination.

The UK Home Office’s Fraud Strategy 2026–2029 sets a new national approach to combat fraud (now one of the UK’s most common and damaging crimes) through three pillars: Disrupt (cutting off the tools, platforms and infrastructure criminals rely on—e.g., launching a public-private Online Crime Centre and strengthening international cooperation), Safeguard (building public and business resilience via expanded Stop! Think Fraud messaging and more proactive, data-led prevention), and Respond (improving reporting and victim support through a new Report Fraud service, developing a Fraud Victims Charter, and strengthening civil/criminal justice responses). It also sets out delivery governance (including stronger cross-system oversight and annual reporting) and metrics to track impact over time.

Europol coordinated a year-long global crackdown on environmental crime and waste trafficking called Operation “Custos Viridis” (intelligence phase Jan–Jun 2025; operational phase Jul–Dec 2025) with partners from 71 countries across five continents. Authorities carried out 1,048 inspections and arrested 337 people, seizing 127,149 tonnes of waste and 602 tonnes of polluting agents (including 398 tonnes of illegal fluorinated greenhouse gases – F-gas), plus 75 tonnes of plant protection products, 2.3 tonnes of mercury, and nearly €10 million in cash/accounts, along with vehicles, heavy machinery and other evidence. Investigators identified organised networks trafficking waste within the EU and exporting it to Africa, Asia and Latin America, alongside related crimes like money laundering, tax evasion, corruption, illicit F-gas trade (valued €15–€20m) and illegal gold mining using mercury/cyanide. Europol set up a coordination hub to share real-time intelligence and connect cross-border leads, underscoring that environmental crime is increasingly global, flexible and closely linked to fraud and corruption.

The UK Home Office and National Crime Agency have announced a major escalation in the fraud crackdown through a new Online Crime Centre launching in April 2026, bringing together government, police, intelligence agencies, banks, telecoms and big tech to share data quickly and shut down scam infrastructure at scale (blocking scam texts/calls, taking down fake accounts/sites, freezing criminal accounts and targeting high-harm offenders), backed by £250m over 3 years and £30m+ specifically to fund the centre; the expanded strategy responds to fraud affecting 1 in 14 adults and 1 in 4 businesses and costing £14bn+ annually, with a strong focus on overseas “scam compounds” and international partnerships, plus using AI to spot emerging patterns, stop suspicious transfers faster and deploy scam-baiting tools, while also improving victim outcomes via a Fraud Victims Charter, national service standards, and a network of PROTECT officers for vulnerable victims, alongside reforms to speed justice and strengthen civil powers

Hungary’s 2026 tax audit plan shows the Hungarian Tax Authority (HTA) is moving to a strongly data-driven, AI-assisted risk screening model, expecting taxpayers to proactively reconcile and correct discrepancies across returns and digital reporting (notably online invoicing and VAT).

BIR Revenue Memorandum Circular No. 005-2026 (Jan 12, 2026) launches an LOA (Letter of Authority) Verifier inside the REVIE chatbot to help taxpayers confirm if an LOA is authentic by entering the taxpayer name, TIN, and LOA case number. If the system matches, REVIE returns “LOA FOUND.” If “LOA NOT FOUND,” the taxpayer should email contact_us-LOA@bir.gov.ph
 with a copy of the LOA and key details; BIR will validate the LOA and provide an official response within three (3) working days.

Singapore has launched a new tool on the Singapore Land Authority’s OneMap portal that lets developers instantly estimate Land Betterment Charges (LBC) for proposed projects, giving businesses earlier cost certainty to support investment decisions. Announced by Law Minister Edwin Tong on Feb 27, 2026, the tool calculates estimated LBC from key inputs and allows scenario testing across different development options. Alongside this, SLA has brought forward the start of valuations for cases needing spot valuations to the provisional permission stage, potentially cutting the process by up to six months. The update builds on the LBC regime introduced in August 2022 (which replaced older development charge and differential premium systems), includes clearer treatment for solar deployments (classified under use group D from Sept 1, 2025), and sits within broader digitisation moves such as a pilot Digital Conveyancing Portal planned for 2026 to shift property transactions toward paperless processing.

The U.S. Department of Commerce announced the next phase of the American AI Exports Program, opening a Call for Proposals for U.S. industry-led consortia to export “full-stack” AI packages (AI-optimized hardware, data center storage, models, cybersecurity, and sector applications) to trusted partners under President Trump’s AI export directives

Bank Negara Malaysia (BNM) issued a new technology risk management policy for Malaysia’s payment services sector to strengthen digital payment resilience, cybersecurity, and operational reliability as digital transactions expand. The document consolidates tech-related requirements for key regulatees such as approved e-money issuers, registered merchant acquirers, and money services businesses, giving clearer, single-framework guidance on technology governance, risk management, and security controls. It applies a tiered (proportionate) approach, scaling obligations based on a provider’s size, complexity, and risk profile, while still setting consistent expectations for secure, reliable operations. The policy emphasizes stronger cyber safeguards (monitoring, detection, incident response), improved fraud detection and transaction monitoring (real-time analytics, automated alerts), and user protection measures like stronger authentication and notifications, while supporting responsible adoption of technologies such as cloud, AI, and advanced analytics without weakening security or stability.

On 15 Dec 2025, the UN General Assembly adopted the first-ever United Nations Principles for Consumer Product Safety. The principles affirm every consumer’s right to safe, non-hazardous products online and offline, place primary responsibility on businesses across the full product life cycle, and strengthen government powers to assess risks, order recalls, remove unsafe online listings, and share alerts cross-border. UNCTAD notes major gaps remain (about 44% of UN Member States lack adequate product safety legal frameworks), and e-commerce complicates enforcement (an OECD study found 87% of recalled/banned products remain available online). UNCTAD is tasked with supporting global implementation, with the next expert session planned for July 2026 (Geneva) and a Consumer Product Safety Handbook in development.

World Economic Forum Global Risks Report 2026 describes the world as entering an “age of competition,” where short-term risks are dominated by geoeconomic confrontation and state-based armed conflict, while longer-term risks increasingly center on environmental pressures and deeper societal fragmentation. The report is based on insights from more than 1,300 experts worldwide and examines risks across three time horizons: 2026, 2028 and 2036. Overall, it argues that leaders must balance immediate crises with longer-term resilience by strengthening cooperation, improving preparedness and addressing interconnected risks that affect economies, security, society and the environment

major global phishing-as-a-service platform called Tycoon 2FA was dismantled through a coordinated international operation led by Europol in partnership with law enforcement agencies and private-sector companies. The platform had enabled cybercriminals to bypass multi-factor authentication, send millions of phishing emails, and compromise accounts across nearly 100,000 organisations worldwide, including public institutions, schools and hospitals. The operation resulted in the takedown of 330 domains and highlighted the importance of Europol’s Cyber Intelligence Extension Programme, which helped translate shared intelligence and technical expertise from industry partners into coordinated cross-border action against cybercrime infrastructure.

Meta worked with the UK National Crime Agency and the Nigerian Police Force to disrupt a suspected online scam centre in Nigeria that used fake social media accounts, fraudulent Facebook groups and fabricated investment testimonials to target UK-based victims with cryptocurrency scams. According to preliminary findings, the operation led to the arrest of seven suspects and the seizure of devices and SIM cards believed to have been used in the fraud network, while Meta also moved to identify and remove violating accounts. More broadly, the case highlights how coordinated public-private action, intelligence sharing and platform safety measures are becoming increasingly important in tackling organised online fraud at an international scale

drivers’ hours regulations are a critical safeguard in commercial road transport, designed to protect road safety, driver welfare, fair competition and public confidence by reducing fatigue-related risks and ensuring lawful working practices. From the Traffic Commissioners’ perspective, compliance requires operators and transport managers to go beyond basic rule awareness by implementing strong systems for route planning, tachograph use, data monitoring, recordkeeping, training and corrective action when breaches occur. The guidance stresses that these rules should be treated as a shared safety responsibility rather than a box-ticking exercise, with proactive compliance, effective oversight and a culture that prioritises wellbeing and legality seen as essential to preventing infringements and avoiding serious regulatory consequences.

Namibia, with support from UNICRI and international partners, is piloting a virtual reality rehabilitation tool in prisons as part of a broader effort to use digital innovation responsibly in correctional reform. Through a three-day workshop in Windhoek, correctional officials, experts and practitioners explored how technologies such as VR can support offender rehabilitation and reintegration while maintaining ethical safeguards, institutional oversight and human-centred design. The initiative builds on earlier UNICRI research and includes practical testing with correctional staff and inmates, helping assess usability, readiness for implementation and future opportunities to scale digital rehabilitation in ways that strengthen accountability, inclusion and rehabilitation outcomes.

Cass County Sheriff’s Office in Indiana is promoting a mobile app to improve public communication, transparency and emergency preparedness as tornado season approaches. The app gives residents access to detention and booking information, registered offender listings, community resources, and mental health and substance abuse support, while also allowing push notifications for National Weather Service alerts and, in the future, major law enforcement incidents. A daily bulletin feature is also being added to share call-log information, making the app a broader digital tool for public safety, community outreach and easier access to important local services and updates.

Europol launched the European Centre Against Migrant Smuggling (ECAMS) to scale up EU efforts against increasingly complex smuggling networks operating both online and offline. The centre will strengthen intelligence-led, data-driven investigations, expand OSINT and digital disruption via the DigiNeX network, and intensify financial investigations to “follow the money” and undermine smugglers’ business models. Europol reports major results in recent years (operations supported, intelligence contributions processed, analytical reports delivered), and says ECAMS will further improve cross-border coordination and partnerships to target high-value smuggling networks along entire route

The Philippine Bureau of Internal Revenue (BIR) suspended audits on 24 Nov 2025 (RMC No. 107-2025) to fix audit controls and address fake/unauthorized Letters of Authority (LOAs) and inconsistent practices. After reforms, the suspension was lifted (RMC No. 8-2026). BIR then issued RMC No. 5-2026, launching an Online LOA Verifier inside Chatbot REVIE. Taxpayers enter TIN, taxpayer name, and LOA case number to confirm authenticity. The system replies “LOA FOUND” (valid) or “LOA NOT FOUND”, in which case taxpayers email contact_us-LOA@bir.gov.ph
 for manual verification. The tool strengthens transparency and helps prevent fraudulent audits, since an audit without a valid LOA is legally void

Pakistan is gradually using machine learning and AI within its tax administration to strengthen compliance risk management, especially in a resource-constrained environment. Rather than increasing the number of audits, the system helps improve audit quality by identifying high-risk taxpayers through patterns found across income tax, sales tax, and customs data. These tools do not replace human judgment; instead, they support field officers with dashboards, risk rankings, and targeted nudges that help prioritize enforcement, improve filing accuracy, and encourage voluntary compliance. Early results show promising outcomes, including higher tax payments among nudged taxpayers, while the broader lesson is that AI works best when combined with human oversight, strong institutional processes, and long-term investment in state capacity.

DAC8 is the European Union’s eighth amendment to the Directive on Administrative Cooperation in Direct Taxation, designed to strengthen tax transparency by extending automatic exchange of information rules to crypto-assets. Effective from 1 January 2026, it requires Reporting Crypto-Asset Service Providers operating in the EU to collect due-diligence and transaction data on EU-resident users, report it to national tax authorities, and support annual information exchanges between member states to help combat tax fraud, tax evasion, and tax avoidance. The framework aligns with the OECD’s Crypto-Asset Reporting Framework, covers a wide range of crypto-assets including stablecoins and some NFTs, and sets the first reporting cycle for 2026 with exchanges due by 30 September 2027.

Northlake, one of the fastest-growing towns in Texas, adopted Envisio dashboard technology to improve how it plans and tracks capital projects amid rapid population growth and limited staff capacity. The dashboard serves as a single digital source for monitoring about 18 projects, such as road reconstruction, meter upgrades, and a hotel conference center, reducing reliance on spreadsheets and manual reporting while improving accuracy, transparency, and responsiveness to both town council and public inquiries. As Northlake prepares for further expansion and possible annexation, the dashboard is expected to play a growing role in guiding development, reflecting a broader trend in government toward using dashboards to connect public investments, budgeting, and strategic priorities more clearly.

Massachusetts has launched GrantWell, a free AI-powered tool designed to help municipal governments identify, understand, and apply for federal and state grant opportunities more efficiently. Developed by the state’s Federal Funds and Infrastructure Office in partnership with Northeastern University’s Burnes Center, the platform can search for relevant grants, summarize complex funding notices, answer questions about eligibility and requirements, and generate a first draft of project narratives. The initiative responds to challenges voiced by local governments during a statewide listening tour, particularly limited capacity to find suitable grants, interpret complicated application rules, and prepare competitive proposals, making the tool a practical way to expand local access to public funding without replacing human review.

Singapore’s Manufacturing Federation (SMF) launched a Johor–Singapore Special Economic Zone (JS-SEZ) playbook to help manufacturers plan and operate across both markets with clearer information on regulations, talent mobility, infrastructure, and support channels. It was launched at the Manufacturing Day Summit 2026, where multiple collaboration agreements were also signed. SMF says it has engaged 100+ businesses since July 2025, supported site visits to Johor, and helped firms like SM Metal Solutions progress toward setting up a factory targeted for completion by end-2026.

Decatur and the Morgan County Landfill in Alabama are investing in a new baler and an AI-powered sorting system to restore and improve recycling operations after a mechanical failure halted collection services. The AI system is expected to reduce dependence on inmate labor, address ongoing staffing disruptions, improve sorting efficiency, and significantly expand processing capacity while increasing revenue from recyclable materials. Officials see the technology as a practical long-term solution that strengthens service continuity, lowers operational risk, and modernizes the recycling center’s performance and resilience.

U.S. federal AI bill led by Senator Marsha Blackburn that would create a broad national framework for regulating artificial intelligence, centered on a new “duty of care” requiring AI chatbot developers to take reasonable steps to prevent foreseeable harm to users. The draft legislation also combines several other AI-related proposals, including protections for children online, limits on liability protections for platforms, safeguards for artists’ voices and likenesses, greater transparency around AI’s impact on jobs, rules for high-risk AI audits, and measures to detect AI-generated content. Overall, the bill aims to replace the patchwork of state rules with one federal standard while addressing safety, accountability, online harms, copyright, and national competitiveness.

BBNJ Agreement, adopted on 19 June 2023 and entered into force on 17 January 2026, is the third implementing agreement under the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea and is designed to protect and ensure the sustainable use of marine biodiversity in areas beyond national jurisdiction. The Agreement focuses on four main areas: marine genetic resources and benefit-sharing, area-based management tools such as marine protected areas, environmental impact assessments, and capacity-building with marine technology transfer. It also establishes broader implementation mechanisms, including funding arrangements, institutional bodies such as a Conference of the Parties, subsidiary structures, a clearing-house mechanism, and a secretariat, making it a major global framework for strengthening international cooperation in ocean conservation.

United Nations Convention against Cybercrime officially opened for signature in Hanoi on 25–26 October 2025 during a high-level conference hosted by Viet Nam and UNODC, with 71 countries and the European Union signing at the opening ceremony. As the first comprehensive global treaty focused on cybercrime, the Convention aims to strengthen international cooperation in preventing and combating cybercrime and in sharing electronic evidence related to serious crimes. UNODC, which supported the negotiation process, will serve as the secretariat for the Conference of the States Parties and help advance implementation and entry into force. The Convention will remain open for signature at UN Headquarters in New York until 31 December 2026 and will enter into force 90 days after the 40th ratification or equivalent approval is deposited.

South Korea’s Presidential Security Service has secured two U.S. patents for its locally developed AI-based X-ray screening technology, which is designed to detect hazardous materials such as sulfuric acid more accurately and efficiently. The patented system combines X-ray equipment with AI algorithms to improve threat detection and reduce reliance on the individual experience and skill of field personnel. After a three-year review process, the patents are expected to support faster research, development, and field deployment, with the broader goal of strengthening national security and public safety through advanced screening technology.

U.S. Treasury Department, through FSOC and the Artificial Intelligence Transformation Office, has launched the AI Innovation Series as a public-private initiative to strengthen the resilience, stability and competitiveness of the U.S. financial system as AI adoption accelerates. Through a series of roundtables bringing together regulators, financial institutions, technology firms and experts, the initiative aims to explore high-value uses of AI in areas such as fraud detection, cybersecurity, credit underwriting and operational risk management, while ensuring governance and supervisory frameworks evolve alongside deployment. Overall, the initiative reflects a strategic shift toward viewing responsible AI adoption not only as a technological opportunity but as a core element of financial stability, economic security and long-term growth.

Malaysia is emerging as a strong player in fintech innovation by focusing on secure, resilient and inclusive digital payment systems that can meet the evolving needs of the Asia Pacific region. Its efforts center on improving digital payment infrastructure through real-time processing, digital wallets and interoperable platforms, while also investing in critical areas such as quantum-safe cryptography, stablecoins, fraud prevention, cross-border remittances and regulatory technology. Supported by collaboration among universities, industry and regulators, as well as investment in talent and research, these developments aim to strengthen financial security, improve efficiency, expand access to services and position Malaysia as an important contributor to the future of advanced financial technologies.

China is expanding the use of artificial intelligence in public tendering and bidding to help detect corruption, bid-rigging, and irregularities in government procurement processes. Under new guidelines, AI tools will be used to analyze bidding documents, monitor review committee decisions, and identify suspicious patterns that may indicate misconduct, while still serving as a support tool for enforcement authorities. This effort is part of China’s broader anti-corruption campaign and reflects a growing reliance on big data and AI to uncover cases that would be difficult to detect manually due to the large volume of public projects.

the U.S. Treasury Department, through FinCEN, has launched a new confidential whistleblower webpage to collect tips on fraud, money laundering and sanctions violations, while also offering financial rewards for eligible information that leads to successful enforcement. This initiative is part of a broader Treasury effort to combat large-scale fraud, especially government benefits fraud, through measures such as investigating money services businesses, improving reporting to speed prosecutions and asset recovery, alerting financial institutions to suspicious schemes and strengthening law enforcement use of financial data. Overall, the announcement reflects a more aggressive, coordinated strategy to protect public funds, strengthen financial integrity and encourage individuals to report actionable information supported by detailed evidence.

U.S. Treasury has completed a major public-private initiative to strengthen cybersecurity and risk management for artificial intelligence in the financial services sector, as part of the President’s AI Action Plan. Through collaboration among financial institutions, regulators and industry stakeholders, the initiative produced a series of practical resources aimed at helping institutions—especially small and mid-sized ones—manage AI-specific cybersecurity risks, improve governance, strengthen data practices, enhance transparency and support secure innovation. Overall, the effort reflects a coordinated approach to making AI adoption in finance more resilient, secure and scalable, while also reinforcing the broader competitiveness and stability of the U.S. financial system.

Estonia is taking steps to integrate its currently fragmented transport system through a new nationwide Mobility as a Service (MaaS) platform designed to make journey planning and ticketing seamless across different transport modes. Led by the Government Office and the Transport Administration, the MaaS X-Tee initiative will create a standardised data exchange layer linking services such as rail, buses, trams, ferries, aviation, micromobility and car rentals, with Turnit developing the prototype expected by November 2026. Overall, the project aims to break down isolated booking and ticketing systems, improve connectivity between mobility services and provide users with a more unified, efficient and convenient travel experience.

Google has officially launched a new cyber threat disruption unit aimed at proactively hindering hacker groups by cutting off the infrastructure and digital pathways they rely on, while stopping short of conducting “hack back” operations. The unit will use legal authorities, intelligence, public exposure of threat actors, infrastructure takedowns and product improvements to disrupt cybercriminals and state-linked adversaries in a defensive but more active way. Overall, the move reflects a broader shift toward stronger public-private collaboration and a more proactive cybersecurity posture, while maintaining legal and ethical limits on how private companies respond to cyber threats.

cities are beginning to use a combination of edge AI and agentic AI to detect and respond to local problems such as potholes, graffiti, illegal dumping and code violations more quickly and accurately. By processing and anonymizing footage directly on cameras mounted to public vehicles, edge AI reduces storage and privacy risks while identifying issues in real time, and downstream systems can then help route those issues into action workflows for staff review and response. Examples from San Jose, Stockton and Boston show that these tools can greatly expand a city’s visibility and efficiency without replacing human judgment, but the article stresses that strong privacy safeguards, oversight, transparency and public trust remain essential as governments adopt these technologies.

the Los Angeles County Metropolitan Transportation Authority has launched a new online Monthly Safety Tracker to make bus and train safety data more transparent and easier for the public to understand. The dashboard presents key safety statistics in a more accessible format than lengthy reports, helping riders see trends in incidents and assess the safety of the Metro system for themselves. This initiative reflects a broader move by transit agencies to use digital tools to improve transparency, support crime reduction efforts and build public confidence, especially as Los Angeles prepares to welcome large numbers of visitors for major upcoming events such as the FIFA World Cup and the 2028 Olympics.

the U.S. Treasury and IRS have issued interim guidance on the Corporate Alternative Minimum Tax (CAMT) to reduce compliance burdens, provide greater clarity and make the tax rules more workable for businesses. Treasury argues that the existing CAMT framework has been overly complex, costly and disruptive, even for companies that do not owe the tax, and that the new guidance is intended to ease administrative pressure, support domestic investment, innovation and job creation, and allow the government to redesign the broader regulatory framework in a more practical and predictable way based on stakeholder feedback.

HMRC is strengthening standards for third-party tax software as part of its strategy to reduce taxpayer errors, improve compliance, and support its shift toward a digital-first tax system. Since reliance on software providers is growing, HMRC plans to apply stronger expectations to all products using its API-based services, with consultation, testing, and evaluation continuing through 2026 and 2027 before a transition period is confirmed. The proposed reforms focus on five main areas: product integrity, supporting correct outcomes, data accountability, error management, and misuse and fraud prevention. More broadly, this forms part of a wider government plan to create a more effective, innovative, and competitive tax software market through better collaboration, oversight, customer empowerment, improved technical integration, and clearer rules around areas such as AI use, provider registration, and switching taxpayer data between systems.

Britain’s Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) defended awarding U.S. firm Palantir a 12-week contract to analyse the regulator’s internal data to help combat financial crime, after lawmakers raised concerns about access to sensitive data and the risk of Palantir becoming too dominant across government. FCA officials said Palantir will act only as a data processor and will not have access to regulatory intelligence, adding that the U.S. CLOUD Act would not apply to this arrangement. FCA CEO Nikhil Rathi told lawmakers the regulator needs “best-in-class” data and analytics tools to be an effective enforcer, while Palantir said it cannot commercialise any data it processes and can only use it under the FCA’s instructions.

that means for the Chemical Weapons Convention. The report highlights both opportunities and risks: AI can accelerate legitimate chemical research (e.g., modeling, synthesis planning, toxicity prediction), but it may also lower the barrier for designing harmful chemicals. For OPCW operations, AI could improve verification by analysing large declaration datasets, detecting patterns and inconsistencies, and supporting open-source analysis (such as satellite imagery) and faster interpretation of analytical chemistry data. The report recommends continuous monitoring of AI advances, stronger engagement with scientists and industry, careful adoption of AI tools with safeguards and human oversight, and capacity-building and knowledge sharing among Member States.

Indian Customs has been developing an in-house, vendor-agnostic AI X-ray image analytics solution since 2022 to strengthen non-intrusive inspection (NII) of cargo. The approach combines models such as product classification, heterogeneity detection, object detection (e.g., YOLOv7), and container weight prediction, supported by strong data collection/labeling, synthetic data generation, and a human-in-the-loop feedback cycle. India uses risk-based selection (not scanning everything), and reports improved detection accuracy and operational efficiency, citing examples like concealed firecrackers, cosmetics, and cigarettes found in misdeclared shipments.

The text explains that HM Treasury has appointed HSBC as the platform provider for the Digital Gilt Instrument (DIGIT) pilot following a competitive procurement process, marking an important step in the UK’s Wholesale Financial Markets Digital Strategy. The pilot aims to explore how distributed ledger technology (DLT) can be used in sovereign debt issuance, while also encouraging the growth of UK-based digital market infrastructure and wider adoption of DLT in financial markets. HSBC will provide its digital assets platform, HSBC Orion, and Ashurst LLP has been appointed as legal adviser for the project. DIGIT is designed to be a digitally native, short-dated instrument issued within the Digital Securities Sandbox, with on-chain settlement and operation separate from the government’s main debt programme, supporting the UK’s ambition to remain a leading global financial centre.

the U.S. Treasury has released two practical resources to support safe and responsible AI adoption in the financial sector: a shared AI Lexicon and a Financial Services AI Risk Management Framework. These tools are intended to address common challenges such as inconsistent terminology and uneven risk management practices by creating a common language for AI concepts and providing tailored guidance for evaluating and managing AI risks across the full lifecycle of financial services use cases. Overall, the initiative aims to strengthen governance, cybersecurity, operational resilience, accountability and consumer protection, while also helping financial institutions adopt AI more confidently, consistently and at scale.

GSA announced it generated $3.9 million by selling the oil and gas mineral rights to about 133 net mineral acres in Big Spring, Texas (formerly held by the Bureau of Land Management) through a public auction. The agency said the sale supports efforts to rightsize the federal footprint, reduce waste, and deliver taxpayer value, aligning with its Title 40 disposal responsibilities and Executive Order 14241 by returning mineral assets to private-sector use and strengthening domestic mineral production. GSA also noted it has identified additional surplus assets for disposal that could help cut federal real estate operating costs by more than $430 million annually.

GSA announced a new OneGov agreement with Broadcom that gives federal agencies up to 64% discounts on Broadcom’s VMware enterprise software to support IT modernization, cybersecurity and AI-ready workloads. The offer includes VMware Tanzu Platform, Tanzu Data Intelligence, Avi Load Balancer, and VMware vDefend (Distributed Firewall + Advanced Threat Prevention), with an optional Tanzu AI Starter Kit that adds professional services to accelerate AI prototyping and deployment. Available through GSA’s Multiple Award Schedule until May 2027, the deal is positioned to reduce cost and complexity, standardize IT procurement, and support Executive Order 14240 and the OneGov unified buying strategy.

Norway’s $2.1 trillion sovereign wealth fund (NBIM) says it may eventually allow limited AI-driven investment decisions under human supervision, but not yet, because the tools still make mistakes. For now, staff use AI mainly to gather and analyse information—such as monitoring thousands of portfolio companies for ESG/financial risks, preparing for meetings, and simulating negotiations—while humans remain responsible for final decisions. About half of the fund’s 700 employees build their own AI tools using Anthropic’s Claude, and the CEO expects roles to shift from back-office administration toward investment work, with headcount broadly stable.

The text explains that ICAO has launched a major update to its Public Key Directory (PKD) system, the global platform used to verify that e-passports and other digital travel documents are authentic and untampered with. The upgraded system, replacing a version unchanged since 2015, expands verification beyond standard passports to include digital visas, health certificates, and newer forms of electronic identity, while also enabling more advanced features such as remote document authentication through smartphones and earlier access to biometric data. ICAO says these improvements will help airlines, airports, and border authorities speed up passenger processing and support digital travel innovation, while the system itself continues to store only security certificates and no personal traveller data.

the European Commission has launched an AI-powered platform called TraceMap to improve food safety oversight and combat fraud across the EU by helping authorities analyse large volumes of data more quickly and accurately. The system brings together information from existing EU food safety databases to detect contamination risks, trace suspicious supply chains, identify high-risk operators, and support faster recalls of unsafe products. A pilot test already showed its value by helping authorities detect and recall contaminated infant milk formula, and overall the platform is intended to strengthen cooperation between Member States, improve targeting of inspections, and make food safety enforcement more proactive and effective.

Washington Metropolitan Area Transit Authority is using data and analytics to make targeted improvements to bus and rail service, focusing on practical measures such as travel times, job access, and service frequency to better meet changing rider needs after the pandemic. By analyzing how many jobs and important destinations can be reached within reasonable travel times, WMATA has been able to redesign services more strategically, improve frequency on high-demand routes, extend access through projects like the Silver Line, and add technologies such as bus signal priority to speed up trips. Overall, the agency is using data not only to improve rider experience and grow ridership, but also to build a stronger case with policymakers for continued investment and expansion.

Inrix has launched Compass, a generative AI safety analytics tool for U.S. transportation agencies that helps identify systemic roadway risks before serious crashes happen. By using large language models together with a data lake containing information such as speeding trends, hard braking, exposure data, vulnerable road user risk factors, and official safety guidance, the system helps agencies move from reactive crash analysis to proactive prevention. It enables faster, data-driven decisions on where safety problems are emerging and what proven countermeasures should be applied, with early users such as Miami-Dade County and Las Vegas reporting that it improves analysis efficiency and supports broader road safety and Vision Zero goals.:

The article explains that China’s cyberspace regulator has issued draft rules to govern digital humans, requiring clear labels on all virtual human content and banning services that could mislead children or encourage addictive or inappropriate interactions, including virtual intimate relationships for users under 18. The proposed rules also prohibit creating digital humans using someone’s personal information without consent, using them to bypass identity checks, or spreading content that threatens national security or social unity. More broadly, the regulations reflect China’s effort to both accelerate AI adoption across its economy and tighten oversight so that the fast-growing digital human sector develops in a controlled, safe, and state-aligned manner.

the North Star Cybersecurity Certification Program, originally developed by the Delaware Small Business Development Center, has expanded nationwide through the U.S. SBDC network of 1,200 centers to help small businesses strengthen their cybersecurity awareness and resilience. The no-cost program trains business advisers to guide especially smaller “mom-and-pop” firms on practical cyber risks such as ransomware, phishing, and credential theft, using the NIST Cybersecurity Framework as a common and actionable foundation. Supported by state and federal backing, as well as a 2024 cyber prize from the U.S. Small Business Administration, the program has already trained hundreds of advisers and is now being embedded across the country so that local SBDC teams can better support small businesses facing growing cyber threats and related requirements such as cyber insurance.

NJ Transit has launched a two-year microtransit pilot called MicroLink in Bergen and Monmouth counties to help commuters travel from their neighborhoods to park-and-ride locations and major bus stops more easily. Funded by the Federal Transit Administration and operated with Via technology, the free on-demand weekday service can be booked through an app or phone call, much like ride-hailing services, and is designed to improve first-mile and last-mile connections to the broader bus network. The pilot includes specific service zones in both counties, uses electric and gas-powered vans with wheelchair-accessible seating, and reflects a broader effort to make public transportation more flexible, accessible, and seamless for daily riders.

Full Sail University in Florida has launched a new 1,500-square-foot cyber defense range to give cybersecurity and IT students hands-on training in a realistic, enterprise-style environment. As part of IBM’s Cyber Campus initiative, the facility includes 28 workstations and supports practical exercises such as malware analysis, threat hunting, digital forensics, and incident response using industry-grade tools and cloud infrastructure from Amazon Web Services and Cloud Range. Aligned with recognized U.S. cybersecurity frameworks, the new range is designed to strengthen workforce readiness by connecting academic learning with real-world security operations, while also serving as a venue for competitions, workshops, and training for businesses and government agencies.

Dublin City Council participated in a quantum-secure communications trial with Trinity College Dublin and other IrelandQCI partners to explore how local authorities can use advanced quantum technology to strengthen cybersecurity for critical infrastructure, citizen data, and digital public services. Conducted under the Smart Docklands programme, the trial demonstrated the potential of publicly owned networks to provide highly secure, future-ready connectivity for government operations. More broadly, the initiative forms part of Ireland’s contribution to the wider EuroQCI effort, which aims to build a secure quantum communications infrastructure across Europe to support smarter, more resilient, and better protected public services.

The article reports that five EU countries—Germany, Italy, Spain, Portugal, and Austria—have jointly called for an EU-wide windfall tax on energy companies in response to sharp fuel price increases linked to the war involving Iran. In a letter to the European Commission, the finance ministers argued that such a tax could help fund temporary relief for consumers, ease inflation, and avoid putting extra pressure on public budgets, while also ensuring that companies benefiting from the crisis contribute to reducing the burden on the public. The European Commission confirmed it is assessing the proposal as part of broader discussions on targeted crisis measures, while industry representatives in Germany rejected the idea, arguing that energy companies are not making unjustified profits and are focused on maintaining fuel supplies under difficult conditions.

IRS’s push to phase out paper refund checks and move taxpayers toward direct deposit or other electronic payments has delayed tax refunds for nearly 1.5 million Americans, with some facing waits of more than two months. Taxpayers who filed without bank information are being asked to provide direct deposit details within 30 days, often through an online IRS account that requires identity verification using facial recognition, and if they do not respond, a paper check is issued only after an additional six weeks. While the policy is intended to reduce fraud and improve efficiency, it has raised concerns about the burden on low-income, unbanked, elderly, rural, tribal, and disabled taxpayers who may have limited internet access or difficulty using digital systems, especially as other government agencies are also moving away from paper checks.

China’s tax and financial regulators are encouraging banks and local authorities to use blockchain and privacy-computing technologies to improve lending services for small businesses by strengthening the “bank-tax interaction” model. The goal is to standardize data sharing, reduce information gaps between tax authorities, banks, and enterprises, improve credit assessment models, and expand financing for compliant, tax-paying businesses. This policy is part of China’s broader strategy to build blockchain-based data infrastructure at a national scale, while continuing its distinction between supporting blockchain for real-economy and financial system applications and maintaining strict restrictions on cryptocurrency trading and mining.

The National Anti-Corruption Authority (ANAC) is developing territorial level public procurement and context risk indicators to measure corruption risks and to promote transparency and integrity in public procurement. ANAC is integrating multiple data sources, designing methodologies for calculation and validation of indicators. The work is focusing on an open approach to risk analysis: open data, open software, and open knowledge.

U.S. General Services Administration (GSA) has released government-wide office space utilization data showing that thousands of federal buildings failed to meet the statutory minimum average occupancy rate of 60%, supporting the administration’s effort to reduce excess federal real estate. Based on data collected from agencies through methods such as badge scans, sensors, and anonymized mobile location information, the findings are expected to guide decisions on shrinking the federal property portfolio, selling underused buildings, reducing maintenance burdens, and co-locating agencies with similar missions. Although GSA noted that some of the information may be incomplete or inaccurate, the release represents a major step toward identifying inefficiencies and restructuring the federal real estate footprint around a smaller and more efficient core.

Vietnam is reforming its intellectual property system to make it a stronger engine for innovation, commercialization, and economic growth, especially in strategic technologies. Recent legal and policy changes show a shift away from treating IP mainly as a form of legal protection and toward using it as a practical tool to turn research into market-ready products and services. These reforms give more ownership and usage rights to researchers and institutions, encourage greater business participation, and expand the role of Vietnam’s IP office to support commercialization. While rising patent filings and grants in 2025 suggest strong progress, experts emphasize that further improvements are still needed in areas such as co-ownership, benefit sharing, enterprise participation, valuation of in-kind contributions, and state-backed risk-sharing mechanisms to ensure that research outputs generate real socio-economic impact and strengthen Vietnam’s technological competitiveness.

Malaysia achieved a record RM426.7 billion in approved investments in 2025, driven mainly by technology, digital infrastructure, and advanced manufacturing, underscoring the country’s transition toward a more innovation-led economy. Strong domestic and foreign investment flowed especially into the services sector, with information and communication projects such as artificial intelligence, big data, cloud computing, and data centres leading the way, while manufacturing also expanded through electronics, semiconductors, machinery, and other high-value industries. Overall, the article highlights how government support, sustainability measures, and skills development are helping Malaysia strengthen its digital ecosystem, create high-skilled jobs, and reinforce its position as a competitive regional hub for advanced technology and long-term growth.

India is expanding access to justice through technology by strengthening the Tele-Law initiative under the DISHA scheme, which connects citizens—especially those in remote and underserved areas—with legal professionals through Common Service Centres and digital tools such as video consultations. The National Consultation 2026 will bring together a wide range of stakeholders to review progress, share beneficiary experiences, and discuss how to improve outreach, service quality, institutional coordination, and the use of emerging technologies in legal aid delivery. More broadly, the initiative reflects India’s wider digital transformation of the justice system through platforms for digital evidence, court processes, cybercrime reporting, and medico-legal reporting, with the overall goal of building a more inclusive, efficient, and technology-enabled legal ecosystem.

U.S. government agencies in jurisdictions with populations of 50,000 or more must make their websites accessible by April 30 under a 2024 Title II ADA rule requiring compliance with WCAG 2.1 standards, while smaller jurisdictions have an extra year to comply.

OPCW is promoting gender equity in chemistry through its annual Basic Analytical Chemistry Course for Women Chemists, which provides female scientists from developing and transition economies with practical laboratory skills to detect and analyse chemicals relevant to the Chemical Weapons Convention. As part of the wider Women in Chemistry Initiative launched in 2016, the programme combines hands-on training, advanced analytical techniques, quality standards, mentorship, and professional networking to strengthen both technical capacity and the role of women in peaceful chemistry-related work. More broadly, the initiative supports international cooperation, improves the quality and reliability of chemical analysis in member states, and helps build a more inclusive and representative global scientific community.

Cincinnati has modernized 14 city-owned parking lots and garages by removing traditional gates and ticket machines and replacing them with a touchless parking system based on license plate recognition and digital payment technology. Under the new setup, parking sessions begin automatically when vehicles enter, and drivers can pay using QR codes, kiosks, or other methods without stopping at exit gates, which reduces queues, improves customer convenience, lowers maintenance costs, and supports more efficient revenue collection. Officials say the response has been positive, with increased adoption and revenue, reflecting a broader shift among cities toward cloud-based, contactless parking systems that improve urban mobility and digital curb management.

California Governor Gavin Newsom has issued an executive order to strengthen how the state procures generative AI technologies by requiring several agencies to recommend reforms that improve oversight, risk mitigation, and accountability. The order directs state departments to develop procurement changes that would require AI suppliers to disclose their safeguards on issues such as illegal content, harmful bias, civil rights, privacy, and supply chain risk, while also exploring ways to expand safe access to vetted AI tools for public employees. In addition, the order calls for broader state action including updating the digital strategy, creating AI-enabled public service tools, expanding training, publishing data minimization guidance, and issuing standards for watermarking AI-generated media, reflecting California’s effort to balance innovation with stronger public protections.

TSA’s PreCheck Touchless ID program is expanding across 65 U.S. airports to speed up airport security by using facial recognition to verify travelers’ identities without requiring them to hand over documents. The service is available to eligible TSA PreCheck passengers who also have a participating airline loyalty account and valid passport data linked to that account, and it is designed to help travelers move more quickly through security at a time when staffing shortages and a partial government shutdown have caused longer and less predictable wait times. Travelers and TSA describe the system as a faster, more efficient option that can reduce processing times significantly, while still requiring passengers to carry a REAL ID-compliant physical ID, and it stands alongside other trusted traveler programs such as Global Entry and Clear as part of a broader shift toward biometric, touchless airport screening.

Fraport AG and the German Federal Police have begun regular operation of the AI-powered APIDS system at Frankfurt Airport, making it the first large-scale deployment of its kind in Europe. APIDS, which stands for Automatic Prohibited Item Detection Systems, uses artificial intelligence to help security staff analyse X-ray images from CT scanners and automatically identify prohibited items in carry-on luggage, while leaving final decisions to human personnel. The system is now active across all airport terminals on more than 50 CT scanners, following extensive testing and national certification, and is intended to improve both the accuracy and efficiency of security screening. Overall, the rollout reflects a major step in modernising aviation security through close cooperation between airport authorities, police, and government, supported by significant investment in advanced checkpoint infrastructure.

UK company NW Pro developed Deeper Scan, an AI-powered airport security screening system, with support from the Defence and Security Accelerator (DASA) and technical help from Dstl. The system uses AI to scan electronic devices such as laptops, tablets, and phones, compare them against a trusted database, and detect modifications or anomalies that could indicate hidden threats, while still allowing human experts to review uncertain cases. The article highlights that DASA’s funding, access to realistic testing, and connections with key stakeholders helped move the technology from concept to commercial trials, while also boosting NW Pro’s credibility and growth. Overall, the story shows how targeted government support can accelerate practical, transparent, and scalable AI security innovations for aviation and other high-risk environments.

Columbus, Ohio is rolling out an “Agentic City” programme that uses connected AI agents across attractions, venues, and tourism locations to create a unified digital experience for visitors, residents, and business travelers. Led by Experience Columbus and Satisfi Labs, the initiative places AI-powered assistants at key points of interest so people can instantly access information about events, destinations, and activities while navigating the city. By linking these individual AI agents into a broader citywide network, the programme aims to reduce fragmentation in the visitor experience and build a more responsive, coordinated, and intelligent tourism ecosystem.

Brazil and the United States have launched a joint initiative to combat organized crime by integrating data from Brazil’s federal tax authority with U.S. Customs and Border Protection in order to strengthen intelligence efforts against illicit shipments of weapons and narcotics. The move comes as President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva increases his focus on public security ahead of the October election, while Brazil continues investigating money laundering schemes tied to criminal groups in the fuel sector. Although tensions remain between the two countries over how to classify and confront organized gangs, officials say the partnership has already been shaped by rising cooperation, with Brazil reporting the seizure of more than 1,100 weapons arriving from the United States and over 1.5 tons of drugs in the first quarter alone.

City of Brownsville, Texas, is expanding its partnership with SHI International to build a smart city public safety solution that uses artificial intelligence and machine learning to improve incident response, enhance resident safety, and create a foundation for broader citywide applications. By combining technologies from Centific, Nvidia, and Lenovo into a scalable integrated framework, the city aims to gain real-time visibility, make better decisions based on live data, and support future uses such as traffic management, fire detection, weather monitoring, and energy optimization. More broadly, the initiative is designed not only to improve safety and resilience, but also to strengthen local economic development by providing advanced AI and networking infrastructure that can support businesses, hospitals, and surrounding communities.

governments and technology providers are preparing extensively to secure the 2026 FIFA World Cup across the U.S., Canada, and Mexico, with a major emphasis on countering drone threats, strengthening communications, and improving multilingual coordination. With millions of spectators expected and billions watching globally, federal and local authorities are investing heavily in technologies such as drone detection systems, radar, cameras, radio-frequency analysis, translation tools, and dedicated communications networks for first responders. Overall, the article shows that drones are emerging as one of the most serious security concerns for major public events, while broader technologies such as real-time translation and interoperable emergency communications will also be crucial to keeping the tournament safe across many cities and venues

Ohio is piloting an iPad-based workforce training program in prisons through Connected Apprentice and Apple, beginning at Chillicothe Correctional Institution, to prepare incarcerated residents for careers in high-demand fields such as construction and health care. The secure iPads provide self-paced trade-specific courses, video instruction, workplace skills, and training on industry software, while also helping participants build basic digital familiarity that is increasingly necessary in modern jobs. Overall, the initiative aims not only to address labor shortages but also to improve post-release employment prospects and reduce recidivism, with success measured by whether participants secure jobs and avoid returning to prison.

Waymo and Waze have launched a pilot in several U.S. cities to detect potholes using Waymo’s vehicle perception and physical feedback systems, then share that information through the Waze for Cities platform and with Waze users in real time. The goal is to give cities and state transportation departments a more complete and timely view of road conditions than they usually get from resident complaints and manual inspections alone, helping them repair potholes more efficiently and fairly while also warning drivers as they approach hazards. Overall, the programme shows how data from connected and autonomous vehicle systems can be reused to support safer roads, smarter maintenance, and better urban mobility management.

Maryland Comptroller Brooke Lierman is prioritizing the successful rollout of a new tax processing system scheduled for August 2026, warning lawmakers that her office has very limited capacity to handle major personal income tax changes at the same time. She stressed that a smooth implementation is critical to maintaining reliable revenue collection for state operations, given that Maryland collects more than $36 billion annually in taxes and fees. The article also notes that the comptroller’s office is seeking more staff and funding for technology upgrades, cybersecurity, and compliance efforts, while reporting that recent modernization and enforcement investments are already expected to generate additional revenue in the coming years.

IRS has issued final guidance on the temporary “no tax on tips” provision, clarifying which workers and which types of tips may qualify for a federal income tax deduction between tax years 2025 and 2028. The deduction applies only to federal income tax, not payroll or state taxes, is capped at $25,000 in qualified tips, and phases out for higher earners. The IRS identified more than 70 eligible occupations across sectors such as food service, hospitality, personal care, transportation, and entertainment, while also clarifying that only voluntary cash or cash-equivalent tips received directly from customers or through tip pools qualify. Although the rule offers a tax break for many tipped workers, the article notes that some of the lowest-paid workers may see little benefit because they do not earn enough to owe federal income tax in the first place.

European Parliament has approved new EU-wide anti-corruption rules establishing a harmonised criminal law framework to prevent and combat corruption across member states. The directive introduces common definitions for offences such as bribery, misappropriation, obstruction of justice, trading in influence, illicit enrichment, concealment, and private-sector corruption, while also aligning sanctions and strengthening cooperation among national authorities and EU bodies like OLAF, Europol, Eurojust, and the European Public Prosecutor’s Office. It also requires member states to adopt national anti-corruption strategies, conduct risk assessments, improve transparency in areas such as political financing and conflicts of interest, publish comparable machine-readable data, and ensure the existence of sufficiently independent anti-corruption bodies, with the overall goal of closing enforcement gaps, improving cross-border coordination, and strengthening trust, accountability, and democracy across the EU.

the European Commission has published an Implementing Act that advances the legal framework for remote onboarding into the European Digital Identity (EUDI) Wallet by defining standards and specifications for verifying users remotely and securely linking their identity data to both the wallet and the device. The new rules make clear that remote onboarding can reach a high level of assurance by combining substantial-level electronic identification with additional onboarding procedures, while leaving room for different compliance paths depending on the assurance level required. The article notes that this does not automatically make the EUDI Wallet universally ready for anti-money laundering use, but it does shift attention toward how eIDAS 2.0, AML rules, identity proofing, and regulatory reliance will be coordinated in practice, including where biometrics may be used in a privacy-compliant way to raise assurance levels.

Japan’s cabinet has approved amendments to the Act on the Protection of Personal Information (APPI) that aim to make the country more supportive of AI development while also strengthening safeguards for sensitive data, especially biometric data and children’s information. The bill expands consent exemptions for certain statistical, AI-related, and socially beneficial data uses to encourage innovation, but it also introduces stricter enforcement powers and heavier fines for misuse or fraudulent data collection. At the same time, it adds stronger protections for minors under 16 by requiring explicit parental consent for collecting biometric data such as facial images, applying a “best interests” standard to children’s data, and imposing new transparency obligations on organizations using facial recognition data, including public disclosure requirements and limits on third-party opt-out practices.

Karnataka is preparing a proposed digital safety law aimed at tightening regulation of social media platforms through a state-level, AI-aware and citizen-focused framework. The draft bill emphasizes mandatory labelling and penalties for AI-generated content and deepfakes, faster platform action on harmful content within 24 to 48 hours, stronger user protections such as grievance redressal and safeguards against harassment and misinformation, and the creation of a new state regulatory authority to oversee compliance. It also stresses prevention through digital literacy, media awareness, and mental well-being, while proposing technology-based tools such as fake news detection, deepfake tracking, and real-time monitoring, positioning Karnataka as a potential pioneer in decentralized digital governance.

World Customs Organization has launched two new virtual reality training modules to strengthen customs officers’ practical skills: one on air cargo clearance with a focus on e-commerce shipments, and another on container control techniques, including container types, markings, dimensions, and inspection methods. Building on an earlier VR training program, these courses are delivered through VR kiosks installed at WCO regional training centers and capacity-building offices, and they were developed with funding from the Korea Customs Service. The initiative has received positive user feedback, and to expand access, PC versions of the courses have also been added to the WCO CLiKC! learning platform, helping more officers benefit from immersive, technology-enabled customs training.

Thailand turned a large stockpile of seized ozone-depleting substances into a successful environmental protection project through a public-private partnership involving Thai Customs, the Department of Industrial Works, Tradewater, and Waste Management Siam. More than 10,000 cylinders of banned refrigerants, which had been stored for years and posed serious climate and ozone risks, were safely collected, tested, consolidated, and destroyed using certified technology that achieved over 99.99% destruction efficiency. The project permanently prevented more than 1.1 million metric tons of CO₂-equivalent emissions and showed how enforcement, technical expertise, and innovative financing through carbon credits can work together to create an effective model for managing hazardous seized chemicals.

Nepal Customs has launched a new Automated Customs Risk Management System (CRMS) integrated with ASYCUDA World to improve how it detects high-risk consignments by using machine learning, real-time data analysis, and a wider range of risk indicators than the older static system. The CRMS draws data from customs declarations, valuation databases, and oversight agencies, then generates risk scores and recommendations for officers through dashboards and alerts, helping identify issues such as undervaluation, misclassification, misuse of tax exemptions, and suspicious trading patterns more effectively. Overall, the system has improved targeting, productivity, decision quality, and revenue collection in major customs offices, and Nepal now plans to expand it further by adding non-intrusive inspection images and deeper integration with other government systems.

Thailand is moving closer to allowing crypto exchange-traded funds by opening a public consultation on a proposed framework that would initially permit spot ETFs linked to Bitcoin and Ethereum. The proposal requires these products to operate as mutual funds using a passive strategy, hold most assets with SEC-regulated custodians, and be traded only on the stock exchange, while also imposing requirements on staffing, systems, supervision, disclosure, investor education, and risk checks. Overall, the framework shows Thailand’s effort to cautiously expand regulated crypto investment products while strengthening investor protection, custody standards, and oversight of digital asset fund management.

Visa has launched Intelligent Commerce Connect to make it easier for merchants and service providers to accept payments initiated by AI agents across different networks and protocols. Through a single integration on the Visa Acceptance Platform, the solution supports key functions such as payment initiation, tokenisation, authentication, spend controls, and orchestration, while also connecting to both Visa and non-Visa payment systems. It is designed to support the growing ecosystem of agent-led commerce by helping merchants manage technical complexity, improve discoverability on AI platforms, and handle compliance needs more efficiently as AI-driven transactions become more common.

ASEAN’s cross-border payment connectivity expanded significantly in 2025, with QR payments reaching 36.2 million transactions worth US$716.4 million and person-to-person instant transfers reaching 1.6 million transactions worth US$305.7 million, showing growing regional use by consumers, businesses, and migrant workers. As ASEAN builds on 29 existing payment linkages, officials stress that the next stage of progress will require clearer legal and regulatory expectations, stronger coordination, better fraud and risk management, and improved interoperability. Beyond payments, the meeting also highlighted wider regional priorities including financial health measurement, digital financial literacy, digital capital market development, AI supervision, and new regulatory tools to strengthen cybersecurity and combat online scams.

after growing security demands in global trade following the 9/11 attacks, U.S. and Canadian importers created the Supplier Compliance Audit Network (SCAN) to make supply chain security audits more efficient, less repetitive, and more impactful for suppliers and importers alike. SCAN established a shared model built on a single audit standard aligned with CTPAT and the WCO SAFE Framework, independent accredited auditors, annual revalidation, training, and a secure platform using blockchain to exchange and record audit documents. Overall, the initiative reduces audit duplication and compliance costs, promotes a stronger culture of supply chain security, and gives both importers and U.S. Customs and Border Protection greater confidence that audited suppliers represent lower-risk actors in international trade.

Madrid has awarded Acciona a contract to build the city’s largest public electric vehicle charging station within the M-30 ring road, transforming a disused gas station into a new renewable-powered “house of mobility.” Scheduled to open in 2027, the facility will offer 20 ultra-fast charging spaces, battery swapping for certain electric vehicles, user services, and event space, while operating entirely on certified renewable energy and incorporating solar generation, air-purifying materials, and sustainable construction elements. Overall, the project is designed not only to expand EV charging capacity, but also to support Madrid’s decarbonization goals, improve urban quality of life, and create a modern public space centered on electric mobility.

Vermont has become the 13th U.S. state to purchase MS-ISAC’s statewide membership program, extending cybersecurity support to a broad range of public-sector organizations including state agencies, municipalities, tribal governments, public schools, health organizations, and utilities. Under this model, eligible entities can sign up at no cost through the state and gain access to services such as threat intelligence, incident response, forensic support, collaboration, and security operations resources. The move reflects a growing recognition that smaller public institutions often lack the staffing and technical capacity to defend themselves effectively, and it also highlights a broader shift toward states taking more direct responsibility for funding and organizing cybersecurity support as federal backing declines.

Motorola Solutions has acquired HyperYou, an AI startup focused on helping 911 call centers manage nonemergency calls more efficiently, in response to ongoing staffing shortages and heavy call volumes. HyperYou’s agentic AI is designed to distinguish between urgent emergencies and routine incidents, route calls to the appropriate services, and reduce pressure on human operators, while also supporting features such as real-time language translation. Motorola plans to integrate this technology into its Command Center portfolio and expand it with additional AI agents that can understand 911 calls, radio traffic, and other data sources, reflecting a broader trend toward using AI to improve speed, capacity, and effectiveness in public safety communications.

California is upgrading its driver’s licenses and DMV services with new technologies aimed at improving security and customer experience. A new digital signature embedded in the barcode on licenses and ID cards will help card readers verify authenticity and reduce fraud, while QR code-based self-check-in at DMV offices is designed to shorten wait times and reduce congestion by placing visitors in a virtual queue. Overall, these changes reflect a broader effort to modernize identity credentials and in-person government services through secure, digital-first tools.

Trinidad and Tobago government has announced a new income tax exemption for pension payments received from approved pension fund plans and approved deferred annuity plans, with effect from income earned on or after 1 January 2026.

Malaysia, through MIDA, is reshaping its 2026 investment strategy to focus less on the sheer volume of approved investments and more on implementation quality, technological upgrading, and long-term economic impact.

The UK published reforms to the National Security and Investment Act regime—expanding/clarifying some sensitive sectors (e.g., water, semiconductors, critical minerals) while removing low-risk categories (e.g., “off-the-shelf AI”) to reduce red tape

U.S. Department of Commerce has launched the inaugural call for proposals under the American AI Exports Program, inviting U.S. companies to form industry-led consortia and submit full-stack AI export packages for international markets between April 1 and June 30, 2026.

UK’s new national knife crime strategy aims to halve knife crime over the next decade by combining greater police deployment with stronger use of surveillance and digital technologies, especially improved CCTV coverage and retrospective facial recognition.

Casper, Wyoming, has approved a 60-day trial of AI software called TRULEO to analyze police body-worn camera footage, with the goal of automating video review and categorization, assessing officer performance during calls, and potentially reducing report-writing time through AI-assisted documentation.
“MyFutureFund” auto-enrolment (state-led): A new automatic enrolment pension system for eligible workers not already in a pension, designed to widen retirement saving coverage.

UK government has launched an intensive recovery plan to address serious service failures in the Civil Service Pension Scheme, particularly for members affected by bereavement, ill health, or voluntary exit decisions.
